Now: `docker/sidecars.compose.yml` is the five sidecars; `docker/compose.yml`'s init is a stock alpine `state-init` that only hands the state bind to the app's uid (the previous init was the app image in a second role and, because it carried `build:`, every `up --build` built the whole app image twice — the double build an update took to notice); registry mode pulls `talaria` alone; the dev loop, worktrees and devboxes stop rendering or starting a search container; `SEARXNG_SECRET` is no longer generated. The SearXNG **client** stays as one operator-pointed provider shape with no default: `SEARXNG_URL` or Admin → Search names a SearXNG-compatible JSON endpoint you already run, otherwise `platform_supply` withholds `search` and every caller is told plainly that the workspace cannot search. The fleet renderer passes a configured endpoint through to each agent's Hermes as `SEARXNG_URL` (a loopback address on a host-run dev app is rewritten to `host.docker.internal`; in a containerized stack a loopback address reaches nothing from an agent and is withheld). Two deploy bugs found on the way: the first-boot postgres-password guard looked for `talaria_pg-data` even on a renamed compose project, so an initialized cluster under `<project>_pg-data` could be handed a fresh random password — it now derives the volume from `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` (shell, then `docker/.env`); and `docker volume inspect` ran with the terminal inherited, printing a "no such volume" error on every fresh host's successful first `up`.
  Verified: `bun run gate` green (check, cli typecheck and tests — 223 cases including the renamed-project volume guard — and the touched crates' `cargo test`/clippy). `docker compose config` on all four layerings (prod, dev, devbox, registry), `sh -n` on the entrypoint. The image boots the way CI proves it: `docker build -t talaria-rc:local .` then `node scripts/deploy-smoke.mjs --image talaria-rc:local` — a fresh stack whose `state-init` ran as root, chowned the bind, exited 0, and whose app came up healthy and answered the claim screen. Hermes's own search surface was read from the running `nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest` container's `agent/web_search_registry.py` and `plugins/web/`, not from memory.

- **The ticket drafter knows the board it is drafting for.** "Draft tickets"
  turned a plan into a flat list from the conversation alone: it could not
  know that half the work was already an open ticket, who on the board does
  what, or that four of its tickets were one deliverable. The reviewer found
  that out one card at a time, and the duplicates it filed were real tickets
  a person then had to close.

  The drafter is now shown the board — its open tickets (`id #no [status]
  title`), its labels, its members — rendered into the prompt the way the
  workflow map already is, and the proposal shape grew three fields:

  - **`parent`** — an *epic*. Three or more tickets that serve one deliverable
    make the deliverable its own ticket and point at it; one level only. The
    review shows the epic badge and "Part of …" on the children; creation
    files parents first and children with `parentId`, and a child whose
    parent the reviewer dropped files as a top-level ticket.
  - **`assignees`** — board members, by id, only when the discussion said who
    does it. They reach the ticket as `user:<id>`, the spelling a ticket
    uses for a person; a bare id would have read as an agent model.
  - **`duplicateOf`** — the open ticket this proposal would re-propose. The
    card says "Possible duplicate of #no …" with a link, and the proposal
    **starts unticked**: ticking it is the reviewer saying "no, this is
    different", which is the decision that was theirs all along.

  **Two readers keep the model honest.** The verify step reads the ids back
  out of the very block the model was shown: a `duplicateOf` naming no open
  ticket, an assignee naming no member, or a nested epic earns the repair
  turn rather than a card nobody can act on. And after the draft, the
  **`ticket-dupe` census site** (choice, certainty 0.85, on) judges each
  proposal the model left unflagged against the open tickets whose titles
  overlap it — "the same work, not the same area" — with the model's own
  silence as the shadow baseline; when it acts, the proposal is flagged and
  unticked the same way. The judgment is per proposal, so a ten-ticket
  draft on a busy board is up to ten calls; an empty board or no overlap
  costs nothing.

  Verified: 441 tests in `talaria-harness-defs` (+6: `parent` remapped like
  a dependency with `null` never read as index zero, a nested child lifted to
  its epic rather than refused, ids coerced as ids and not prose, the block's
  id parsers, every branch of the context check, a `duplicateOf` nothing on
  the board earning the repair turn); 12 fixtures
  across three bands (+2: the open ticket named instead of re-proposed; a
  four-part deliverable grouped under one epic); 416 in `talaria-fitness`
  unchanged; 14 in `talaria-runs-plan-draft` (+7: the overlap ranking, a
  model-flagged duplicate left alone, the unticked duplicate); 93 in
  `talaria-decide` including the census consistency tests; 3 in
  `talaria-channel-plan` (the block pinned character for character); 10 UI
  tests for the create order and the store's normalize; svelte-check clean.
  The review walk's Save body learned the three fields too — without that
  every autosave would have dropped the epic links and the duplicate flag.

  A live draft needs a model and the Z.ai account answers "insufficient
  balance" today, so the fitness fixtures are the proof of the prompt until
  it is recharged; the plumbing is proven by the tests above.

- **Added:** The Work harness grows the controls its server half was waiting for. Research has three dials beside the preset — Effort (rounds), Breadth (queries per round) and Sources (what the writer sees) — each a 1-to-3 meter that the preset seeds and a run started from inside a session now discusses and reports into that session; a session that already has a run going says so, and a duplicate question says that instead (the route names which conflict it was). A clock in the session header schedules the session's agent: the fleet's own cron form, the session's schedules underneath with their next run and a quiet Remove, and the scheduled turn stamped on its row. The rail is organised per viewer: pinned threads first, collapsible groups, drag to reorder or onto a group header to file, pin and file from the row's hover control and the right-click menu alike, on threads shared with you too. ⌘K opens a palette to jump to a session. On an agent's Summary tab the subagent cap sits beside the Developer Agent and pinned-session switches, applied explicitly because it rolls the agent; on its MCP tab the Hermes toolsets this agent does not get are checkboxes with an explicit Apply, the two Talaria always keeps off shown as such; the fleet roster now carries the governed toolset vocabulary so the UI never guesses it. Verified: ui vitest 108 files / 1689 tests, svelte-check 0 errors; `talaria-routes-fleet` 31 and `talaria-routes-workbench` unit tests, clippy clean; `bun run docs:api` and `bun run check`; an adversarial review round over the diff with its two blockers and four majors fixed (the palette mounted, a cleared cap no longer saved as 0, the cap applied explicitly, a pinned row refusing a group drop, pinning clearing the slot, the 409 sentence following the route's reason); live on the worktree stack the roster's toolsets field and a research run with dials from a session, recorded in the pull request.

- **Added:** What an agent did in a turn now reads as cards, not just a count of tool calls. A web search leaves its sources beside the reply (title, host, snippet — at most six, deduped by URL). An `edit_document` leaves a document card that says what moved: each edit's label with its line deltas and a one-line before/after. A delegated child is a card with its role and goal, a status dot that turns done or red, the summary it came back with, and the tools it used. A screenshot an agent took lands as an image you can open, whichever browser tool wrote the file — `browser_vision`'s own result, or a fresh PNG any other browser tool names, such as the browser-use harness behind `browser_exec`. A tool that failed is a red ✕ in the tool list instead of a quiet check, from the Hermes frame through the stored row to the screen; a pinned session's tool rows now also show live, not only after the turn is stored. The "Thinking" disclosure remembers, per viewer, whether you keep it open. Server side, the edit route answers slim with the changes first and lands its chip directly, so it no longer depends on the agent's clamped tool-event round trip; chips are computed from secret-scrubbed results; a document chip is a snapshot whose change list grows across edits in one turn; and a tool's terminal status is one rule in the api and the client. Verified: `talaria-chips`, `talaria-doc-edit`, `talaria-routes-knowledge`, `talaria-routes-fleet`, `talaria-gateway`, `talaria-chat-persist` unit tests and clippy clean; ui vitest and svelte-check 0 errors; `bun run check`; an adversarial review round over the diff with its blocker and majors fixed and re-verified; the Hermes plugin's screenshot forwarding exercised with a stub transport (fresh PNG forwarded once, stale or non-browser or failed call forwards nothing); live on the worktree stack with the real model, the result recorded in the pull request.

- **Fixed:** The durable run plane counted every re-entry of a running row as a driver crash, so three rolling deploys (or three momentary Redis blips) killed a research expedition as "gave up", and a cross-instance stop was only honoured at the end of the in-flight step because the row-side heartbeat guard matched the wrong type. A clean stop now releases the row back to `queued`, a new `runs.crashes` column counts only claims that found the previous driver dead, and `max_attempts` bounds that; one unreachable-Redis renewal beat is tolerated before the drive stops; a refused heartbeat (cancelled, taken, gone) stops the drive within one beat; and a cancel is relayed through a short-lived Redis flag the driving instance polls every five seconds, so a stop pressed anywhere lands in seconds. Two `rag-reindex` / `rag-backfill` runs can no longer start together — a partial unique index `runs_one_live_per_kind` refuses the second insert, the start reads it as "already running", a backfill stands down under a live reindex, and each collection's `rag_points` delete and schema stamp are one transaction after the Qdrant drop. `start_scheduler` refuses to arm when a required job is missing (the docs now say nine), a research search call is bounded at nine minutes and re-entered from its checkpoint up to twice before it counts as a failed angle, the `research_runs` and `plan_drafts` rows are written before their run is enqueued (so the drive can no longer lose the caller's conversation and dials), the plan-draft save fails loudly on zero rows, and `store.answer` carries the question key in its UPDATE predicate. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-runs-run -p talaria-runs-store -p talaria-runs-reclaim -p talaria-runs-reindex -p talaria-research-def -p talaria-research -p talaria-plan-drafts -p talaria-runs-plan-draft -p talaria-scheduler -p talaria-jobs`, clippy `-D warnings` on the same, `bun run migrations:check` replaying 458 statements against the worktree database with the snapshot matching, `node scripts/check-invariants.mjs`.

- **Fixed:** Three things on the chat persistence path. A stream that died mid-reply, or an agent whose gateway refused the turn after some prose had already arrived, had its words replaced by the error line; the drained prose is now kept and the reason is appended after it, the same rule the stale sweep already followed. Two tabs sending into one conversation at the same instant raced for the next message number and the loser got a 500; the loser now gets a 409 that says another message landed at the same moment and to send again, and an assistant row that loses the same race takes the next free number instead of leaving a question with no reply row. A pinned agent whose Hermes state volume was lost (a re-hire on the same slug, a swapped volume, a host restore) silently answered from an empty session while the transcript on screen said otherwise; the session create now tells a fresh room from an existing one, and a fresh room where a transcript was expected sends that turn with its full history instead, logged once per conversation. A steer the running agent accepted mid-turn was re-sent to Hermes on the next turn as part of the message; it is now left out of the transcript the agent is sent, as it already was out of the chain. Verified: `talaria-chat-persist` unit tests (`dead_stream`, `conversation_line`), `talaria-gateway` tests, `talaria-conversations` and `talaria-routes-comms` clippy clean with `-D warnings`; `bun run check`.

- **Fixed:** Deleting or archiving a conversation left its scheduled jobs ticking in the agent's own scheduler — each run reaching the cron-output door, finding no listener and being dropped, forever and unmetered. A hard delete now removes the thread's jobs from the agent before the cascade drops the rows that name them; an archive pauses them (the rows stay, so the schedule list still shows them) and a restore resumes the same set. Best-effort per job: a container that cannot be reached is logged and the delete or archive still proceeds. Verified: `talaria-agent-crons` and `talaria-routes-comms` clippy clean with `-D warnings`; `bun run check`.

- **Fixed:** A hire run re-entering its create stage adopted any agent with the same slug — another manager's, if two hires raced — wrote its starter skills onto it and reported success without ever adding the hirer as a manager; a process death mid-create left an agent the hirer did not manage. The create stage now stamps `managed` and the hirer's manager row in one transaction straight after the def is written, and the resume path adopts a def only when it is managed and the hirer is among its managers — anything else is the honest "already exists" conflict. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-fleet-create -p talaria-runs-agent-hire`, clippy `-D warnings` on both.

- **Fixed:** Editing an MCP server's URL kept everything the old host had been trusted with. The org headers, the stored OAuth discovery and every connected account's token stayed on the row, and the next gateway call — or the hourly health pass — sent them to the new host. A URL whose host or port moves now drops all of it: every `mcp_oauth_tokens` row (the org's and each person's), the in-flight OAuth states and reconnect flags, the stored discovery, and the sealed org headers unless the same request sets new ones; the catalog is cleared as before and the route then asks the new host what auth it wants and what tools it has, inline, so the server card and the "drop missing tools" offer never read an empty catalog as "all missing". A `timeoutSecs` change now rolls the server's carriers too — it rides config.yaml, and a running Hermes only reads it at start. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-mcp` (the host-change rule has a unit test: path, scheme, case and default port are the same host; host, subdomain and port are not), `cargo test -p talaria-routes-fleet`, clippy `-D warnings` on both, `bun run check`. The DB side of the drop has no unit test — the crate's suites are pure (RUST-MIGRATION rule 9).

- **Fixed:** A secret's `allowed_hosts` is now checked against the server that actually receives the credential, not only against hosts mentioned in the arguments. The gateway hands the spend boundary the destination — the upstream URL's host for a remote server, or a token for a server Talaria answers itself (`talaria-builtin://`, `talaria-workbench://`, `talaria-pkg://<name>`, `talaria-app://<slug>`), which an allowlist names verbatim to admit — and a restricted secret refuses when the list does not cover it, whatever the arguments say. Before, a secret restricted to `github.com` could be sent to any server the agent could call by mentioning `github.com` somewhere in the arguments, and the audit row recorded the mentioned host as where it went. The `secrets.spend` audit row now carries the destination beside the mentioned hosts. Handles are substituted by walking the parsed arguments tree and replacing inside each string, instead of splicing the value into serialized JSON, so a value carrying a quote, a backslash or a newline (a service-account blob, say) lands intact; before, such a value broke the JSON round trip, the literal handle went upstream, and a one-shot relay had already been burned and destroyed on the attempt. A handle written twice into one call now spends once. A legacy shared-key caller (identified by the org-wide key, not proven to be the agent it names) spends nothing: each handle it wrote is reported to the operator as `unproven-caller`. The same rules apply on the app-server gateway in the TS runtime, which passes `talaria-app://<slug>` and the caller's proof. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-workspace-secrets` (a quote-and-backslash value round-trips the tree exactly, keys are never substituted, each spelling is listed once); `cargo test -p talaria-routes-fleet --lib mcp_gw_server` (the destination is the host or the first-party token, lowercased, and a token admits only when named verbatim); `bunx vitest run src/server/workspace-secrets.test.ts` (51 passed) (a restricted secret refuses `mcp.notion.com` while the arguments mention github.com, admits the host, a subdomain and a named token, the audit row names the destination; nested quote/backslash values substitute intact and a one-shot written twice spends once; an unproven caller gets nothing); `bun run typecheck`; clippy `-D warnings`; `bun run check` (its invariant pass reports three failures, all in files this change does not touch: a hand-unwrapped secretbox in `fleet_defs_id_rotate_key.rs`, an off-board status literal in `mcp/src/index.ts`, and duplicate `too_many_requests`/`agent_brake` bodies in the knowledge and comms route crates).

- **Fixed:** A work session that went silent during a long tool call was failed at ten minutes and re-opened by the redispatch sweep against an agent still mid-turn, and "stop work session" was undone the same way within six minutes, up to twenty-five times — by any board viewer. The agent's own tool-event frames now ping the turn's liveness tap (the thrash watcher subscribes to the run's watch channel already), a session that erred moments ago gets the same two-minute settle a reclaimed turn gets before a new generation starts, the stop route requires edit access and writes a `work_dispatch_blocks` row per (ticket, agent) that the dispatcher refuses until a person moves the ticket's status, and disabled agents are not dispatched at all. The thrash watcher is aborted whenever the turn's future is dropped (it leaked a task and a Redis subscription per interrupted turn), and `live_work_session_for(agent, session)` answers a tool frame's run by the session id it names — the tool-events route should call it before its newest-session fallback. The gateway hold re-POSTs a turn only when the connection was refused or reset before any byte; a 502/503/504 or silent headers after the request was sent come back as the error they are instead of a second copy of the same turn. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-runs-work-session -p talaria-work-dispatch -p talaria-gateway -p talaria-routes-boards`, clippy `-D warnings` on the same, `bun run migrations:check` with the snapshot matching.

- **Fixed:** Any signed-in user could re-point another team's ticket onto a particular person's coding subscription, list which accounts (emails) sit behind agents on boards they could not see, and — because the pinned `model` went onto the harness's invocation line verbatim — put a shell command into a Developer Agent's sandbox. The ticket coding-pin routes (`GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /api/workbench/coding/pin/{taskId}`) now require `can_edit` on the ticket's board, the same gate the human job route puts on approving a plan, and answer 404 for a ticket that is not there. A pinned model, and every per-role pick on an agent's coding plans, must fit the model-id grammar `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:/-]{0,199}$` (400 otherwise). Independently of that, every value slotted into an invocation line — the `--model` argument, the session dir, the inline `PI_SMOL_MODEL`/`PI_SLOW_MODEL`/`PI_PLAN_MODEL` assignments — is now shell-quoted (`sh_quote`: the model vocabulary passes through bare, anything else is single-quoted), so a value that gets in some other way is one word, not a command. The sandbox's `OPENAI_API_KEY` is `${LLM_WORKBENCH_API_KEY}` alone; the `:-${LLM_API_KEY}` fallback that let model-authored code read the personas' fleet-wide, unmetered key out of its own environment is gone (an operator on a raw upstream sets `LLM_WORKBENCH_API_KEY` explicitly). Verified: `talaria-coding-accounts`, `talaria-workbench-harnesses` and `talaria-routes-workbench` unit tests — the grammar's accept/reject table, the hostile `x; curl … | sh; #` model arg landing as one quoted word on both the `--model` line and the role env prefix, and the env carrying no `LLM_API_KEY` — fmt and clippy `-D warnings` clean on all three.

- **Changed:** An agent holding a tool subset on an MCP server is now refused `resources/*`, `prompts/*` and `completion/*` with JSON-RPC `-32601`, and each refusal is recorded in the call record under the request's own method. A subset is an admin's statement about what the agent may reach, and those surfaces relayed with the injected credential and no tool name for the gate to read — so an agent narrowed to one tool could still read every resource the server exposed, unrecorded. An agent with no subset keeps today's relay; `initialize`, `ping`, notifications and the tool methods are unaffected. Documented under "Enforcement: the gateway" in `docs/MCP.md`. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-routes-fleet --lib mcp_gw_server` (each closed method is refused with -32601 under a subset and relays without one; protocol chatter and the tool methods pass); `cargo test -p talaria-mcp --lib calls::` (a refused method begins a log under its own method, capped like a tool name; a tools/call still records as `tools/call`); clippy `-D warnings`; `bun run check` (its invariant pass reports three failures, all in files this change does not touch: a hand-unwrapped secretbox in `fleet_defs_id_rotate_key.rs`, an off-board status literal in `mcp/src/index.ts`, and duplicate `too_many_requests`/`agent_brake` bodies in the knowledge and comms route crates).

- **Fixed:** A workchain `positions` PATCH naming only some steps silently un-gated the rest (no predecessor reads as the head, and the heartbeat served them to agents at once), two concurrent wires could land a 2-cycle because the cycle walk and the insert were separate statements, and a repeated `taskId` stored a self-edge. The PATCH now refuses a line that does not name every step exactly once, the edge POST checks and inserts under the chain's row lock in one transaction, and the table carries `CHECK (from_step <> to_step)` (existing self-edges are deleted by the migration). A workflow PUT is one transaction. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-routes-boards -p talaria-workflows`, clippy `-D warnings` on both, `bun run migrations:check` with the snapshot matching.

- **Changed:** `create_google_doc` and `create_google_folder` stay immediate in the account's own Drive or inside a folder the agent created, and now queue for approval (`doc_create` / `drive_folder_create`, executed at approve time and recorded as the agent's) when the caller names any other parent folder — a file placed in a shared folder inherits that folder's sharing, which is a disclosure a person decides. An agent's standing to replace the whole body of a doc it created without a card ends when someone else edits it: the route asks Drive for the last modifier before an immediate full-body replace, and a doc last changed by anyone other than the token holder queues like a human-owned doc from then on (an append stays immediate). The agent arm of `export_to_google_doc` writes the same `artifact.export_google` audit row the human arm does, with the identity it acted as and the file it made. `create_google_meeting` and `update_google_event` validate like `draft_calendar_event`: attendees are checked addresses capped at 50, the agenda is bounded, and `start` / `end` must be a date or an RFC 3339 timestamp. `read_drive_file` and `import_drive_file` stop at the upload limit (25 MiB), on `Content-Length` and again on the streamed bytes. Google token refresh, revoke, exchange and userinfo calls carry a 60-second request timeout. Verified: `talaria-google-docs`, `talaria-google-drive`, `talaria-google-pending`, `talaria-routes-integrations`, `talaria-routes-knowledge`, `talaria-google-connections`, `talaria-google-org` and `talaria-google-oauth` unit tests, `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` on each, and `bun run check`. The Drive round-trips themselves need a consented Google account and were not exercised live in this change.

- **Fixed:** Four agent-plane doors accepted less identity than they acted on. `GET /api/agents/{id}/heartbeat` let an UNNAMED org-wide-key caller read any agent's work queue and stamp its liveness (the cross-check only ran for a caller it could name) — it now refuses with 403 `x-agent-name required`. `POST /api/agents/register` was gated on "holds any fleet key" and upserted by `name`, so any credential could rewrite any agent's role, framework, capabilities and status — the row is now bound to the caller's identity: a `tak_` caller registers only its own model, a legacy caller only the name it asserted (and never a personal or elevated one, which `agent_caller` already refuses), anything else is 403 "this credential belongs to …". `POST /api/agents/cron-output` and `POST /api/tasks/{id}/usage` wrote under `caller.model` without asking whether that identity was proven; both now call `refuse_legacy`, so a shared-key holder naming a non-privileged agent can no longer post a fabricated cron reply into its listening thread or inflate its ticket spend. `GET /api/skills/{owner}/{name}` let any signed-in member read every agent's SKILL.md, a personal assistant's custom prompts included — the shared root and an org agent's skills stay org work material, a personal assistant's are readable by its owner, its managers and fleet-wide readers only. Also: `edit_cron_job` trimmed AFTER its leading-dash guard (a prompt of `" --schedule …"` reached `hermes cron edit` as an option); it trims first now, name and schedule alike, matching `create_cron_job`. Verified: `cargo clippy -p talaria-routes-fleet -p talaria-routes-boards -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p talaria-routes-fleet -p talaria-agent-crons`.

- **Changed:** The agent write doors that fan out — to every channel member, every admin, web push, mail and an LLM call — now carry per-agent budgets, each answering 429 with Retry-After in the house error shape and failing open when Redis is unreachable like every limiter in this house: channel posts 30/min, reactions 60/min, `/api/search` 60/min for an agent caller, `report_gap` and `report_problem` 10/hour, `create_kb_space` 20/day (counted from the table, so a restart hands nothing back). A notification kind an agent originates is capped per recipient: fifty agent mentions a day land in a person's inbox and the rest are dropped with a log line, so a thousand `@jon ping` posts become fifty rows and fifty pushes. A repeat of a capability gap bumps its count and last-seen stamp and nothing else — a gap a person dismissed stays dismissed instead of flipping back to open on every repeat (the dedupe key was already the normalized kind: lowercase, non-alphanumerics folded). The 429 and the brake live once, in `talaria-ratelimit`, and every door imports them. Verified: `cargo clippy -p talaria-ratelimit -p talaria-notify -p talaria-mentions -p talaria-gaps -p talaria-routes-comms -p talaria-routes-knowledge -p talaria-routes-fleet -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test` on the same crates; `bun run check`.

- **Changed:** Pointing an agent at another person's Google account is an admin's call. `PUT /api/fleet/defs/{id}/google` with `principalKind: owner` and a `principalUserId` that is not the caller now answers 403 unless the caller is an admin; an agent's manager can still bind it to their own account. Either way the person named is notified in-app — which agent, pointed by whom, and where to undo it — beside the audit row the route already wrote. Connecting an agent's own Google account records the manager who did it (`connected_by`) and writes an `agent.google_connect` audit row; connecting the shared org account writes `google.org_connect`. `docs/GOOGLE-WORKSPACE.md` now lists the scopes the code actually requests (`openid`, `email`, full `drive`, `calendar.events`, `gmail.modify`, `gmail.send`; full `calendar` and `drive` for the org connect) instead of the retired `drive.file` / `drive.readonly` / `gmail.readonly` set. Verified: `talaria-routes-fleet`, `talaria-routes-integrations` and `talaria-google-oauth` unit tests, `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` on each, and `bun run check`.

- **Fixed:** An agent key can no longer put a document on the unauthenticated web or re-point a file at an upload it cannot read. `POST /api/artifacts` from a general agent always creates at `org` visibility — the `visibility` field is still validated and then ignored, as the PUT has always stripped it, because publishing is the human `artifacts.publish` power (the MCP `create_document`, `create_sheet` and `create_page` descriptions still advertise `public`; they are wrong and should say the field is ignored for every agent). An agent's `PUT /api/artifacts/{id}` with a `storageRef` is refused unless the agent can read that upload through its own access model (a ticket on a board it works, a channel it sits in), so a non-private artifact cannot be used to widen an upload's audience. Agent creates — the artifacts route and `agent-media/{model}/save` — now write an `artifact.create` audit row under `agent:<model>`, as a person's create always has. `edit_document` carries a version precondition: the save binds the `updated_at` the read carried and writes only if the row still has it; when a person saved in between, the edit is re-read and re-applied once (anchored edits make that safe), and a second move answers 409 "the document moved — read it again" instead of silently replacing the paragraph that landed in the window. `DELETE /api/artifacts/{id}` and `POST …/pull/google` answer 404, not 500, to an id that is not a uuid. Verified: `cargo clippy -p talaria-artifacts -p talaria-routes-knowledge -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p talaria-artifacts -p talaria-routes-knowledge`; `bun run check`.

- **Fixed:** `post_to_channel`'s `threadId` now threads an agent's post — the root is resolved exactly as a person's is (replying to a reply re-roots onto its thread; an unknown root is a 400) where it used to be silently dropped and the reply landed top-level. An agent's mention notification names the channel it was posted in, not the agent (the two arguments were swapped). An archived channel is closed to agents on every arm, so a seat left on its roster no longer keeps a door open the person who archived it believes is shut. The reactions route authenticates and checks channel access before it looks the message up, so an outsider learns nothing about whether a (channel, message) pair exists. Verified: `cargo clippy -p talaria-channels -p talaria-routes-comms -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p talaria-channels -p talaria-routes-comms`; `bun run check`.

- **Fixed:** One approval could ring twice — the request path on one instance and the escalation sweep on another both read an empty announce map in the same window and each wrote its mark only after sending — and in a mixed-version fleet the instance that could not define a run kind pruned the mark the other wrote, re-announcing the question on alternating ticks. Both announcers now claim the mark in one statement under the settings row's lock before sending and give it back when nobody heard, and the prune keeps every key a parked run still carries, whatever its kind. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-approvals`, `cargo clippy -p talaria-approvals -- -D warnings`.

- **Changed:** Approving an agent's email or calendar chip no longer unlocks that tool for the rest of the conversation. The grant an approval leaves on the conversation (`conversations.unlocked_tools`, now `{tool, expiresAt, usesLeft, recipients}` per tool instead of a bare name) lasts 30 minutes, covers one further call, and — for `gmail_send` and `calendar_create` — only a draft whose to/cc/bcc or attendees are a subset of the people the approved draft named; the next `draft_email` / `draft_calendar_event` spends it once, under a row lock, and answers "Sent — the earlier approval covered this one; the next needs its own." Anything outside the grant queues a fresh card, and the old unbounded string entries grant nothing. A pending Google action is now claimed (`status = 'executing'`) before it runs, so two approvals of the same row inside the Google round-trip — two admins, or the chip and the inbox card — send once and the second sees it already decided; a not-connected outcome hands the row back. `list_pending_sends` / `read_pending_send` show an org agent only the rows it queued, not every org agent's unsent mail. Verified: `talaria-chips` unit tests (grant shape, recipient normalisation, subset rule, one-use consumption, merge), `talaria-google-pending` and `talaria-routes-integrations` unit tests, `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy -D warnings` on each, and `bun run check`. The live approve path against a real Google account was not exercised in this change.

- **Fixed:** An npm or pypi package server answered the Workbench's catalog instead of its own. The package spec parser required an `image`, which only an oci package carries — nothing ever recorded the stock runtime image for the other two kinds — so every npm/pypi row failed to parse, fell through the registry's in-process branch, and had the Workbench's tools stored as its catalog (and the gateway could not dispatch to it at all). The runtime image is now one table (`runtime_image(kind)`) read by the parser and by the install's pull; a package row that still does not parse (the install's pull has not pinned it yet) answers "ask again shortly" instead of falling through; and the in-process branch serves the Workbench's catalog only to the Workbench row. Verified: against a worktree stack, installing `@modelcontextprotocol/server-memory` as an npm package and refreshing its tools answered the Workbench's seven tools before the fix; `cargo clippy -p talaria-mcp -p talaria-routes-fleet --tests -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p talaria-mcp` after.

- **Fixed:** The MCP OAuth callback now requires a Talaria session, and the signed-in person must be the subject the flow was started for — or hold `agents.manage` for an `org` flow. Before, the callback had no session check: a user could start a flow for their own row, hand the provider's authorize link to somebody else, and when that person consented the provider's redirect stored their tokens under the first user's connection. A state older than ten minutes is refused at the callback (states were only swept at the next start, so one could sit for days); a state the wrong person or a stale one arrives with is consumed, not left for a retry. The callback page still explains each refusal in the same window. Starting a personal (`scope=me`) connection is refused on a server that does not take one — disabled, not per-user, the builtin toolkit, an app's in-process server — before any discovery or registration runs against the server's URL. Storing a personal connection's headers (`PUT /api/me/mcp`) now requires an existing, enabled, per-user server, refuses the framing and hop-by-hop names (`host`, `content-length`, `transfer-encoding`, `connection`, `mcp-session-id`, `cookie` and the like) outright, and when the server declares its `requiredHeaders` takes only those names (`Authorization` stands in when nothing is declared, as the connect form offers); a disconnect still works on any existing server. A legacy shared-key caller is now refused the Workbench and gets no org OAuth bearer, as `subject_proven`'s contract always said. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-mcp-oauth --lib` (a state started for one user is refused to another, an org state needs the permission, a user named "org" cannot pass as the org); `cargo test -p talaria-routes-integrations --lib me_mcp` (the never-set names, the declared-set rule, `Authorization` without a declaration); `cargo clippy -p talaria-routes-fleet -p talaria-mcp -p talaria-mcp-oauth -p talaria-routes-integrations --tests -- -D warnings`; `bun run check` (its invariant pass reports three failures, all in files this change does not touch: a hand-unwrapped secretbox in `fleet_defs_id_rotate_key.rs`, an off-board status literal in `mcp/src/index.ts`, and duplicate `too_many_requests`/`agent_brake` bodies in the knowledge and comms route crates).

- **Fixed:** App-published MCP servers are governed exactly like every other server, which `docs/sdk/mcp.md` had promised and the TypeScript gateway had not kept. Team grants work: the resolver behind `/api/mcp/gw/app-<slug>` now reads `mcp_team_access` joined to `team_agents` for the agent and to `team_members` for the acting owner, with the Rust resolver's rules (a team grant counts as assignment on a scoped server; a person's own deny wins; a team deny with no allow anywhere denies; null is all tools, `[]` is none), so an admin granting an app to a team no longer gets `403 no access to this MCP server` from every agent on it. Every app `tools/call` — the refused ones too — lands as a row in `mcp_tool_calls` with the same columns and the same never-the-arguments rule as the Rust gateway's call log (tool name capped at 200, one sentence capped at 300 and scrubbed of the agent's argument strings, a fixed sentence when the call spent a credential), so Observability shows app calls beside the rest. The registry row's tool catalog, which Rust seeds as `[]` and cannot fill, is written from the module on the first load after enablement and on every build, so Manage → MCP's tool-subset picker has something to pick. A call's `arguments` must be a JSON object, and app tool arguments are checked against the advertised `inputSchema` (zod's `fromJSONSchema`, extra properties allowed; a schema it cannot compile is passed through) before the handler runs, so a wrong shape is a tool error naming the field rather than a `TypeError` naming nothing. Verified: `bun run test -- src/server/mcp-registry.test.ts` (13 tests over the agent- and owner-side grant rules, the tables faked by query shape), `bun run typecheck` (svelte-check, 0 errors), `cd mcp && bun run build`; not exercised against a live stack in this change — the call-log insert statement is the Rust one verbatim against the same schema snapshot.

- **Fixed:** The docs stop disagreeing with the toolkit. No document states the tool count any more (`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` said 51, `DEVELOPERS.md` 62, the fitness crate's header 62, against 84 registered): they say "the toolkit's registered tools", the count is checked by `bun run check`, and `mcp/README.md` lists every tool by name, one line each, grouped by family — it named 33. The README no longer teaches the scope-drop trick the toolkit's own constants forbid, and it and `mcp/src/index.ts` cite the workspace paths (`api/crates/talaria-tasks`, `talaria-mcp-service`, `talaria-agent-auth`, `talaria-routes-fleet`) rather than the pre-workspace `api/src/…` ones, which matters because the README's "the warning lives at every file the edit passes through" argument depends on those paths being real. `docs/sdk/mcp.md` and `docs/APPS.md` say that a tool argument may arrive carrying a resolved credential and must not be persisted, that `inputSchema` is now enforced, that every call is recorded (never its arguments), and that an app's throw isolation covers awaited throws only. Verified: `bun run check` (`check-docs` link check, the new count and README-completeness checks); `git grep 'api/src/' mcp/` returns nothing.

- **Changed:** Every agent container now reaches the LLM gateway on **its own** key instead of one fleet-wide `LLM_API_KEY` shared by every sandbox. The fleet render mints a `tlk_` key per enabled agent (`agent:<slug>`), stamps it into `fleet/.env` as `LLM_API_KEY_<SLUG>` beside the agent's `tak_` credential, and interpolates it into that agent's compose service as `LLM_API_KEY` — so Hermes and the rendered `config.yaml` keep reading the same variable, but no container holds the fleet's key; a retired agent keeps its line, a slug that no longer exists loses both the line and the key. At the relay an agent key is the agent: its budget subject is the agent's model id (so `llm_budgets.perAgent` and `agents{…}` finally bind an agent, on the same `agent_model` window its chat turns are ledgered in), its calls are unmetered and never annotated by prefix rather than by a list, and a request for any model outside the set its rendered config routes to (`gateway_agent_models`, written by the render) is a 403 before any upstream is touched; `GET /v1/models` on that key lists the same set. Cron-driven turns inside a container remain unmetered at the relay — Hermes makes that call, not Talaria, so nothing the chat proxy sends can mark it; closing that needs the chat proxy to register its in-flight turns. Verified: `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --tests -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` for `talaria-gateway`, `talaria-fleet-brain`, `talaria-fleet-render`, `talaria-routes-fleet` (new unit tests pin the key-name round trip, the scope row the render writes and the relay reads, the model gate's exact match, the `LLM_API_KEY_<SLUG>` sweep and the relay's subject rule); `bun run check`.

- **Fixed:** `list_boards` answers each board's own status keys to an agent — `statuses: [{key, label, category, agentStart}]` on every row, in the board's order with the system Blocked column where it sits — so an agent on a board that renamed its columns can read the key before it moves a ticket instead of learning it from a 400; `triage_ticket`'s description points at it. Verified: `cargo clippy -p talaria-routes-boards --tests -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p talaria-routes-boards`; `cd mcp && bun run build` for the description change.

- **A new agent starts closed: no shell, no code execution, no file tool, no self-scheduling, and no cross-conversation recall on a shared agent — until a manager opens each one.** Every Hermes toolset used to be on for every hire and Talaria forced Hermes' approval gates to `approve`, so a default agent could run `env` and `curl` on a prompt-injected page with no confirmation step anywhere in the chain. `talaria-agent-defs` now carries `DEFAULT_DISABLED_FOR_NEW` (`terminal`, `code_execution`, `file`, `cronjob`), written into `disabled_toolsets` on INSERT only (an existing slug keeps what its managers opened; `browser`, `delegation`, `memory` stay on), plus `session_search` for an agent that is nobody's personal assistant (`SHARED_AGENT_DISABLED` — the personal create path opens it once the owner is marked). The Developer Agent switch opens `terminal`/`file`/`code_execution` when turned on and closes them when turned off (`apply_developer_toolsets`, on a change only). The rendered `approvals` block follows the same switch: a Developer Agent keeps `unattended_mode`/`cron_mode: approve`; every other agent renders `deny`, which refuses `execute_code` and a dangerous terminal command outright instead of waving them through — file, browser, web, memory and MCP calls are not approval-gated and are untouched. An org-level floor joins the mandatory pair: the `app_settings` key `agents.mandatory_disabled_toolsets` (a JSON array of governed names, set with SQL for now — no admin route writes it yet) and/or the env `TALARIA_MANDATORY_DISABLED_TOOLSETS` (comma-separated), merged ahead of every agent's own list by the renderer; strangers are logged and dropped. The toolset editor still shows the per-agent list; the org floor is not yet painted there. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-agent-defs` (new tests pin the closed default, the personal exception, the developer trio and the floor merge) and `cargo test -p talaria-fleet-render` (the approvals and toolset-merge tests updated for the new signatures), clippy `-D warnings` clean on both.

- **Fixed:** Two workbench jobs could share one branch. `start_job`'s one-job-per-ticket check only counted `started`, so a second call while the first was still `queued` or `awaiting_approval` minted the same deterministic branch name, "resumed" the first job's branch from a second workdir, and `finish_job` on either opened a PR carrying both. The check now counts `started`, `queued` and `awaiting_approval`. The queue sweep's promotion (`queued → started`) re-asks the per-agent live cap and the per-ticket rule at the moment the job would become a clone and a harness — holding a job that fails either in its place (not blocking the queue behind it) rather than flipping it on rules that were only true when it was filed. And the job sweep gained two conservative staleness rules for what nothing else can close: a `started` or awaiting-approval job with no ticket and no `updated_at` for seven days is abandoned and its workdir removed; a job still `queued` after a day is abandoned (it never had a workdir) and its ticket's board-level wait cleared. Verified: `talaria-workbench-queue` unit tests (the promotion rule at the cap and on a ticket with a started job), `talaria-workbench-mcp` unit tests (the sweep's decision table: closed tickets as before, an open ticket keeping its job however old, a ticketless job at six days left and at seven abandoned, a queued job at a day abandoned and younger left, undated never stale); fmt and clippy `-D warnings` clean on both.

- **Fixed:** A marketplace package could mount the host into its container. The run-flag allowlist admitted `-v`, `--volume`, `--mount` and `--add-host` by name alone, so a registry entry (or anyone holding `agents.manage`) could declare `-v /:/host` or mount the docker socket and run an image of its choosing as root — host root, every fleet key, the Postgres volume. The gate now checks values, not just names (`check_run_flag`, shared by the install parser and the spawn): a volume may only be a `talaria-mcp-*` named volume with an absolute destination, a publish may only bind `127.0.0.1`, `--mount` and `--add-host` are refused outright, and an admin's fill for a placeholder passes the same rule as the declaration. Every package container now runs as uid 65534 on a read-only root with one tmpfs at `/tmp` (HOME — npx and uv keep their caches there, so a respawn re-downloads; the named cache volumes are gone). oci-http containers get their own `talaria-mcp-<instance>` bridge network, which the api joins on demand when it runs in-image, instead of the api's `*_internal` network beside Postgres, Redis and Qdrant. Installing a package server is an admin's call (403 otherwise); URL-only servers keep `agents.manage`. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-mcp` (the flag rule has its own test, value by value, including the docker-socket and `/` cases), `cargo test -p talaria-routes-fleet`, clippy `-D warnings` on both, `bun run check`.

- **Changed:** The doom-loop guard counted identical `(tool, arguments)` calls and stopped the turn at five, so an agent polling a build job every thirty seconds was cut off as if it were stuck. The guard now counts a call at its completion, keyed on the tool, its arguments and a hash of what the call produced: the same call with the same answer is the loop, the same call with a changing answer is polling and is never touched. The two thresholds are settings — `chat.loop_warn_at` and `chat.loop_stop_at` in `app_settings`, defaults 3 and 5, read once per turn — so an operator who knows a workflow repeats raises them without a rebuild; a stop set equal to the warn is the stop. Verified: `talaria-chat-persist` unit tests (`doom_loop`: thresholds, settings parsing and fallback, polling exempt, the moment the answer stops moving counts) and clippy clean with `-D warnings`; `bun run check`.

- **Fixed:** An agent key could start research — an expedition included — with no permission, no agent gate and no limit, and a plan draft could be pointed at any board by id. `POST /api/research` on the agent leg now requires that the agent's responsible user (the attribution ladder's answer) holds `research.run`, refuses an agent with nobody behind it, and caps an agent at two live runs and twenty a day, answered 429. `POST /api/plans/{id}/draft` and `POST /api/channels/{id}/plan` now require edit access on the body's `boardId` before the run that reads that board's tickets, labels and members is enqueued; a stranger gets a 403 where they used to get the board's open tickets back as proposals. Verified: `cargo clippy -p talaria-routes-workbench -p talaria-routes-boards -p talaria-routes-comms -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo test -p` for the three route crates, `bun run docs:api` and `bun run check`.

- **Fixed:** Two rolls of one department could remove each other's live container: a roll read `active_slot` and `max(gateway_port)+1`, rendered, cut over and removed the old slot with nothing written back until the cutover, so a double click, a `roll_running_agents` racing `reconcile_fleet`, or two api instances interleaved into the same slot and port. `roll_agent` now holds a process-wide per-department set (`talaria-fleet-reconcile`'s `ROLLING`, the shape chat-persist's `CONTINUING` guard has) and a Postgres session-level advisory lock (`pg_try_advisory_lock(hashtext('fleet-roll:<department>'))`, released on every path) around the slot read → cutover → remove sequence; a second roll answers the soft verdict "already mid-roll", the control route answers 409 up front, and `reconcile_fleet` skips a department mid-roll instead of starting its steady-state service under the cutover. Also fixed: `fleet/.env`, `fleet.json`, every `config.yaml` and the compose file were rewritten in place (truncate, then write), so a process killed mid-write left an empty env file that started every container with no key at all, and fleet-brain's writer created the env file with the process umask. All five now go through `talaria_fleet_brain::write_atomic` — a sibling temp file opened with the target mode (0600 for `.env` and `fleet.json`), fsynced, renamed over the target. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-fleet-brain` (a new test checks the bytes, the mode and that no temp file survives), `cargo test -p talaria-fleet-render`, `cargo clippy -p talaria-fleet-reconcile -- -D warnings`.

- **Added:** `POST /api/fleet/defs/{id}/rotate-key` — this agent's managers revoke its `tak_` credential and mint a fresh one, the answer to a leaked key that is not "retire the agent". The old secret stops authenticating the moment the `agent_keys` row is replaced; the route re-renders the fleet (the new secret lands in `fleet/.env`) and queues a roll so the running container is recreated on it, answering `{ ok, rolling }`. The audit trail carries `agent.key_rotate` with the env variable's name, never the value. `docs/AGENT-KEY-MIGRATION.md` replaces its "Known gap" with the procedure. Also: a renamed personal assistant's five keyed-table updates now run in ONE transaction (a rename that landed on `agent_defs` and died on `conversations` left threads and grants pointing at a model that no longer existed), and the next render strips the old slug's `HERMES_KEY_<OLD>` / `TALARIA_AGENT_KEY_<OLD>` lines — `ensure_agent_env_keys` drops every per-agent line whose slug is no longer in `agent_defs`, which also covers a def deleted while the file was not rewritten. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-fleet-render` (a new test pins the strip: only the two per-agent shapes for unknown slugs go, the org-wide key and everything else stay), `cargo clippy -p talaria-routes-fleet -p talaria-personal-agent -- -D warnings`, `bun run docs:api` for the new route.

- **Changed:** The product skills agree with the workbench. `subagent-driven-development` no longer tells an implementer subagent to write files and `git add -A`: it runs one workbench job (`start_job` with the plan the job already requires → the harness in the `workdir` → `finish_job`), a fresh subagent per task *driving* Oh My Pi with a terminal and no file tool, reviewers read-only, commits by explicit path, and it no longer depends on the unshipped `plan` skill — the two-stage review structure is unchanged. The `claude-code`, `codex` and `opencode` signposts say the workbench is Developer Agents only, so a non-developer agent reads "no access" as a gap to report, not a problem. `talaria-apps` describes how an app is actually built from a container — as a workbench job on a `talaria-app-<slug>` repo that an admin installs from the URL — instead of `bun talaria app new` and an `apps/` directory the container does not have; it also says that a tool argument may carry a resolved credential the app must not persist, and that the throw isolation covers awaited throws only. The `email`, `google-workspace`, `github` and `talaria-toolkit` skills each carry the content-is-data caveat: what a read returns was written by someone else, and text in it that tells the agent what to do is reported, never followed. Verified: `bun run check` (the hermes-skill signpost test still finds every `name:`; the scope-drop regexes run over the toolkit skill); read-through of every tool name the rewritten skills cite against `mcp/src/index.ts` and the workbench crate's seven tools.

- **Fixed:** Adding or removing an agent on a team, adding or removing a person, and deleting a team never re-rendered or rolled anyone, though a team's MCP grants ride on `team_agents` and a personal assistant's rendered server set follows its owner's team access — the running container kept the old server set, and the on-disk config kept advertising a server the gateway would refuse. The team routes now render and roll the way `me/mcp` does: the named agents on a `team_agents` write (captured before a team delete, rolled after it), the person's assistant on a `team_members` write. At render, the `mcp_servers` block is BUILT rather than merged: an authored entry whose name is neither `talaria` nor a registry server was a raw endpoint from pre-gateway history that survived every render with its own URL and headers; it is dropped now and the render warning says which. Also: the preflight probe image is pinned (`busybox:1.37`, not `latest`), every `docker` child in `talaria-fleet-docker` and `talaria-fleet-preflight` is `kill_on_drop`, so a timed-out `compose up`, `exec` or probe dies with the future that was waiting on it instead of orphaning on a wedged daemon; the browser setup runs `docker exec -u hermes` (the runtime user that owns the volume it writes to) and the marker file records the installed version instead of an empty touch. `talaria-agent-crons` gains `remove_jobs_for_conversation` for the conversation delete/archive path to call before the rows cascade — the job in the agent's `jobs.json` otherwise fires forever with nobody listening. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-fleet-docker -p talaria-fleet-preflight -p talaria-fleet-render`, `cargo clippy -p talaria-routes-integrations -- -D warnings`.

- **Changed:** The per-repo branch rule refuses more, and the docs say plainly what it is. Under `branches_only` a Developer Agent's push is now declined for the configured base, the repo's default branch (a flow based on `rc` still has a `main` that promotion owns — before, only the configured base was refused) and `main`/`master`/`rc` whatever the rule names; `free` keeps its meaning as the operator's explicit opt-out. The installation token the sandbox's credential helper hands git is now narrowed to `contents: write`, `pull_requests: write` and `metadata: read` on top of its one-repo scope, with one retry on the installation's own grants (logged) when the App was never granted one of those; the installation-wide token used for listing and repo creation is not narrowed. And the sentence the 2026-09-22 entry made — "enforced by the platform before a byte leaves the container" — is withdrawn: the rule is asked by a client-side `pre-push` hook that git skips on `--no-verify`, and the token can push, so the base branch is only actually closed by the repository's own branch protection. `docs/WORKBENCH.md` and the `workbench-driving` skill now say branch protection on every granted repo is required, and the clone URL `start_job` returns is described as what it is, a plain `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git` with no credential in it. Verified: `talaria-github` unit tests — the decision table across a null base, a named base, an `rc` base with `main`/`master`/`rc`/`develop` all refused and `main-ish`/`rc/agent-1` allowed, and `free`; the narrowed `access_tokens` body carrying exactly the three permissions and the retry body none — fmt and clippy `-D warnings` clean; `bun run check` green.

- **Fixed:** The model-fitness code probe ran model-written JavaScript inside the api process, where boa's limits bound loop iterations and recursion but not memory and not its regex engine: a reply of `'x'.repeat(2**32-1)` allocated gigabytes in `talaria-api` before anything fired, and a catastrophic regex pinned a core the timeout could only abandon. The evaluation now runs in a child process — the api binary re-executed in a hidden argv mode (`talaria-api __code-probe`, dispatched in `main` before any runtime is built) that reads the script and budget as JSON on stdin and answers on stdout — under `RLIMIT_AS` (1 GiB, room for the binary's own image) and `RLIMIT_CPU` (the budget plus a few seconds) set in `pre_exec`, with an empty environment, and the parent kills it at its deadline. A runaway candidate now costs one small process and never the api; the in-process evaluator is the child's body and what the unit tests still call directly. Verified: `talaria-fitness-code-runner` unit tests (the grading suite as before, the child protocol round-tripping a reply, a non-string, a spin and a bad ask over in-memory streams, and the wrapper against a binary that is not an evaluator); the real `talaria-api` binary driven by hand in the hidden mode with an empty environment (a correct script answers `{"Outcome":{"Reply":…}}`, a spin answers the budget's own timeout sentence, a bad ask exits 2, and a string-doubling memory hog under a 1 GiB address-space limit aborts in under four seconds with `memory allocation … failed`, exit 134 — the api untouched); the api integration test `code_probe_child` covering the same chain is written beside the others in `api/tests/it` (its crate did not compile at the time on an unrelated in-flight change to `RunRow`, so it is not yet a green run); fmt and clippy `-D warnings` clean on the runner and on the `talaria-api` binary.

- **Fixed:** An agent answering several people at once could land one person's screenshot, question, plan, subagent card or tool chips in another person's thread. Every door now resolves its landing row by `(agent, conversation)`: the talaria-events plugin sends the Hermes session id on screenshot and subagent posts (it already did on tool events), and for a pinned agent that id is the conversation id; the MCP `ask`, `todo` and `expose_tools` tools take an optional `conversationId`, and every turn's prompt now carries a line naming the conversation so the model has it to pass. A door with no usable id is served only while the agent has exactly one turn it could mean — several, and it answers 409 with a sentence that names the ambiguity and the field that resolves it; an id naming a thread the agent is not in lands nothing. A screenshot stamped on a shared work session is now readable by that session's members and teams, the same readers the thread itself admits. The uploads and subagent-events route headers note the trust boundary: the key those doors take is readable from the container, so the platform cannot tell plugin from model and treats the chips as the agent's own claims. Verified: `talaria-chips` unit tests (the exactly-one-live-row rule, the recent tier, the hint parsing, the refusal sentence), `talaria-routes-fleet`, `talaria-routes-comms`, `talaria-chat-persist` and `talaria-uploads` clippy clean with `-D warnings` and tests green; `python3 -m py_compile` on the plugin; `bun run build` in `mcp/`; `bun run check`.

- **Changed:** The gates see what they were missing. The MCP end-to-end job's path filter names every crate the MCP story passes through — `talaria-agent-mcp`, `talaria-fleet-render`, `talaria-safe-fetch`, `talaria-api-routes`, `talaria-routes-integrations`, `talaria-body`, `talaria-users`, `talaria-workspace-secrets` — not only the ones spelled `mcp`, and `mcp end-to-end (playwright)` joins the required contexts for `rc` and `main` in `docs/BRANCHES.md`; branch protection lives in the repository, so an admin re-runs the two recipes for it to take effect, and it is safe to require because the job skips per job (`needs: [changes]` + a job-level `if`, which GitHub reports as success). `bun run check` gains the toolkit's prose gate: it reads every registration out of `mcp/src/index.ts` with the file's own regexes — resolving the interpolated constants so it sees whole sentences — and fails a description that names "closed" without archival, or any tool, field, README or toolkit-skill text that teaches an agent to drop a scope argument to get past a refusal (the pattern list gained the README's own wording, "without it the gap still lands"); it also fails any doc that states a toolkit tool count the source does not have, and a `mcp/README.md` that does not name every registered tool. Verified: `bun run check` from the worktree root — the new checks pass on this tree and the scope-drop rule caught the README sentence before it was deleted; the ci.yml `changes` step is shell, re-read for quoting.

- **Fixed:** Until an instance was claimed, any Google account that finished OAuth — or anyone who reached the password claim form — became the admin even when the operator had set `AUTH_ALLOWED_EMAILS` / `AUTH_ALLOWED_DOMAINS`. The org-domain gate and the allow-list now run before `claim_admin` on the Google callback, and the password claim refuses an address the allow-list does not name. Verified: `cargo clippy -p talaria-routes-integrations -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p talaria-routes-integrations`.

- **Fixed:** `report_problem` no longer rewrites a board. It used to find ANY live board named "Helpdesk" — a team's private one included — and on every call make it org-wide, move it to the Talaria team, join every user as editor and reset its agent policy. The Helpdesk board is now resolved by its stored id (`app_settings.helpdesk_board_id`), created exactly once — org-wide, on the Talaria team, open to every agent — and never written to again, so an admin's membership removals and agent restrictions stand; a stored board that was archived or deleted is replaced by a fresh one rather than resurrected. The route is braked at ten reports per agent per hour (429 with Retry-After, the house error shape), and the same agent reporting the same summary within a day is acknowledged — `duplicate: true`, a relay sentence — without a second ticket or a second round of admin notifications, the posture `report_gap` has always had. Verified: `cargo clippy -p talaria-routes-fleet -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p talaria-routes-fleet`; `bun run check`.

- **Fixed:** Four knowledge-base doors stopped answering with rows or placements their caller should not have. `create_kb_space`'s find-or-create matches only a space the agent could have listed — the same read gate as `GET /api/kb/spaces` — and a name collision with a space it cannot read is a 409 with no row, where it used to hand back a private space's landing page and owner. A `parentId` on doc create and on `PUT /api/kb/docs/{id}` passes the two checks the move route has always run — the parent is a doc of the same space, and not the doc itself or one of its descendants — so a doc can no longer be filed under itself (a loop for every tree builder) or into another space's tree. `GET /api/kb/public/{slug}` serves on the doc's EFFECTIVE visibility, inherited from its folder like every other read, so a doc inside a space made private is no longer public by its old slug. `GET /api/kb/search` runs its ACL over a 300-row ranked page instead of 60 before truncating to 20, so a member whose readable hits rank below a wall of private ones still gets them. A draft in a space bound to a custom brain no longer grounds that brain until a human marks it official — the gate the org brain always had; an owner's explicit per-doc routing still indexes as written. `DELETE /api/kb/docs/{id}` answers 404, not 500, to a non-uuid id. Verified: `cargo clippy -p talaria-kb -p talaria-retrieval-sources -p talaria-routes-knowledge -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test` on the same crates; `bun run check`.

- **Fixed:** The MCP gateway's relay to a registered upstream now goes out on a client that never follows a redirect and re-checks the address it dials at connect time, and any 3xx from the upstream is answered as a 502 ("upstream answered with a redirect, which the gateway does not follow") instead of being followed. Before, the hop used the first-party client, which followed up to ten redirects outside the SSRF guard — so a compromised upstream could bounce the api onto a cloud metadata address or a loopback port, with the org's API-key headers attached, and have the answer relayed into the model's context. The builtin toolkit and package containers keep the first-party client (loopback and container DNS are what the guard refuses); the relay still streams and never buffers. The gateway also forwards only a body that parsed: every parse failure — an empty body, a bare word, SSE framing, a body a UTF-8 byte-order mark made unparseable — is answered with JSON-RPC `-32700` over HTTP 200, and a leading BOM is stripped before parsing so a well-formed body behind one still works. Before, only a brace-led failure was refused and everything else was forwarded verbatim with the credentials attached and without the tool gate, the spend boundary or the `tools/list` filter running on it. The `tools/list` filter now reads multi-line `data:` frames (an SSE event's data lines are joined before parsing), so a server that splits one message over several lines no longer leaks its unfiltered catalog. The in-process dispatchers (builtin, Workbench, app servers) negotiate the MCP protocol revision on `initialize` the way the not-connected answer already did, instead of echoing whatever the client sent. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-safe-fetch` (9 passed; a loopback listener answering 302 gets exactly one request and the 302 comes back with its Location); `cargo test -p talaria-routes-fleet --lib mcp_gw_server` (the parse-failure set, the BOM strip, the multi-line SSE filter); `cargo test -p talaria-mcp-jsonrpc` and `-p talaria-mcp --lib not_connected` (a revision nobody speaks, or an empty one, is negotiated down); clippy `-D warnings` on each; `bun run check` (its invariant pass reports three failures, all in files this change does not touch: a hand-unwrapped secretbox in `fleet_defs_id_rotate_key.rs`, an off-board status literal in `mcp/src/index.ts`, and duplicate `too_many_requests`/`agent_brake` bodies in the knowledge and comms route crates).

- **Fixed:** Three smaller MCP registry edges. The marketplace mirror's incremental sync advanced its `updated_since` mark even when the run's time budget cut it off mid-window, so the pages it never fetched were never asked for again (a long outage followed by a catch-up is exactly that case); a cut-off run now keeps the mark and re-asks the window next run — the upsert is idempotent, a skipped page was not. Registering a server whose URL the library's liveness job last found dead now answers 400 with the probe's detail unless the body says `force: true` — the marketplace sends it when the person chose "show unreachable" and picked one. And the Talaria toolkit child (`mcp/dist`) no longer inherits the api's whole environment — the database URL, the secretbox key and every provider credential were in it; it gets what `mcp/src/index.ts` reads plus `PATH`, `HOME` and the `NODE_*` knobs. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-mcp-library`, `cargo test -p talaria-mcp-service`, `cargo test -p talaria-routes-fleet`, clippy `-D warnings` on each, `bun run check`.

- **Changed:** The `rc → main` promotion pull request lists what is going in — every changelog entry rc added over main, reduced to its bold lead sentence, with the count beside the commit count — and folds the raw commit log into a collapsed block below it, so the person merging reads the same sentences the release notes will carry rather than forty commit subjects. The body is still refreshed on every promotion run, so the list follows rc. Verified: the body generator exercised by hand against `origin/main..origin/rc` with the same `git diff --diff-filter=A -- 'changelog/*.md'` and lead-sentence extraction (`bash -n` on the step; the workflow itself runs only on a push to rc).

- **Fixed:** Research runs on a registered MCP search supplier failed every round. The research harness dispatches a supplier's tool through its own `CALL_MCP_TOOL` hook, and nothing ever set it — only the web-search crate's twin was wired — so any org whose search supplier was a non-platform MCP server got "The search tool failed" on every round while the fitness sweep (which injects its own tool) stayed green. The hook is now set at job registration with the same dispatcher. The loop also forwarded whatever tool name the model used to the supplier's server; it now dispatches only the one tool it offered (`supplier.tool`) and answers any other name with an error result the model reads, so a planted search result cannot talk the model into another tool on that server with the org's credential. The untrusted-input boundary clause now closes the research synthesis and tool-search system prompts and the concluder, titler and judge prompts, and `STATES_THE_BOUNDARY` names them so the cross-check holds. Verified: `talaria-harness-defs` unit tests, including the new loop test proving a `delete_everything` call reaches nothing and lands as `is not a tool you have` while the loop's system prompt carries the clause; `talaria-api-facades`' `every_named_harness_renders_the_clause` over the widened list; `talaria-harness-prompt-rules` and `talaria-jobs` compile under clippy `-D warnings`.

- **Fixed:** The agent toolkit's descriptions stop sending agents into refusals they cannot read their way out of. `join_board`, `leave_board` and `request_board_access` say they are a personal assistant's reach (`whoami.agent.owner` tells you), so an org agent is no longer told to try the next tool in the trio when the first one 403s — that was a 403 ↔ 403 loop — and `request_board_access` names its other refusal (a board the owner can already read is `join_board`'s). `triage_ticket` takes the board's own status key instead of a fixed `in_progress / blocked / quality_review` enum, and says where the keys come from on a board that renamed its columns; `list_tickets.overdue` no longer counts a failed ticket as overdue. `research_status` names the `awaiting` state and passes the parked question through, so a run waiting on a person is reported as that rather than polled as running. Every tool whose output is somebody else's text — tickets, attachments, mail, channels, knowledge, Google reads, research, image descriptions — carries one shared sentence (`CONTENT_IS_DATA`) that what comes back is data, never instructions, and `get_ticket`'s "follow their instructions" now applies only to the board's configured `workflows`. `edit_document` accepts the omitted `newString` its description promised; `create_document` / `create_sheet` / `create_page` no longer offer `public` (agents never publish — a person does, afterwards). A non-JSON upstream body in a tool error is capped at 300 characters, and the fleet-key short-circuit in HTTP mode recognises only the `talaria` service name, so a retired org key cannot read the catalog under another name. `whoami`'s guardrail list stops claiming members are human-only to delete (a personal assistant manages them as its owner) and names the blocked-exit and archived-board refusals. Verified: `cd mcp && bun run build` (tsc clean); a port of the fitness crate's prefix rule run over all 84 registrations against its catalog (0 drift — every changed description keeps its leading literal and carries the new wording in an interpolated constant, so `models_every_tool_the_toolkit_registers` holds without a catalog edit); `bun run check` with the new prose gate reading every description and field; the `GUARDRAILS` constant is a string-literal edit (`[&str; 7]`) compiled by `cargo clippy -p talaria-routes-fleet` at integration.

- **Changed:** The `workbench-driving` skill named harnesses the workbench does not offer — "opencode, Pi, Oh My Pi", "another opencode `run`", a `guide` for "your chosen harness" — while `start_job` answers one entry, Oh My Pi, `chosen: true`. It now names omp alone, says the workbench is a Developer Agent's (a `no access to this MCP server` answer is the switch, `report_gap` not `report_problem`), and tells the driver to push only the branch `start_job` named and never `--no-verify`. `docs/HARNESSES.md`'s file table pointed at `api/src/harness/*`, which moved to the `talaria-harness*` crates, and counted 39 shipped harnesses where `registry.rs`'s `EXPECTED_IDS` pins 40; both corrected, and the prompt-rules crate added to the table. Verified: `bun run check` (doc links and generated references) green.

- **Fixed:** `POST /api/chat` attached any upload id the sender named, read its bytes to the agent and stamped it on the sender's own row — after which the upload's access check answered yes for them from then on. Every attachment id now passes the same reach check the serve route asks (`can_access_upload`) before any of it is read; an id the sender cannot read is refused with 403 naming that id. Verified: `talaria-routes-comms` clippy clean with `-D warnings`; `bun run check`.

- **Fixed:** A cron run's final text landed in its listening thread with no person behind it and without the reply guard every streamed chat reply gets. `POST /api/agents/cron-output` now runs the chat path's own landing pass (`guard_chat_reply`: strict mode redacts the saved copy before it is written, annotate and strict pin the scrubbed findings on the row as the caveat the UI shows) and attributes the turn to the person who set the schedule up (`conversation_schedules.created_by`) as its responsible user, in the one slot a turn carries for a human. A re-delivered execution finds the stamp already there. Verified: `cargo clippy -p talaria-agent-crons -p talaria-routes-fleet --tests -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p talaria-routes-fleet`; `bun run check`.

- **Fixed:** An agent could keep replacing the body of a Google Doc it created after its owner had edited it from their own account: the only probe before an immediate replace was Drive's `lastModifyingUser.me`, and the owner is the token holder, so Drive reported the edit as the agent's own. `agent_created_google_docs` now carries `last_agent_write_at`, stamped on every agent write (create, immediate replace or append, and an approved `doc_update`); a full-body replace also holds Drive's `modifiedTime` against that stamp and queues for approval — dropping the agent's standing on the doc — when the revision is later than the agent's own write, by more than a 5-second clock-skew allowance. Appends stay immediate; rows from before the column fall back to the `me` flag alone until the agent's next write stamps them. The decision is the pure `modified_after_agent(modified_time, last_agent_write_ms)` in `talaria-google-docs`, with an RFC 3339 parser beside it. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-google-docs` (timestamp parsing incl. fractions, offsets, a leap day; a later/earlier/inside-skew revision; unknown on either side is not evidence); clippy `-D warnings` on `talaria-google-docs`, `talaria-google-pending`, `talaria-routes-integrations`; `cd ui && bun run migrations:check` replayed the appended migration against the worktree database and the snapshot matched; `bun run check`.

- **Fixed:** A fresh `talaria worktree` could render no fleet, and its `ui/.env`
  strip-list could drift one key short a third time. Two things seen on a fresh
  `bun talaria worktree <name> origin/rc`: the app on `:53xx` answered every
  `/api/*` with `upstream unreachable` while its own api was healthy on `:54xx`
  (main's `TALARIA_RUST_API_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5274` survived the copy and
  `talaria dev` derives the url only when nothing names it), and
  `POST /api/fleet/render` 500'd with `fleet chassis missing` because only
  `talaria setup` seeded `fleet/chassis.yml`. Both lines of code had landed on
  `rc` before this (`da23c0bb`, `ec3b0865`); what had not was the guard against
  the next one, a test for the chassis seed, and the docs.

  The strip-list is now derived from what the generated block writes
  (`WORKTREE_ENV_KEYS`, with `stripOwnKeys`) rather than kept by hand, and a
  test asserts the two sets are equal — a key appended to the block but missing
  from the filter is the exact shape of both earlier bugs. That closed a real
  third instance: a devbox's `ui/.env` carries `TALARIA_GATEWAY_SELF_URL` and
  `TALARIA_FLEET_PROJECT`, so a worktree cut from inside a box inherited them
  and its agents would have called back to the box's app under the box's fleet
  project. The fleet seed is `seedFleetPlane`, tested on its own: seeds the
  chassis from `scripts/chassis.template.yml` and says so, keeps an existing one
  (user-owned config) and says so, and warns rather than silently skips when
  the template is missing — a silent skip reproduces the 500 this step exists
  to prevent. `docs/WORKTREES.md`'s step list names every key the env rewrites
  and the fleet plane step.

  Verified: `cd cli && bun test` — 13 in `worktree.test.ts`, whole suite green;
  removing one key from `WORKTREE_ENV_KEYS` fails two tests (the set-equality
  guard and the devbox-fixture strip); `bun run check` clean.

- **Changed:** A repo's project env store reached the sandbox as plaintext files on the host — every granted repo's values unsealed into `fleet/agents/<slug>/workbench-env/<owner>/<name>.env` (0644) by the fleet render and mounted read-only into the agent's container for its whole life — so a job on one repo could read every other granted repo's env, and `docs/ENCRYPTION.md`'s "never in config files" was not true of them. The render no longer writes that directory or mounts it (an existing one is removed on the next render).
