Instead `prepare_env` — the step the agent runs on its fresh checkout — writes only the job's own repo env to `<workdir>/.talaria/env` (as the agent, 0600, through the exec's stdin, never a shell line) and answers with `projectEnv` (path, count, the `set -a; . …; set +a` line that loads it); `start_job` writes nothing, because a file in the workdir would make `git clone <url> <workdir>` refuse a non-empty directory, and its rules tell the agent where the env will land. `finish_job`, abandon and the sweep remove it with the job's processes, and a resumed job gets it again from its next `prepare_env`. A checkout at the workdir root gets `.talaria/env` added to `.git/info/exclude`. The work-session brief points at the new path. Values stay sealed at rest exactly as before. Verified: the write script runs in a test against a scratch workdir — the file lands at 0600 with no temp file left, a rewrite over a root checkout excludes it from git exactly once, and the remove script clears it idempotently; `talaria-workbench-mcp`, `talaria-fleet-render`, `talaria-fleet-docker` and `talaria-runs-work-session` fmt, clippy `--tests -D warnings` and tests green; `bun run check`.

- **Changed:** A work session's files come from the API, opening one creates nothing, and the agent is told which file is open. New `GET /api/conversations/{id}/files` (same gate as the conversation, 404 otherwise) answers `{ kind, files }`: every Talaria document and every Google file a chip on the session's messages names, in order of first appearance with `lastTouchedAt` the newest message naming it, then the session's `pinned_files`, then a legacy work session's living document. Artifacts the caller cannot read (the artifact GET's own check) or that were deleted are left out, and the list stops at 100. The derivation is pure, in `talaria_chips::session_files`, beside a Rust port of `parseGoogleFileUrl` (Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive `/file/d/` and `open?id=`). Google tools now leave a chip naming the file they worked on (`create_google_doc`, the Docs, Sheets and Slides reads and writes, `read_drive_file`; a source pill at the file's canonical URL), and `import_drive_file` leaves a document chip, so the files a session touched in Google are in its list too. `GET /api/conversations/{id}/doc` on a work session never creates: it answers a legacy session's existing document, else 404 "this session has no plan document"; `POST` there is a 409. A work turn no longer triggers the post-turn document rewrite (`plan_meta` is built for plans only). `/api/chat` takes an optional `focus: { kind: 'artifact' | 'google', id, title? }`, and every work turn carries one system line after the work-mode prompt naming the open file (title stripped of control characters and line breaks, capped at 300 UTF-16 units, quoted) or saying nothing is open and to create a file when asked. `WORK_MODE_PROMPT`'s first paragraph now describes the files pane, names `create_document` / `create_sheet` / `create_page` / `create_google_doc`, and says there is no separate plan document; the `hermes:work` harness renders the same focus line the product sends. A queued or auto-resumed work turn carries the same two lines the live one computed (`TurnMeta.work_prompts`); before, a chained work turn ran with the plan prompt, and with none once plans stopped being built for work. Plan sessions are unchanged. Verified: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --tests -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` for `talaria-work-mode` (13), `talaria-chips` (61, with the URL parser, the session-files derivation and the Google chips), `talaria-conversations`, `talaria-artifacts`, `talaria-routes-boards`, `talaria-routes-comms`, `talaria-harness-defs` (442), `talaria-api-routes` and `talaria-chat-persist`; `bun run docs:api`; `bun run check`. Exercised against the worktree's api on :5403 with a real artifact made through `POST /api/artifacts`. The files list came back in first-appearance order with the row's title over the chip's. A re-mention moved `lastTouchedAt` and not the position, a docs.google.com source chip came back as `googleType: "document"` at its canonical URL, someone else's private document was left out, the pins followed, and a linked legacy document came last as `living`. `/doc` answered 404 then 409 on the work session, 200 with the legacy document once linked, and created nothing. A plan session still found-or-created its document. A bad `focus` was a 400. Two mock-gateway work turns recorded prompt sizes 62 tokens apart, exactly the focus-line difference. Not exercised with a live agent.

- **Fixed:** `POST /api/research`'s duplicate-question check ran over every queued or running run in the org and answered 409 with the other run's id — so a caller learned that someone else was researching the same question, and where. The check is now scoped to the runs the caller may read, through the same viewer rule the list route and `research_role` use (a person: their own, shared and org runs; an agent: its owner's, so a general agent sees org runs only). A stranger's in-flight question is neither detected nor disclosed. Verified: `cargo clippy -p talaria-research -p talaria-routes-workbench --tests -- -D warnings` clean; `bun run check`.

- **Fixed:** An agent's tool-event frames (the talaria-events plugin's `POST /api/agents/tool-events`) were attributed to the agent's NEWEST live work session, so with two sessions on one agent — or a session and a chat — the thrash brake could abort the wrong run and the two transcripts mixed (audit 05-F13.3, left open in #559). A work-session turn is now sent as a Hermes SESSION turn keyed by its run id (`session_for_turn` → the harness transport's `PersonaSession`, through `proxy_session_turn`): created on turn 1, resumed on every later turn of the same run, and a session the container has lost falls back to the full-prompt completion for that turn the way a pinned chat does. The plugin's `sessionId` is therefore the run id, and the tool-events door resolves it exactly through `live_work_session_for` — a chat conversation's id lands nowhere — falling back to the newest-session read only for a frame that names no minted key. The workbench MCP `wtool` line, where no plugin reports and no session id arrives, is keyed by the ticket the call names (`taskId`, or a `jobId`'s ticket) and takes the newest session only when the call names none. The liveness tap and the `run-watch:{run}` thrash watcher read the same channel as before; the retire-on-reclaim and interrupted-turn settle logic is untouched. A session turn refuses by name any request field its body cannot carry (`temperature`, `response_format`, `tools: none`) rather than dropping it. Verified: `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --tests -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` for `talaria-harness`, `talaria-runs-work-session`, `talaria-routes-fleet`, `talaria-workbench-mcp` and `talaria-gateway`, with new tests for the session-keyed turn (`a_turn_keys_the_persona_session_by_its_run_and_resumes_after_the_first`), the non-key short-circuit, the frame's named-session read and the session-arm request mapping; `bun run check`. Not exercised against a live Hermes.

- **Changed:** A work session's pane shows the session's files, not a plan document. Every Talaria document, sheet or page and every Google file the agent creates or opens in the session is a tab, read from `GET /api/conversations/{id}/files` and re-read on every landed turn and every finished write tool (the Google writers included); a file that is new, or that a newer message touched again, opens and takes the pane, newest touch first. A session opens on the tab you were reading last time, else the file touched most recently, else the first. Opening a session creates nothing: no "Document" tab that would not close, no "Plan document" row, no Sync from chat, no Auto-saves label. Each file has one header row for every type (type label, title, Read/Edit, comments, Open ↗, fullscreen, More, close): the artifact editor's own toolbar folds into it, with share and official moved into More, and a Google file embeds without a second title row. Closing a tab hides that file for you in that session until the agent touches it again, or until you reopen it from "All files (N)" at the end of the strip. An empty session says "Nothing open yet" and offers New document and Open a Google file, and a pasted Google link is now appended to the session's pinned files instead of replacing them. The open file goes out with every work turn as the chat body's `focus`, so "this doc" names the file in front of you. The header loses the zero-state plan template picker; Research, Export, Schedule and Draft tickets sit in one quiet icon-and-label group, Rename, Archive and Delete move behind a `⋯` menu, and the narrow-screen toggle reads Chat / Files. Plan sessions keep their living document, now headed "Plan", with Sync from chat, comments, and Draft tickets as the gold primary. Verified: `cd ui && bun run typecheck` (0 errors, 0 warnings); `bunx vitest run src/lib/session-files.test.ts src/lib/workspace-tabs.test.ts src/lib/chat.test.ts` (the focus rule, new and re-touched detection between two reads, a closed file coming back on a re-touch, the bounded hidden-files key, the wire parse, appending a pin, every tab closing, seeding that never moves the reader, remembered over seeded focus over first, an agent touch winning, `focus` in the streamed and queued bodies), then the whole suite (119 files, 1874 tests); a client `vite build`; `bun run check`, whose only failure is the `docs/api` drift for the files and doc routes that the API half of this change regenerates. Driven in Chromium against the worktree stack at 1440×900 and 390×844, with a session whose messages name a Talaria doc, a sheet and a Google Doc, an empty session, a legacy work session carrying an old "Plan —" document, and a plan. The tabs came up in server order with the newest-touched sheet active and fully in view (the strip now slides to the active tab). Selecting the doc and wheeling over it scrolled the editor's own box with the page at 0. Closing the Google tab kept it closed across a reload with "All files (3)" still listing it. A new message naming the Google Doc brought its tab back. New document on the empty session opened "Untitled document" and the files route listed it as pinned. The legacy session showed its old document as a plain file with no Sync from chat. No console errors.

- **Fixed:** `message_user`'s daily cap was per agent↔person pair, so a general agent could DM every person in the org three times a day, and the count-then-insert let concurrent calls overshoot the cap they did see. There is now a per-agent daily total as well (`dailyDmTotalCap`, default 20, beside `dailyDmCap` in Admin → Outreach and `GET/PUT /api/admin/outreach`; a PUT without it keeps the stored value), and the slot is claimed before the message exists: both counts and the claiming insert run in one transaction under an advisory lock keyed on the agent, so concurrent calls serialize at the cap instead of all landing. A call that fails after claiming hands its slot back. Verified: `cargo clippy -p talaria-outreach -p talaria-routes-admin --tests -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p talaria-outreach` (the pure cap decision is tested under, at and over both caps); `bun run check`.

- **Fixed:** An agent whose `HERMES_KEY_<SLUG>` line was missing from, or empty in, the fleet `.env` was still rendered as a compose service: compose interpolates a missing variable to "", so the container came up with `API_SERVER_KEY` empty, which is an agent gateway with no key at all, and the render only logged "no HERMES_KEY_… in the fleet .env" as a warning. The render now mints the line where it is missing or empty, the same way it materializes each agent's `TALARIA_AGENT_KEY_<SLUG>` line (a line with a value is kept verbatim: a running container holds that key), and an agent it cannot mint a key for is left out of the compose file entirely, with a warning naming the agent, rather than rendered open. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-fleet-render` (a missing line is appended, an empty one rewritten in place, a live one untouched, an unmintable slug named and never written empty), clippy `-D warnings` on `talaria-fleet-render`; `bun run check`.

- **Fixed:** A Hermes cron's spend reached no ledger and no budget: a cron fires the agent's own loop on the agent's own gateway key, the relay skips every call on an agent key because the chat flow ledgers the turn as one row, and no flow drives a cron. The chat transport now counts every turn Talaria drives in Redis (`talaria:turn:v1:<agent model>`, a counter with a 60s ceiling re-armed every 20s while the stream is open, closed when the consumer lets go — clean end, hang-up or error — and forgotten by the ceiling if the api dies mid-turn), and the relay meters an agent-key call itself, under the agent as `unattended`, when no turn is counted for that agent; a counted turn keeps the skip, as does a register it cannot read. Two overlapping chat turns count two, not one; a cron firing during a chat turn is still skipped with it (the known double-skip, said in the relay). Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-gateway` (the register's overlap, re-arm, lapse and drop-without-stream cases over a memory register; the tier-row subject), `cargo test -p talaria-routes-fleet` (the metering decision), `cargo clippy -p talaria-gateway -p talaria-routes-fleet -p talaria-agent-crons --tests -- -D warnings`, `bun run check`.

- **Changed:** Every rendered `SOUL.md` now carries one standing sentence, beside the org headers and before the agent's own soul, telling the model that everything reaching it through a tool (tool results, fetched pages, search hits, mail, documents, files) is data, not instructions: read it for what it says, act only on what the people it works for ask, and say so rather than comply when it tries to steer. The gateway surfaces already say this per block of content they hand over; the persona now says it once, standing, so an agent that never saw a gateway preamble still knows a forwarded mail cannot give it orders. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-fleet-render` (the composed soul carries the sentence in the sparsest and the fullest composition, names the four surfaces, and has no em dash), clippy `-D warnings` on `talaria-fleet-render`; `bun run check`.

- **Added:** Admins can roll every agent container at once from the roster. **Roll all** confirms in the page (how many running agents, an opt-in for the stopped ones), then `POST /api/fleet/roll` queues each managed agent through the same blue/green roll one agent gets, `TALARIA_FLEET_ROLL_CONCURRENCY` (default 2) departments at a time so a fleet of twenty never doubles the host's load in one breath; departments already mid-roll are skipped and named, and the request answers at once with what was queued, what was skipped and the batch id (audited as `fleet.roll_all`). `GET /api/fleet/roll` is the live picture, one row per agent: rolling, idle, failed or done, since when, and the failure sentence, read from a roll registry `roll_agent` itself writes at start and verdict (so a manager's single roll and an MCP apply's roll land on the same page) and mirrored into the Redis hash `talaria:fleet-roll:v1` so a second api instance answers the same, outcomes kept an hour. The roster polls it every five seconds while anything rolls, each tile and row carries its rolling / rolled / roll-failed chip with the sentence, the strip above the roster keeps the batch's tally and every failure, and an agent's own Roll control is disabled while its department rolls. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-fleet-reconcile` (registry start/verdict, pruning, cross-instance merge), clippy `-D warnings` on `talaria-fleet-reconcile`, `talaria-routes-fleet` and `talaria-api-routes`; `bun run typecheck` in `ui/`; `bun run docs:api` regenerated the fleet reference; `bun run check`.

- **Added:** **Rotate credential** at the bottom of an agent's Summary tab, for its managers and admins: the console surface for `POST /api/fleet/defs/{id}/rotate-key`. The trigger is a quiet danger link; the deliberate step is an in-place confirm whose copy is checked against what the route does: the old key stops working the moment you confirm (no undo, no grace period); the fleet is re-rendered and a managed agent's container is rolled onto the new key, with the old container locked out until the roll's new container is healthy, so a toolkit call or a workbench session in flight on the old key fails and has to be retried while conversations carry on in the new container; an agent Talaria does not run gets the new key the next time it starts; the audit trail records who rotated which key, never the value; a failed roll leaves the agent on the dead key, and the confirm says how to recover (roll it again, or stop and start it). The result and any failure land in the same place rather than a toast, and the new secret is never shown. `docs/AGENT-KEY-MIGRATION.md` no longer says the route is the only surface. Verified: `bun run typecheck`; the route read end to end (`fleet_defs_id_rotate_key.rs`) against every sentence of the confirm; `bun run check`.

- **Fixed:** The code-probe integration test that failed rc's api job at `99e10098` stops racing two correct outcomes. Its spin case (`while (true) {}` under a 200 ms budget) pinned the timer's sentence, but boa's ten-million-iteration loop ceiling can end an empty loop inside 200 ms on a fast runner, so the run ended on the loop limit and the assertion failed on a tree that passed everywhere else. The test now accepts either sentence; both are the child process ending the spin, which is what it proves. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-api --test it code_probe_child` passing locally on three consecutive runs before the change (the race does not reproduce on this host), and after it.

- **Fixed:** A long document in the session pane scrolls again, and an agent turn no longer throws you back to the top of it. `LivingDoc`'s root had no height, so the editor's scroll box had nothing to scroll within and a long plan ran off the bottom of the pane. The root now carries the height chain (`flex h-full min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col`), and the editor owns the one scroll box under its own toolbar instead of sitting inside a second one. A sync from chat used to remount the editor after every turn; it now remounts only when the body that comes back differs from the one the editor is showing, and when it does it puts the scroll position back. In a work session the artifact editor, the Google frame, the report, the drafts panel, the comments and the empty state each sit in a bounded flex column with their own scroll box, and a finished write tool refreshes the artifact rather than remounting it, so your reading position stays put. Verified: `cd ui && bun run typecheck`; the height chain read through from the stage to every scroll container in the pane; a client `vite build`. In Chromium against the worktree stack: a 40-section plan, a work-session doc and a legacy document each scrolled inside the pane with the page itself at 0. With the plan scrolled to 2400px, Sync from chat with an unchanged body and then with a rewritten one (the rewrite stood in for by a body PUT, since that stack had no model) left the reader at 2400px both times, the second showing the new text.

- **Fixed:** Four low-severity gateway findings from the 2026-10-20 audit. The one place an upstream body reaches a log line (`talaria-error`'s `log_upstream_error`, which the MCP gateway's relay, its notification stream and the LLM relay all go through) now scrubs it before the 500-char cap: `Bearer <token>`, `tlk_`/`tak_`/`sk-`-shaped keys, `"access_token": "…"`-style JSON fields (and `refresh_token`, `client_secret`, `api_key`, `authorization`, `password`, …) and `x-api-key: …`-style header echoes each become a `[redacted]` marker that keeps the prefix or the key name, so a 4xx that quotes the credential it refused no longer puts that credential in the log. The gateway binds an upstream session to the agent it was minted for: the `mcp-session-id` an `initialize` answer carries is recorded against the caller (Redis, `talaria:mcp-session:v1:<server>:<sid>`, 24 h, refreshed on use) and a later request presenting a session recorded for another agent is refused with JSON-RPC `-32602` ("this session belongs to another agent"; 403 on the GET stream) instead of relayed — before, the caller's session header was forwarded as-is, so two agents sharing an org credential could present each other's sessions; a session the gateway never saw passes through, and Redis out of reach fails open with a log line like every Redis-backed gate here. Every tool catalog an upstream answers is bounded before it is cached, on every path (hosted, package, Workbench): a tool name is capped at 200 UTF-16 units and an entry whose name is empty, missing or over the cap is dropped, a description is clipped to 300, and an `inputSchema` over 32 KiB is replaced by the permissive object schema plus `inputSchemaTruncated: true` — before, the package path stored names, descriptions and schemas at whatever size the upstream chose. The health pass's drift sentence names at most the first twenty tools a side and says "and N more". OAuth discovery refuses an endpoint that is not `https://` (token, registration, authorization, and the metadata documents on the way to them) with a sentence naming it, even on the server's own domain, except a loopback host admitted by name through `TALARIA_FETCH_ALLOW_HOSTS` (the e2e stub's `127.0.0.1`; the suite's stub serves https regardless). Verified: `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --tests -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` for `talaria-error` (the scrubber on a JWT bearer, an OAuth token document, a Talaria key in prose, an OpenAI key in a provider's sentence, a header echo, an escaped quote, a body cut mid-token, and a set of plain bodies — a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge, a provider's prose, multi-byte text — that must pass untouched), `talaria-routes-fleet` (`mcp_gw_server`: the pure binding rule and the refusal's framing), `talaria-mcp` (the catalog bound's drop/clip/mark set and the twenty-name drift line), `talaria-mcp-oauth` (plain http refused on-domain, every loopback spelling admitted, a LAN host admitted by the guard still refused); `bun run check`.

- **Fixed:** The omapak submission fails before it does any work when its token cannot push, and the error says what to regenerate. `desktop-v0.11.0` reached the store step and died at the push with `Permission to outcrop-labs/omapak.git denied to <account>` — the clone succeeds because the repo is public, so the only sentence was GitHub's, which names the account and not the token. The job now asks GitHub what `OMAPAK_SUBMIT_TOKEN` may do first and fails with the exact PAT shape to regenerate (repository access listing `outcrop-labs/omapak`, Contents and Pull requests read and write) and the `gh secret set` line. Verified: `bash -n` on the step; the live run that motivated it is actions run 39545506268 — the fix for that release is the secret, re-run by dispatch with the tag once it is regenerated.

- **Fixed:** `prepare_env`'s repo scan ran as root inside the sandbox over files the agent controls, following symlinks: a `.talaria/workbench.toml` (or any marker, or a directory on a marker's path) symlinked at a root-only file handed its first 8 KiB back to the agent in the scan's output. The scan now runs as the sandbox's own user (`docker exec -u hermes`, the way the browser setup already does), reads only plain files whose real path is inside the checkout, reports every symlink or escape under `skipped` instead of opening it, and skips a symlinked directory when looking for the checkout. `apt-get` still runs as root, and still only after the scan has read the file as the agent and every package name has passed validation. Verified: the scan script runs in a test against a scratch checkout with a marker symlinked outside, a symlinked directory on a marker's path, a dangling symlink, a symlinked in-checkout alias and a symlinked sibling directory — the real files are read, the alias is followed, the three escapes are listed as skipped and not one byte of the outside files comes back; `talaria-workbench-mcp` and `talaria-fleet-docker` fmt, clippy `--tests -D warnings` and tests green; `bun run check`.

- **Changed:** `docs/WORKBENCH.md` now says what the audit found unsaid: code running in a Developer Agent's sandbox can read the attached coding account's access token, or an API-key account's key itself, through the broker; the refresh token never leaves the api; an API key is therefore a long-lived secret the sandbox can exfiltrate, so attach only keys you can rotate. Every snapshot read of an account's credential (`GET /api/workbench/auth/v1/snapshot`) now writes an audit row — `coding.snapshot_read`, actor `agent:<model>`, target the account id, the provider and agent id and no credential value — rated in memory to one row per account per ten minutes so omp's long poll does not flood the log. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-routes-workbench` (the first read is logged, a poll inside the window is not, a full interval later is, and the claim is per account); clippy `-D warnings` on `talaria-routes-workbench`; `bun run check`.

- **Added:** The org-wide toolset floor is now an admin setting with an editor, not a row set by SQL. `PUT /api/admin/settings` takes `mandatoryDisabledToolsets`, a list of governed Hermes toolset names: trimmed, deduped and sorted on the way in, `todo` and `clarify` implied and never stored, and a name outside the governed vocabulary refused with a 400 that names every stranger in the list (`unknown toolsets "brower", "discord"`), not just the first. The GET answers the stored floor beside `toolsets` (the governed names, the builtin pair, and anything `TALARIA_MANDATORY_DISABLED_TOOLSETS` pins), so the panel cannot offer a name the write would refuse. The write audits as `settings.toolset_floor` with before and after, and rolls nothing: the renderer reads the key on every render, so the floor lands on each agent at its next render or roll, which is what the panel says when it saves. The editor is **Admin → Security → Agent toolsets**: the agent editor's own grid over the whole fleet, the builtin pair and the env-pinned names locked with their reason. `GET /api/fleet/defs` now answers `toolsets.mandatoryDisabled` as the whole floor (the pair plus the org floor) and adds `toolsets.orgDisabled` for the org part alone, so the agent toolset editor locks an org-closed row with "closed org-wide by an admin" rather than the pair's reason; an org-closed name a manager had stored stays stored, so lifting the floor later gives each agent back exactly what its managers chose. `docs/user/admin-agents.md` describes the toolset grid and the floor. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-routes-admin --lib admin_settings` (the stored spelling, every stranger named, the body grammar, the vocabulary); `cargo test -p talaria-routes-fleet --lib fleet_defs` (the floor rides whole and the org part alone); `cargo clippy -p talaria-routes-admin -p talaria-routes-fleet --tests -- -D warnings`; `bunx vitest run src/components/fleet/toolsets.test.ts` (an org-closed row is locked with its own reason; `builtinFloor` keeps an org-closed name in the stored list); `bun run typecheck`; `bun run docs:api`; `bun run check`.

- **Fixed:** A Developer Agent's coding harness no longer fails to start with `env: 'bun': No such file or directory`. Oh My Pi is a bun program (`#!/usr/bin/env bun`), the agent image ships no bun, and the only step that installed one was `prepare_env` after a clone — which also reached the PATH only through a login shell's profile. So a fresh agent's `doctor`, and any command its terminal ran as a plain `bash -c` (Hermes's default), found no bun at all, and agents correctly refused to start jobs. The workbench now provisions the harness's runtime itself, idempotently and as the agent's user, before `doctor`, `start_job` or `prepare_env` hands the harness out: mise onto the volume if it is missing, bun `1.4.0` pinned and installed, and `bun` linked into `/opt/data/.local/bin`, which the container's own `PATH` carries. The doctor reports the runtime and probes the harness from a non-login shell; the boot hook also links an already-installed bun, so a rolled container has it before its first call. Verified: the bootstrap run in a throwaway `nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest` container on an empty volume — before, a non-login shell had no `bun`; after, `bun --version` answers `1.4.0`, a rerun is a no-op, and the harness probe `npx -y @oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent@latest --version` answers `omp/18.8.3` from a non-login shell; the failure itself reproduced read-only in the live engineering agent's container (`sh -c 'command -v bun'` → nothing; `bun` there is an unpinned mise shim). `cargo clippy --tests -D warnings` and `cargo test` for `talaria-workbench-harnesses`, `talaria-workbench-mcp`, `talaria-fleet-render`.

- **Changed:** A personal assistant used to read and post in its owner's human↔human direct messages as part of the owner's view, with no way to say otherwise. Settings → Assistant now has **Your DMs** — **None**, **Read**, or **Read & post** — stored per owner (it outlives the assistant's handle, model and container) and honoured at both doors: the assistant's channel listing leaves DMs out at None, and the access predicate (`agent_may_access_channel`, which now takes the intent) refuses a read below Read and a post or reaction below Read & post. Channels and relays follow the owner's membership as before. The default is **Read & post**, so nothing changes for an existing owner until they choose. `GET/PATCH /api/me/assistant` carry it as `dmAccess` (`none` | `read` | `read-write`); a patch that carries only it lands without a new agent version or a restart. Verified: `cargo clippy -p talaria-users -p talaria-channels -p talaria-routes-comms -p talaria-routes-integrations --tests -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p talaria-users -p talaria-channels` (the three-way predicate is unit-tested at every kind × intent); `cd ui && bun run typecheck`; `bun run check`.

- **A revise round keeps its pull request, repos are created on the org's own GitHub App installation, and an agent learns what happened to its repo requests.** When a reviewer bounced a ticket, `start_job` minted a second job on the same branch, and `finish_job` asked GitHub for a second PR for that branch, threw on the refusal and left the job `started`. Now `start_job` resumes the job whose PR is still open (same row, branch and workdir), and `finish_job` keeps any open PR for the branch: it records the PR number, posts the summary on the PR, and the ticket reads `workbench PR updated`. Abandoning a resumed round puts the job back on its PR. `create_repo` asks GitHub which installation owns the org (`GET /orgs/{org}/installation`) instead of guessing from a repo cache. An org the App is not on, or an installation the admin did not select, is refused with what to fix. `doctor` now reports `repoCreation` (the approved orgs and whether creation can work here). `request_repo` is refused up front outside App mode, for an org off the list, or for an org the App is not installed on. A request records the agent's responsible user, a `visibility` (private by default, and the approver can change it) and an optional app slug. A rejection's note goes on the requesting ticket, and `list_repos` returns the agent's requests with their outcomes. A new read-only `pr_status` tool reports a job's PR state, each check's conclusion with one verdict, and the review decision. It never merges or comments. Verified:
  - `cargo test -p talaria-github`: 19 pass. Twelve of them run the flows against a loopback GitHub stub: an open PR reused with no second `POST /pulls`; a branch with no PR getting one; GitHub's 422 "already exists" race resolving to the existing PR; `create_repo` minting on the org's installation (90002) and never touching the first one (90001), refusing a 404 org and an unselected installation, and posting `private: true` by default; `pr_status` making only GETs, reading a failing check and a change request, and naming a missing Checks permission.
  - `cargo test -p talaria-workbench-mcp`: 48 pass. The ignored live-DB test passed against a fresh postgres 16 with the full migration replay, driving the verbs through `call_tool` with a stub GitHub. `finish_job` kept PR #41 and stored its number. The pr_open job resumed once and never twice. `pr_status` read checks passing and changes requested. Abandon returned the job to `pr_open`. `request_repo` was refused in PAT mode, for an unlisted org, for a bad visibility or slug, and for an org whose installation answered 404. A public request for app `notes` was filed. `list_repos` showed its rejection note.
  - `cargo test -p talaria-routes-workbench`: 22 pass. Clippy with `-D warnings` is clean on all three crates. `bun run gate` passed: check, svelte-check (0 errors, 0 warnings), the ui suite (1880 tests) and the three api packages.
  - On the worktree stack, through the real MCP gateway as a Developer Agent: `doctor` answered `repoCreation` for PAT mode (possible false, with the reason) and for App mode (possible true, orgs `["acme"]`). `request_repo` gave the off, incomplete-App, unlisted-org, visibility and app-slug refusals. Two requests against ticket PLG-1 were filed, one public for app `notes` and one private whose responsible user was the hiring admin. `tools/list` lists `pr_status`. `pr_status` refused a job with no PR, and `job_status` read `prNumber` 17 off a pre-column PR URL. Migrations reached 464 and the schema snapshot was regenerated on postgres 16.
  - In Chromium at 1440×900 as the admin, Admin → Org showed both requests with their visibility, the `app notes` chip and the PAT-mode warning. The GitHub status was the one intercepted answer, because its real form calls api.github.com. Approving the private request as public sent `visibility: "public"` and showed the api's "requires the GitHub App connection" refusal. Rejecting with a reason removed the request, wrote `rejected the new repo acme/talaria-app-notes that wbdev-engineering asked for: Use the existing acme/wiki repo for notes` on PLG-1, and `list_repos` returned that note. At 390×844 the request row wraps and nothing scrolls sideways.

- **Fixed:** Agent crons are driven through Hermes's own cron REST (`/api/jobs` on the agent's API server, the chat door and bearer) instead of `docker exec hermes cron` and a `jobs.json` read, so "Run now" stops reporting false failures and the admin frequency floor can no longer be slipped past. Since Hermes v0.22 the CLI's `run` executes the whole turn on the caller's thread, so any run longer than the exec's 30s bound came back as an error while the run carried on; REST `run` marks the job due for the next tick (≤60s) and answers at once. The floor used to read the schedule with a grammar of its own and allow anything it could not parse, which let `every minute` (Hermes's bare-unit interval), croniter's `0/1` and any 6-field cron through. Now a job is written paused, the floor judges the schedule Hermes parsed, and only then does the job start; any shape it cannot read is refused. A schedule edit pauses an armed job, patches it, judges it and resumes it, and a refused edit puts every changed field back. A create or schedule edit runs its calls on the agent to the end in its own task, so a client that hangs up partway cannot leave the job stranded paused. The edit form now sends only the fields that changed, so a rename never re-times a schedule and a job whose prompt was written longer than the cap below (the CLI had none) can still be renamed or rescheduled; an API client that sends the schedule back unchanged does not re-parse or re-time it either. The floor also reads the hour field now, so a floor above an hour stops refusing a daily cron. "Run now" on a paused job is refused, because Hermes's `run` would resume it for good (an archived thread's schedules are paused so they stop spending), and the Run button is disabled on paused rows. Prompts are capped at 5,000 characters, Hermes's own REST limit, at every cron door and in the forms. The list asks for `include_disabled=true`, so paused jobs still show. `talaria-gateway` gains `fleet_chat::agent_request`, one json call on an agent's own door, and `talaria-agent-crons` no longer depends on the docker socket. Verified: `bun run gate`, re-run after review (check, ui typecheck and 1887 ui tests, including the edit form's changed-fields-only patch, and clippy and `cargo test` for `talaria-agent-crons`, `talaria-fleet-docker`, `talaria-gateway`, `talaria-routes-fleet` and `talaria-routes-comms`; the crons crate's new tests cover every schedule shape Hermes stores, the `N/STEP` and 6-field cases, the hour-aware gap, the refusal sentences and the job-id grammar); the workspace compile and test is CI's. End to end in the worktree stack on a `nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.22.4@sha256:7a6920…` agent, a scripted run of 35 checks, all passing, each one read back from Hermes's own `/api/jobs`. `every minute`, `minute`, `0/1 * * * *`, `* * * * * *`, `*/2 * * * *`, `every 0m` and `every 4m` were refused with nothing left behind in Hermes. Create, both lists, edit, a refused edit restored with the job still armed, an unchanged-schedule rename that kept `next_run_at`, pause, resume, delete and a malformed id all behaved as described. Run-now answered in 49 ms and the scheduler claimed the job on its next tick 44 s later. Run-now on a paused job was refused and the job stayed paused. The conversation door was checked too: a refused schedule, a create, the merged live list, archive pausing, restore resuming and unschedule. With a 120-minute floor an hourly cron was refused and a daily one passed; with the floor at 0 a 1-minute job was accepted and edited. A stopped container came back as the per-agent error on the fleet list. Before and after on the same agent, with a model upstream that never answers: rc's `docker exec … hermes cron run` was killed by the 30 s bound while the CLI run kept going inside the container, and the new run-now returned 200 in 0.13 s. After review the stack was rebuilt and the same 35 checks passed again. Fifty hang-ups partway through a request (30 refused edits and 20 creates, the socket closed 2–56 ms in, most before the api answered) left no job paused or half-edited in Hermes. A job written through the CLI with a 5,999-character prompt was renamed through the real edit form: the form sent only `{"name"}`, Hermes kept the prompt, the schedule and `next_run_at`, and the old form's three-field body on the same job is refused with a 400. The `/api/jobs` surface this relies on (the routes, `include_disabled`, `paused` on create, the 12-hex id, the 5,000 cap, `run` marking the job due) was read in both the v0.22.4 source and the host's cached `:latest` (v0.21.4, revision 7ce19044), and is the same in both. The model call itself was not exercised, because the stack had no working LLM endpoint.

- **Fixed:** **an agent whose model cannot see now reads images, through Hermes' own vision path, and Talaria's `describe_image` tool is gone.** Every fleet agent runs `provider: custom` with a gateway model id that Hermes' catalog does not know, so Hermes had to guess at every agent's sight. It described each attached image with the agent's own model. Once a model was known to be blind it had no describer at all, because its fallback chain (OpenRouter, Nous, DeepInfra) has no key in a Talaria container. The render now writes Hermes' own keys from Talaria's capability facts, which come from a fitness run's vision probe, the provider catalog, or a declaration. Each model the agent runs on whose sight is known gets `model_overrides.custom.<id>.supports_vision`. When any of the agent's models is not known to see, the org's `vision` role model becomes its describer as `auxiliary.vision`. That spec is routed through the gateway and key-scoped like any other. An endpoint-qualified role renders by its bare id only when that id cannot land on an endpoint not known to see, and a bare role is refused when one of its endpoints is known blind. Hermes keeps one image mode per agent, and the render picks it from the main model: `native` (pixels) for a main model known to see, `text` (the describer first) for one that is not. So under a seeing main model, a turn on a tier or fallback that cannot see gets pixels too and does not read an attached image, though that model still has `vision_analyze`. What a def authored about any of these keys stands. A blind agent with no reader, or a role that cannot be rendered, is named in the render's warnings. Assigning or clearing the `vision` role re-renders the fleet. A new capability fact reaches agents at the next render, and a re-render reaches a running agent only once #574 (hx-rolls) lands; until then it lands on the agent's next start. With the render in place, the per-upload-id copy of that mechanism goes: the `describe_image` MCP tool, `POST /api/vision/describe`, the `talaria-vision` crate, the capability-platform refusal branch, the capability-reach vision supply, and the fitness mirror and sandbox handler. The Apps SDK's in-process `ui/src/server/vision.ts` stays. The `vision` role is now marked wired, with a hint that says what it does, and Models → Roles files it under its own "Agents' eyes" category instead of Reserved. It stays out of the fitness matrix, because no Talaria harness reaches it. The toolkit skill and `fetch_attachment`'s description no longer promise "an image you can see": a tool's image arrives as a `MEDIA:` path, which a blind agent reads with `vision_analyze`. Known gap: talaria-vision metered each description against the ledger as `vision:describe`. A describer call Hermes makes while a chat turn is open now goes unmetered, through the relay's open-turn skip, until hx-metering lands. Verified: `bun run gate` was green. It ran check, ui typecheck and tests, mcp typecheck, and fmt, clippy and tests for the eleven touched crates. New fleet-render tests cover each sight case, def-authored keys, the pool rule, and the describer's routing, key scope and YAML round trip. CI is the full-workspace proof line. Exercised on the worktree stack with the pinned `hermes-agent:v0.22.4@sha256:7a6920…` image and a Z.ai coding-plan endpoint. The main model was `glm-4.5-air`, which answers 400 code 1210 to an image part, and the vision role was `zai-coding/glm-4.6v`. The container's `/opt/data/config.yaml` carried the three keys. Hermes' own code, run in the container, resolved the main model as not seeing, chose `text` mode, picked `custom`/`glm-4.6v` at the gateway as the vision client, and exposed `vision_analyze`. A Talaria chat turn with an attached image was described by `glm-4.6v` and answered correctly ("MARMALADE", "blue"), with 0 gateway errors. Hermes' `vision_analyze` on a file path posted `model: glm-4.6v` to the gateway on the agent's key and read the word back. With the main model switched to `glm-4.6v` and a blind tier, the render gave `native` mode, Hermes chose native, and the image turn made no describer call. A blind main model with no role, and a role pooled with an endpoint not known to see, each rendered no describer and printed their warnings. Clearing the role through `PUT /api/admin/model-roles` re-rendered the agent's config with no describer and narrowed its key scope to `[glm-4.5-air]`, with no manual render. Assigning it again restored the describer, `text` mode and the `[glm-4.5-air, glm-4.6v]` scope. Before a restart the running container still held the previous file's inode, which is what #574 fixes; after `docker restart` it read the new render. A bare `glm-4.6v` role rendered while its endpoint was known to see, and was refused with the "known not to read images" warning once that fact was flipped to false. In the browser, Models → Roles showed the role under "Agents' eyes" with no reserved chip, and the Models → Fitness matrix drew the same 18 columns as before, with no vision column. Not exercised live: `fetch_attachment` itself, because this stack's MCP gateway proxied to another worktree's toolkit and got a 401; a tier turn, which waits on #568's `model_routes`; and a fitness run writing a `vision` fact, which is read from the code (the vision probe runs for gateway-served models). The exercise's vision facts were hand-declared `model_capabilities` rows, to set up each case.

- **Fixed:** Rolling a running agent works again, config edits reach a running agent without a roll, and every host runs the same pinned Hermes. Three things were wrong.
  - **Rolls of running agents could never succeed.** The blue/green roll started a second container on the agent's state volume while the first still ran. Every Hermes since v2026.4.30 holds an `flock` on `/opt/data/gateway.lock` in that volume, so the second gateway logged "Cannot reserve gateway profiles: Gateway runtime already owns profile /opt/data" on every s6 respawn and was discarded after about two minutes. Rotate-key therefore left the agent on a revoked key, and every MCP call it made returned 401 until someone stopped and started it by hand. The Developer switch, Roll and Roll all failed the same way. A roll now recreates the container in place (`compose up -d --force-recreate --no-deps`) and waits up to 180s for health. Slot-B rendering, port churn and the `-b` cutover are gone. An agent an old roll left in `agent-<dept>-b` moves back to `agent-<dept>` on its next roll. The home service's image is pulled while `-b` is still serving, so a failed pull puts the agent back on `-b` instead of leaving it with no container.
  - **Stops can now drain.** A plain `docker stop` never drains a Hermes agent, whatever the grace: s6-overlay revives the SIGTERMed gateway and KILLs everything 3s later. Every stop, restart, remove and roll now stops the gateway through s6 inside the container first (`s6-svc -d`, then `s6-svwait -D`), so Hermes holds cron and `/v1` runs open for up to its 30s drain floor before exiting. The render gives every service `stop_grace_period: 45s` as the outer bound, and nothing is retired with `docker rm -f` any more. A stop, restart or recreate that fails before it reaches the container brings the gateway back up (`s6-svc -u`), so a failed step never leaves an agent running without one.
  - **Config edits never reached a running agent.** Since 2026-10-20, `config.yaml` was replaced by an atomic rename under a single-file `:ro` bind, so the container kept reading the inode it started with. The render now rewrites `config.yaml` and `SOUL.md` in place (`write_in_place` in `talaria-fleet-brain`): same inode, under an `flock`, skipped when the bytes are unchanged, never truncated first, with the mtime bumped last so Hermes's stat-signature cache always sees the final write. The file ends in a YAML `...` document end, so the stale tail a shrinking rewrite briefly leaves is a parse error, and Hermes keeps serving its last good config through it. Because a written config is live at once, the render widens each agent's gateway scope to its old and new models before it writes any `config.yaml`, and narrows it to the new set afterwards. A model change therefore never meets a relay that refuses the id Hermes just switched to.
  - **The image floated.** `nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest` was never pulled, so each host ran whatever it had cached first. The chassis now pins `nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.22.4@sha256:7a69…a4cf`. A host's `fleet/chassis.yml` is copied once and never rewritten, so the render treats every stock default a template ever shipped (the old `:latest`, and from now on each past pin) as not chosen and renders the current pin. A pin bump appends to that list, so it reaches hosts seeded on an older pin too. An image an operator wrote stays theirs, and `HERMES_IMAGE` still overrides both. A host pulls a pin it lacks before any start or roll (`compose pull --policy missing`; a failed pull leaves the running container untouched). The workbench image builds `FROM` the same pin, and the chassis CI smoke pulls it. To bump the pin, see `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, "The fleet".
  - **`LLM_MODEL` is no longer provisioned.** Hermes ignores it (it reads its model from `config.yaml` alone), and a spec-less agent's gateway scope no longer falls back to it.

  Agents started before this change are still reading an orphaned `config.yaml` and need one roll. On an image install the post-deploy fleet roll does it. Checkout and dev installs never roll the fleet on upgrade: run **Roll all** (`POST /api/fleet/roll`) once after upgrading.

  Verified on the worktree stack against the pinned v0.22.4 image, with a Z.ai endpoint behind the gateway:
  - **Before (unmodified rc).** A roll of a healthy agent failed after about 2 minutes ("replacement never became healthy"). The incoming container's gateway log showed the profile-ownership error on every respawn. A render-only toolset edit changed the host's `config.yaml` (new inode, 716 bytes) while the container still read the old one (727 bytes), and Hermes's `GET /v1/toolsets` still listed the old set.
  - **Roll.** Done in 49s. The new container ran the pin rendered from a chassis with the legacy `:latest` line and no `HERMES_IMAGE`, with `StopTimeout=45`. Its `config.yaml` was the host's inode, and `/v1/toolsets` showed the edit.
  - **Edit without a roll.** Closing `file` and `image_gen` by render alone landed in the same running container (same id and start time). The file kept its inode, and `/v1/toolsets` dropped both at once. Reopening them shrank the file cleanly to `...\n`, and Hermes logged no parse error. A re-render with nothing changed left the mtime untouched.
  - **Key rotation.** The old key answered 401 at once. The roll finished in 23s, and the new container's `TALARIA_AGENT_KEY` matched `fleet/.env` and got 200 from `/api/agent/whoami`.
  - **Drain.** A plain `docker stop -t 45` took 3.9s and cut an in-flight `/v1/chat/completions` off. With the s6 drain, a roll started 4s into a 400-word turn finished the turn (200, the whole reply; Hermes logged `drain took 21.37s … api_at_start=1, api_now=0`), and the new container came up healthy. An idle stop took 4.9s and exited 0.
  - **Legacy slot.** An agent placed in a running `agent-rolls-b` container rolled home: `active_slot` went to `a`, `-b-1` was drained and removed, `-1` came up healthy on the same port, and chat answered.
  - **Legacy slot, failed pull.** With `HERMES_IMAGE` pointed at a tag that does not exist, a roll of an agent in a running `agent-rolls-b` failed in 3s with "could not pull the image for agent-rolls … not found". `active_slot` stayed `b`, and `-b-1` kept its container id and start time, stayed healthy with its gateway up, and answered chat. With the override removed, the next roll moved it home in 23s, healthy, and chat answered.
  - **Failed stop.** With `fleet/.env` unreadable, compose failed after the drain. The control-route stop answered an error, the container kept running, its gateway came back up within seconds, and chat answered. For contrast, a gateway drained the same way and left alone was still down 20s later (health unreachable) until `s6-svc -u`.
  - **Scope order.** A render-only model switch on a running agent (`glm-5.3-flash` to `glm-4.5-air`) was run with a trigger logging every write to the scope row. The widened row (both models) landed at 22.677s, the `config.yaml` mtime is 22.697s, and the narrowed row (`glm-4.5-air` alone) landed at 22.700s. The container was not restarted, and its next turn went upstream as `glm-4.5-air` (usage row).
  - **Roll after these fixes.** Done in 22s, with a new container id, healthy, and chat answered.
  - Unit tests cover every stock default ever shipped rendering the current pin, operator images staying theirs, and the widened scope row. No past pin exists yet, so a host seeded on one was not exercised live. `ui/src/server/chassis.test.ts` (10 tests) checks the pin, the workbench `FROM` and the grace. Not exercised: a real pull of a missing pin, because the image was already on the host. CI is the compile and test proof for the Rust crates. Locally, `bun run gate` passed: check, ui typecheck and tests, cli typecheck and tests, and `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings` and tests for the eleven touched api packages.

- **Added:** **Agents search the web with the provider the operator picks, through their own Hermes: one setting, Admin → Search → Agent web search, renders Hermes's `web:` backend and the vendor key into every agent, and once anything is chosen, Hermes's keyless public tiers stop catching agents' queries.** Hermes v0.22.4 picks its web backend from `web.search_backend` / `web.extract_backend` and reads each vendor's key from the environment. Talaria now writes both from one org setting (`agent_web_search`, new crate `talaria-agent-web-search`). The setting offers Tavily, Exa, Parallel, Firecrawl, Keenable, the Perplexity Search API, Brave Search, or SearXNG at the workspace search URL, each checked against `plugins/web/<vendor>/provider.py` (NAME, KEY_ENV, EXTRACT, KEYLESS), plus an optional separate provider for reading pages. Three registered v0.22.4 backends are left out: `ddgs` (the image does not ship the package), `xai` (a model call to x.ai outside the gateway), and `openai-native` (it needs the Codex Responses transport). The key is sealed into the setting row. Each render unseals it into `fleet/.env` as `TALARIA_WEB_<VAR>`, and the agent service interpolates it under the exact name the provider reads, so the value never appears in the compose file or config.yaml. Hermes's own provider env blocklist keeps it out of terminal and execute_code children. When a provider is picked, or the search URL is rendered into the agents as `SEARXNG_URL`, the render also sets `web.keyless_fallback: false` and `web.keyless_rescue: false`, unless the operator ticks **Allow Hermes's keyless public tiers**. Rendered is not reachable: nothing probes the URL from an agent, so a URL the agents cannot connect to still counts. Without the tick, a failing provider no longer falls through to the anonymous Exa, Parallel, Firecrawl or Keenable tiers. Left unset, nothing is rendered and Talaria recommends no vendor. Brave Search and SearXNG only search. With nothing picked for reading pages, Hermes's `web_extract` autodetect lands on them and every call fails with its typed "search-only backend" error, so the render warns about it. This is a warning, not a refusal, because SearXNG alone is a legitimate keyless setup. The same warning covers a search URL with nothing else picked, which already broke `web_extract` before this change. The org choice overrides an agent's own `web:` backend keys and any per-agent secret named like the vendor key. Admin → Search shows the render's own read-back: the `web:` keys, the env names and the warnings. The panel no longer restates the render's rules. Research does not read the setting: it keeps its own search stage on the search URL or a registered search MCP server, and the panel says so. `PUT /api/admin/search/agents` refuses a backend it does not offer, a search-only backend for page reading, a key for a vendor that is not picked, a key `.env` could not hold, a keyed vendor with no key (unless its anonymous tier is allowed), Perplexity or Brave with no key at all, and SearXNG with no search URL. Switching vendors drops the old key. The PUT reads, applies and writes under the setting row's lock, the same lock key rotation takes, so two saves at once cannot drop each other's keys. The write audits as `search.agents_configure`, recording vendor names only, and rolls nothing: the choice reaches each agent at its next roll. The key appears in the secrets inventory and is re-sealed by key rotation. Admin → Search is a new tab, and it also gives the existing search URL (`/api/admin/search`) the editor it never had. Verified on the worktree stack, with an agent on the pinned `nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.22.4@sha256:7a6920…` image. Nothing set: `/opt/data/config.yaml` had no `web:` block, the container env had no vendor key, and Hermes's own `_get_search_backend()` landed on its keyless ring. With Tavily and a test key saved: the container's config read `search_backend: tavily`, `keyless_fallback: false`, `keyless_rescue: false`, and its `TAVILY_API_KEY` equalled the saved key. Hermes resolved `tavily` with its keyless tier and rescue both off, and `web_search` reached `api.tavily.com` and returned Tavily's own `Unauthorized: missing or invalid API key.` with no rescue. A real chat turn on the agent's API server (LLM through the gateway) called `web_search`, Hermes logged `Web search via tavily`, and the agent quoted that error. With public tiers allowed, the same failed call was rescued through the keyless ring (`rescued_from: tavily`, three results), which is the fallthrough the default now prevents. A search URL alone rendered `SEARXNG_URL` plus the two keyless switches, and Hermes resolved `searxng` with no rescue. SearXNG search with Firecrawl page reading rendered both keys, and Hermes resolved search to `searxng` and extract to `firecrawl`. Clearing the setting removed the `web:` block, the compose variable and the `.env` line. Every PUT refusal above was exercised. A key rotation re-sealed the key from v1 to v2, and the next render delivered the same value. A headless browser drove the panel: picking Tavily held it as a draft until its key was saved, then both landed together. The search-only case was then exercised in the same container. With Brave Search and its key, and nothing picked for reading pages, the render route returned the warning. Hermes's `_get_extract_backend()` resolved `brave-free`, and `web_extract` returned `Brave Search (Free) is a search-only backend and cannot extract URL content`. It did the same with the public tiers allowed. With Firecrawl picked for reading pages, the warning was gone and extract resolved to `firecrawl`. With a search URL alone, extract resolved to `searxng` and `web_extract` failed the same way. That includes the render with no `web:` block at all, which is exactly what agents got before this change. Admin → Search showed the render's summary and that warning. A PUT sent while a psql session held the setting row's lock (and changed the row) waited 6.7 s, then kept that change. A refused PUT left the row's `updated_at` untouched, and a refused first save left no row behind. `bun run gate` passed (check, ui typecheck and 1,887 tests, and fmt, clippy and tests for the seven touched api packages, including 17 new `talaria-agent-web-search` tests). `bun run docs:api` regenerated `docs/api/admin.md`. CI is the proof line for the full workspace, because `Cargo.lock` moved with the new crate. Running agents pick the setting up only on a recreate. A config-only change reaches a running container once hx-rolls (#574) lands, but the vendor key rides the container environment, so it always needs the roll.

- **Fixed:** An app scaffolded with `talaria app new` can be enabled from Manage → Apps again, in dev and in production, without anyone editing its build status or `app_settings` by hand. Five bugs stood in the way. (1) The app client build left Vite's `preserveEntrySignatures` at its default, so the built `app.js` had no default export. The production probe refused it ("app.js is not an ESM client bundle") and the host had no surfaces to mount. The build now keeps the entry's exports, and the probe asks for a default export rather than any `export`. (2) The built bundle imported `svelte/internal/client`, which every compiled component uses, from `/runtime/rt-svelte.js`, because the import mapping took the first shared specifier that was a prefix. That file has no `from_html`, so the app failed in the browser. Each shared specifier now maps to its own runtime file (`clientRuntimePath`), and an import of an unshared subpath such as `@lucide/svelte/icons/check` fails the build with a message that names it, instead of shipping a bundle the browser cannot link. (3) In dev the build probe loads `app.ts` in Node, and `@talaria/sdk` reached the router (ViewHeader → `lib/view-title`, and Markdown → AgentMediaImage → SaveDialog). sv-router reads `location` when it loads, so every dev rebuild failed with "location is not defined" and disabled the app. `lib/view-title` now gets the router's pathname from `router.ts` instead of importing it, and AgentMediaImage loads SaveDialog when it is first opened. (4) A fresh app's first database call failed with ENOENT because `db.env` was written before `app-data/<slug>/` existed. The directory is now created first, with mode 0700. (5) Two container-naming problems. `talaria dev` now passes `TALARIA_WORKTREE` to the Rust api, so in a worktree the api and the app side name the same app database container (`talaria-appdb-<worktree>-<slug>`) and uninstall stops the right one. Separately, a checkout install (`server-entry.ts` on the host) no longer counts as the product image, so it reaches the app database on the published loopback port rather than by a container name the host cannot resolve; only `TALARIA_INSTALL=image` means the image. A host outside the image that sets `TALARIA_APP_DB_NETWORK` dials the app database by container name too, because on that network the database publishes no port. An app built before this change is rebuilt, not reused. The build cache key now includes a build-recipe version (`BUILD_RECIPE` in `ui/src/server/app-build/key.ts`), which is bumped whenever `build.ts` changes what a build emits. Before, dev and checkout installs (no `TALARIA_VERSION`) kept the same key across the recipe change, reused the broken build still marked ready, and the first production probe turned the app off. Verified: `bun run gate` (svelte-check 0 errors; vitest 1894 passed; cli `tsc` and `bun test` 258 passed), including new tests. A real Vite build of a small app checks that `app.js` keeps `export{… as default}` and imports only host runtime files, `rt-svelte-internal-client.js` among them. A build with a deep `@lucide/svelte/icons/check` import fails and names it. Components compiled in runes mode and legacy mode, and a runes module, have every `$.<name>` and named import checked against the exports of the runtime file its import maps to. These tests fail under the old prefix mapping, and the build test fails without `preserveEntrySignatures`. A walk of the SDK's load-time import graph finds no route to the router or sv-router; before the change it printed both chains. Other new tests cover `writeDbEnv` creating a fresh directory (0700) and a 0600 `db.env`, `inImage`, and `apiEnv` lifting `TALARIA_WORKTREE` from ui/.env with the shell winning. Live, on a worktree stack (api :5405, app :5305): `bun talaria app new field-notes`, then Enable in Manage → Apps under `talaria dev`. The build came back ready, `talaria-appdb-apps-enable-field-notes` started, the work surface at /x/field-notes added an item, and the item was still listed after a reload, read back both through `GET /api/apps/field-notes/items` and with `psql` in the app's own database. Then `bun run build`, and `bun server-entry.ts` with the worktree's api. Enable rebuilt the app (`app.js`, `app.css`, `server.js`, `mcp.js`). The surface loaded the built `app.js`, whose only imports are `rt-svelte-internal-client.js`, `rt-svelte-internal-disclose-version.js` and `rt-talaria-sdk.js` and which ends `export{H as default}`. A second item was stored and both items were listed. Back under `talaria dev`, with the api running with `TALARIA_WORKTREE=apps-enable`, Uninstall in Manage → Apps returned `{"ok":true}`, and `docker ps -a` showed no `talaria-appdb-apps-enable-*` container. `apps_enabled`, `app_db_passwords` and `apps_installed` were left empty. New tests: changing `BUILD_RECIPE` changes the key, `buildApp` rebuilds a ready build left under the previous recipe's key and still reuses one made under the current key, and `dialsByName` covers the image, the named network and the loopback case. The key test and the rebuild test both fail when the recipe is left out of the hash. Live, on a worktree stack (app :5303, api :5403). Under `talaria dev`, with `build.ts` set back to the old recipe and the key without a recipe, Enable built `field-notes` as ready at key `d957d2553b2bc22c`. Its `app.js` had no export and imported `rt-svelte.js`. Control: `bun run build` and `bun server-entry.ts` at the PR's previous head reused that key and failed the probe ("app.js has no default export (defineApp)"), and the app was turned off. With this change, the same state was used: `current.json` and `apps_enabled` were written back to their values from before the control. The boot rebuilt the app from `d957d2553b2bc22c` to `8aeedb16d15528e6` (`app.js` ends `export{H as default}` and imports `rt-svelte-internal-client.js`). The app stayed enabled, and in Chromium /x/field-notes loaded that build, added an item and still listed it after a reload, with no page errors. Bumping `BUILD_RECIPE` to 3 and rebooting rebuilt the app at `e1b3c6da312361d1`. The browser loaded that build, a second item was added and both were listed (and in the app's own database). The bump was then reverted.

- **Added: an app can have routes below its surfaces — `/x/<slug>/<anything>` renders the work surface and `/x/<slug>/manage/<anything>` the manage surface.** An app's list, record pages and tabs now have addresses that can be linked, bookmarked, reloaded and stepped through with Back and Forward. Before this, `/x/<slug>/items/42` rendered Not Found. sv-router lets a top-level `*` beat a catch-all nested in the `/` layout group, so Not Found moves into that group as `(*)`, a catch-all that breaks out of the shell: the app routes stay under `/` and win, and an unknown path still renders Not Found bare. The route table moves to `ui/src/route-table.ts` so a test can run sv-router's own matcher over it. No `layout`, `hooks` or `meta` key sits at or below `/x`: sv-router matches those config keys as path segments that outrank `/:app`, so beside the slug they would shadow an app named `hooks` or `layout` and its matcher would throw. Install and `talaria app new` now refuse those three words as new slugs, and an app that already has one still opens. The SDK gains `useAppRoute()`, which gives the path below the surface, its decoded segments, the query, and `match('items/:id')` with params typed from the pattern. It also gains `appHref(path, { surface? })` and `appNavigate(path, { surface?, replace? })`, which resolve relative to the surface the page shows; `useApp()` gains `rest` and `query`. A settings tab stays one page with no routes below it, and links elsewhere with `{ surface }`. The route gate, the dock, the manage sidebar and Rust's `ViewGrants::denies` give every route below `/x/<slug>` to the work grant and every route below `/x/<slug>/manage` to the manage grant. They compare paths case-insensitively, as the router does: a work grant used to pass `/x/<slug>/MANAGE`, which the router mounts as the manage surface, and `/X/<slug>` passed as a core view nobody denies. `navigateHref` now passes a query and hash in the router's options instead of in the path, so notification and activity links such as `/artifacts?a=<id>` open their view instead of Not Found. It also resolves the href as the browser will before the router matches it (`..`, `%2e%2e`, `./`, backslashes, tabs, newlines and control characters), so the router mounts the surface for the same path the route gate checks, and it refuses an href to another origin. Unresolved, `/x/<slug>/manage/../items` mounted the manage surface at the address `/x/<slug>/items`, which the gate judged as the work view. `appHref` and `appNavigate` resolve a path the same way and throw when it would leave its surface, such as `'../items'` from the manage surface; `{ surface }` is how to cross. The shell's route gate now withholds a denied view instead of only bouncing from it: as an effect alone, following a link into a surface the person does not hold rendered that surface for a moment before Home replaced it. The scaffold's work surface links each item to its own page at `items/<id>`, and its server answers `GET items/<id>`.

  Verified: `bun run gate`; ui vitest for the new `app-route` suite (surfaces, rest, `match`, href resolution, `appNavigate`), `resolveHref` (was `splitHref`), `app-grants`, `nav-sections`, `manage-area`, `app-hooks`, and the shared-fixture suite, whose new `routes` cases Rust also asserts (`cargo test -p talaria-users --lib`: 17 passed). `client-docs.test.ts` compiles and svelte-checks the new client.md example and the scaffold's `Item.svelte`, and it failed as expected when the example read a param the pattern does not capture. `cd cli && bun test src/cmd/app/new.test.ts` passed, `vite build` passed, and in the build the SDK's `appNavigate` reaches the same router chunk as the host. On the worktree stack I scaffolded an app with `bun talaria app new`, gave it manage and settings surfaces, enabled it from Manage → Apps (with #583 merged in locally for the enable step only), and granted three members through `PUT /api/admin/users`. In Chromium, for both that build and this branch alone:
  - A work-only member deep-linked to `/x/<slug>/items/<id>`. The list's `appHref` links clicked through without a page load, Back and Forward stepped list ↔ record, a reload kept the record, and the dock tile stayed lit. `/x/<slug>/a/b` stayed open, and `/x/<slug>/manage`, `/manage/fields/color` and `/MANAGE/fields/color` bounced home without the manage surface rendering.
  - A manage-only member deep-linked to `/x/<slug>/manage/fields/color`, which was handed rest `fields/color` with the sidebar row lit. `appNavigate('fields/size?x=1')` moved both route and query, and Back and Forward undid and redid it. The settings tab rendered with an empty rest and linked into the manage route. `/x/<slug>`, `/x/<slug>/a/b` and a record page bounced.
  - A member with no grant bounced from all four app paths tried, including `/X/<slug>/items` and `/x/<SLUG>/manage`.
  - An admin reached both surfaces, and a record page for a missing id showed the read's failure with Retry.
  - Review round. `route-table.test.ts` runs sv-router's own `matchRoute` over the real route table for every path in the shared fixture (now with `hooks`, `layout` and `meta` slugs and app routes named like them), for escaped and doubled spellings, and for resolved hrefs, and checks each mounts the surface the gate's `appViewFor` names (or that the gate fails closed on an escaped slug). Run against the previous table shape, it failed 4 of its 8 cases, including the throw on `/x/layout`. `cargo test -p talaria-apps` covers `install_slug` (3 tests) and `talaria-users` pins `RESERVED_APP_SLUGS` to the fixture; `new.test.ts` checks `talaria app new` refuses the same words.
  - Live, on a fresh worktree stack with an app under the slug `hooks` (scaffolded under another name and renamed, as an app installed before the refusal would be) and an ordinary app, both enabled through `POST /api/app-host/<slug>/rebuild` and `PUT /api/admin/apps`, I ran 81 Playwright checks in Chromium, and all passed. `POST /api/admin/apps` answered 400 "is reserved" for a repo named `hooks`, for `talaria-app-meta.git` and for the override `layout`, and `bun talaria app new hooks` exited 1. For both apps, a work-only member deep-linked to a record, followed the list and record links, stepped Back and Forward, reloaded, opened `/x/<slug>/a/b` and `/x/<slug>/hooks`, and had `appNavigate('manage/fields')` refused in place. `/manage`, `/manage/fields/color` and `/MANAGE/fields` bounced without the manage surface rendering, as did `navigateHref('/x/<slug>/items/%2e%2e/manage/fields')`, while `navigateHref('/x/<slug>/manage/../items')` mounted the work surface at `/x/<slug>/items`. A manage-only member deep-linked to `/manage/fields/color`, moved route and query with `appNavigate`, stepped Back and Forward, and had `appNavigate('../items')` refused; its link into the work surface, three work paths and `navigateHref('/x/<slug>/manage/../items')` bounced without the work surface rendering. A member with no grant bounced from eight paths. An admin opened both surfaces, `/x/layout` and `/x/meta/items` showed "App not available" instead of a blank page, `/nope/deeper` and `/a/nope/deeper` showed Not Found without the shell, and no page raised an error. The hooks dock tile opened the app after a hover. With `navigateHref` temporarily passing the raw path, the work-only member was left on the manage surface at `/x/hooks/items`. With the gate's old effect-only bounce, six of those bounces showed the denied surface for a moment first.

- **Changed: the app docs now say what actually runs an app harness — only the app's own `server.ts`, through `runHarness` — and the SDK's `defineHarness` is now the platform's, so an app's JSON harness refuses a model measured unable to produce JSON.** That is a behavior change for app authors. The SDK used to hand a definition back untouched, so an app's JSON harness ran on a model that a probe or an admin had recorded as `json: false`. It now gets the floor every platform harness derives (`json` added to `floor.capabilities`, `refuseBelow: true`), so on such a model it makes no call and returns `refused: true` with the harness's floor note. An untested model, or one whose JSON failure the gateway only learned from a 400, still runs. The docs: `docs/sdk/harnesses.md`, `docs/APPS.md`, `docs/HARNESSES.md`, `docs/RUST-MIGRATION.md` and the `@talaria/sdk/server` header now say that nothing compiles, registers or scores `apps/<slug>/harnesses/*.ts` today. HARNESSES.md points its 18 deleted `api/src` paths at the crates that hold them, counts 40 harnesses, documents the derived JSON floor, and drops the JSON-row workbench harness and the Claude Code/Codex/Aider row. APPS.md's uninstall says what uninstall does: the `wipeData` flag changes nothing. `docs/sdk/mcp.md` says a secret with a host list resolves for an app's tools only if the list names `talaria-app://<slug>`, and that otherwise the handler receives the handle text. `apps/README.md`'s client example reads `things.data?.things`. With the app grants, server contract, client, routes and MCP changes it merges in, `apps/README.md`, `docs/APPS.md` and `docs/sdk/getting-started.md` now agree with them: each surface is its own grant (per person or per team), the settings tab follows the manage grant, the gateway admits a holder of any surface and a manage-only route checks `ctx.access.manage`, the server context is `user`, `access`, `perms`, `can`, `segments`, `path`, `url`, `origin`, `store`, `api`, `secret` and `signal`, surfaces read their slug from the host and never spell it, each surface owns the routes below it, an app with no UI ships no `app.ts`, and an app that is turned off keeps its MCP server row and grants until uninstall removes them. `reference.md` and `getting-started.md` stop describing `harnesses/*.ts` as loaded, and `mcp.md` says an unresolved handle can sit anywhere in a string. The API reference generator now lists a required body field that a handler reads by hand, so `docs/api/admin.md` shows `installUrl` (six other route bodies gain required fields, and PUT `/api/admin/apps` renders as its two variants). `PlatformAgentId` gains `ticket-relevance`. Stale source comments in `ui/src/server/apps.ts`, `app-build/paths.ts`, the Dockerfile and `.dockerignore` now point at what exists. Verified: `bun run gate` passed (check, docs drift, svelte-check with 0 errors, 121 test files and 1888 tests), and again with the stack below merged in (svelte-check 0 errors over 5583 files, 141 test files and 2108 tests, cli 262 tests, and clippy and tests for the twelve api packages the stack touches). `ui/src/sdk/client-docs.test.ts` now also compiles and svelte-checks every example in `apps/README.md`, its server and MCP modules included: it caught the README's MCP search tool ignoring its `query` (now fixed), and it fails when the client example loops over `things.data` again. On a worktree stack, an app built verbatim from the README's examples answered as the README says: a member granted only the work view added and listed things and got 403 from the manage-only `stats` route, a member granted only the manage view got `{things: 2}` from it, as did an admin, a member with no grant got 403 and no session 401; the work surface, which never spells its slug, read `/api/apps/readme-probe/things` and rendered both names for the work member and the admin, and sent the manage-only member to the Inbox; the app's MCP row listed `things_search` from the load probe. New tests in `ui/src/sdk/server.test.ts` cover the doc's harness carrying the floor, a probed or declared `json: false` model being refused with zero transport calls, and a learned fact still running. Four of them fail against the old SDK. The new `ui/src/server/platform-agents.test.ts` holds the TS catalog to the Rust one and fails on the old list. On a worktree stack I built a throwaway app from the docs' examples. Its `defineHarness` returned `{capabilities: ['json'], refuseBelow: true}`. Its run on a model with a probe `json: false` fact came back refused without touching the endpoint, while an untested model on the same endpoint tried it, and so did the old SDK on the same model. Playwright showed the README surface rendering both stored names, and the old snippet rendered none. Five secret-handle cases resolved or passed through verbatim exactly as mcp.md says: unrestricted, locked without the token, locked with it, a shared-key caller, and an ungranted agent. An uninstall with `wipeData: false` still deleted the codebase and `db.env`, while the postgres-owned `pg/` survived.

- **Changed: each file in an enabled app's `harnesses/` registers again. It gets its own column in Admin → Models → Fitness, and the fitness sweep scores candidate models on its eval fixtures.** The app build compiles `harnesses/*.ts` into `harnesses.js`, with one lazily imported chunk per file under `_harnesses/` (build recipe 3). The load probe checks every harness on each build and enable. The checks are the ones the api runs on its builtin harnesses: the guard rule ids exist, the floor is a subset of `requires` and is empty unless it refuses, the JSON floor is derived as `defineHarness` derives it (so a JSON harness must list `json` in `requires`), capability names are real, fixture names are distinct, a widening has a reason, a temperature is in range, and the id is neither a builtin's nor one another enabled app registers. A harness that fails a check, or whose file throws on import, is skipped and never disables the app. Manage → Apps shows "N harnesses" and "N harnesses skipped" on the app's row, with one line per skipped file. The data is carried on the build status as `harnesses: { registered, problems }`. Two new host routes serve the fitness plane, and only to a loopback caller holding the internal service credential. Both HTTP wrappers stamp the caller's address as `x-talaria-peer` and overwrite any value a client sends. `GET /api/app-host/harnesses` lists every enabled app's harnesses as data: id, label, job, requirements, floor, guard rules, output kind, fixture names and bands, and source `app:<slug>`. It also names each file it skipped and why. `POST /api/app-host/<slug>/harnesses/<id>/cases/<name>` replays one fixture with the model pinned.
