The run writes no `harness_runs` or guard-findings rows, and the route returns the value, the model, the fixture's verdict, and the run's contract, repair, latency and token figures. On the api side, the new `talaria-app-harnesses` crate fetches that listing and interns each harness as metadata. `merge_app_layer` appends app harnesses after the builtins and never lets one replace a builtin. The eval sweep sends an app harness's fixtures to the host. It scores them with the same arithmetic as a builtin's: a floor refusal is a skip, a gap is unscored, and a host that cannot replay leaves the case unmeasured. The fitness matrix gets a new `app` slot kind, one column per app harness, labelled `<App name> · <label>`. That column is bound to that harness only and never to a role or platform-agent column. The value view now counts an enabled app harness's `harness_runs` rows instead of dropping them. The production entry tells the api where this host listens (`TALARIA_APP_HOST_URL`); `talaria dev` passes `PORT`. The app-harness divergence is gone from RUST-MIGRATION.md. docs/sdk/harnesses.md, APPS.md, HARNESSES.md, the SDK header and the generated API reference describe the registry. Spend from a sweep's model calls still reaches the usage ledger, as it does for every sweep case. Verified: `bun run gate` exited 0. It ran check, svelte-check with 0 errors, the full ui suite (2169 tests), the cli suite, and clippy `-D warnings` and the tests for every package the stack's diff touches. The ui suite includes new suites for the checks (25 malformed definitions, each with its sentence), the listing (enabled-only, import failure, builtin and cross-app id clashes), the probe's report, the loaders in dev and prod, the wire shape, the replay (pass, fail, gap, a throwing check, a contract failure after the repair turn, a floor refusal, estimated tokens, no rows filed), and the two routes with their guard. A test reads the Rust `EXPECTED_IDS` to pin the builtin id list. The cli suite (262) passed. `cargo test` on talaria-app-harnesses (7), talaria-harness-defs' registry (25), talaria-fitness (423) and talaria-routes-admin, and clippy `-D warnings` on all four, passed. New Rust tests cover the merge (append order, builtin refusal, first app keeps a clashing id), the interning, the sweep sending app fixtures to a scripted host (verdicts, skips, no dry run for an app tool loop, a host that refuses), the app column's binding and score, and an app harness's runs counting in the workload. Live, on a worktree stack under `talaria dev`, I scaffolded a test app with `bun talaria app new` and gave it two harnesses: a valid JSON triage harness with three fixtures, and one that names a guard rule that does not exist and refuses on `search` without requiring it. Enable in Manage → Apps showed "1 harness" and "1 harness skipped", with the reason line. `GET /api/app-host/harnesses` with the internal token listed only the valid harness and reported the other. It answered 403 with no token, a wrong token, an admin session cookie, or the token sent from the LAN address with a spoofed peer header, and the replay route refused a LAN caller the same way. An OpenAI-compatible mock on loopback was registered as an endpoint. "Test a model" on the Fitness page ran harness conformance for `mock/mock-small` across all 366 fixtures, and the matrix showed a `Help Desk · Ticket triage` column, unfit at 2 of 3 fixtures with the refund case failing as scripted. The api's registry counted 41 harnesses. `harness_runs` and `guard_findings` stayed empty, and disabling the app removed the column. Then on the same stack, with `bun run build` and `bun server-entry.ts`, the api was spawned with `TALARIA_APP_HOST_URL=http://127.0.0.1:5303`. Enable built `harnesses.js` with one chunk per file, and an app-only sweep replayed the three fixtures from the built artifact.

- **Fixed:** an app's MCP tools are checked when the app loads, its server row carries them from the moment the app is enabled, a broken build takes the server off every agent without losing a single grant, and app tools are never picked as the org's web-search supplier. The build probe checks each tool (a unique name of at most 200 characters using letters, digits, `_` and `-`, a description, an object `inputSchema` of at most 32 KiB, a handler). A tool that fails is left out of tools/list, tools/call and the catalog, and the reason shows on the server's card in Manage → MCP. It never disables the app. The probe writes the checked catalog to the app's data directory (`app-data/<slug>/mcp-catalog.json`), which is never served over HTTP, and the api copies it into the row on enable, at boot, and when the host asks. That ask goes through a new internal route, `POST /api/internal/apps/mcp-sync`. It accepts only a credential both processes derive from the encryption root, and the host's proxy answers 404 for `/api/internal/*`. "Discover tools" on an app server answers the stored catalog instead of a 502. When an app is turned off or its build or database fails, its row is no longer deleted (the delete cascaded every agent assignment, team grant and user grant). The row is marked off in a new `app_off` column with the reason, the agents that carried it roll and stop listing it, and the app MCP gateway refuses its tools. When the app is enabled and passes its probe again, the same row serves the same grants and those agents roll back. Only uninstalling an app deletes its row. The sync never touches the row's `enabled` flag after creating it, so an admin's **Disable server** on an app server (which the api now accepts; it used to answer 500) survives every boot and resync. Syncs run one at a time under a Postgres advisory lock, and a failed read of the enabled set fails the sync instead of taking every app server off. A stored enabled set that is not a list of slugs is a failed read too, by the rule every app gate reads it with: the sync fails and leaves the rows as they are, and the app MCP gateway refuses the app's tools with the reason. A lenient read had matched a slug inside a string value. The catalog writer creates the app's data directory owner-only, as the app database does. The web-search supplier lookup drops app rows in both the api and the TS harness runner, so a pin to an app tool falls through to the platform's own engine. Verified: `cargo test` for talaria-apps (the off/serve plan), talaria-mcp (`serving`, the wire's `appOff`), talaria-session (`require_internal` refuses no header, a session cookie, an agent key, a wrong or truncated token), talaria-config (the shared HMAC vector) and talaria-capability-reach; the new live tests `app_mcp_sync_live` (an agent assignment, a team grant and a user grant kept through an admin disable, two resyncs, a failed build and an app gone from disk, then deleted by uninstall) and `internal_routes` (403 without the token, 200 with it) against a real database; vitest for app-health (`failHealth` asks the api to resync and writes no row), the app MCP gateway route (a disabled or off app answers 403 with the reason, recorded in `mcp_tool_calls`, and its module is never loaded), app-mcp and mcp-status. Live on a worktree stack, with a throwaway app granted to a hired agent directly, to a second agent through a team, and to a person: the admin's Disable server took it off both agents, and after an api restart (the boot sync rewrote the row a second later), an internal-route resync and an app rebuild, it was still disabled. Re-enabled, both agents called the tool. Breaking `mcp.ts` and rebuilding turned the app off and marked the row off with the build error, both agents' rendered configs, whoami and MCP tabs dropped the server while their containers rolled, all three grants stayed, the gateway answered 403 and recorded it, and Playwright saw the card read APP OFF with the reason and "1 agent · 1 person · 1 team". Restoring `mcp.ts`, rebuilding and enabling the app brought the tool back to both agents with the grants intact. Uninstalling the app then deleted the row and its grants. The catalog file was in `app-data/`, and `/app-builds/<slug>/mcp-catalog.json` answered 404. Verified again with #583, #576, #586, #578 and #585 merged in, live on a worktree stack. An app whose `app.ts` imports the SDK and an MCP-only app with no `app.ts` both built, enabled and catalogued their tools, with the left-out tool named on the card. Discover tools answered 200 from the card. Two agents, one granted directly and one through a team, called the tool. A broken `mcp.ts` disabled through Manage → Apps showed APP OFF with the reason, and both agents dropped the server with all three grants kept. Rebuild and Enable brought it back. An admin's Disable server stayed off through an api restart, an internal resync and a rebuild. With `apps_enabled` set to the string `"mcpchk-suite"`, the gateway refused `mcpchk` with the reason, the internal resync answered 500 and left the rows serving, and the app's door answered 503.

- **Changed: an app surface now knows which app it is, `invalidate('things')` refreshes the filtered list the docs pair it with, and the SDK's fetch helpers are the host's own.** `AppSurface` hands each surface `{ slug, surface, manifest }` through a new `useApp()`, so client code no longer spells its slug: `useAppQuery(path, options?)`, `useAppInvalidate()` and the new `useAppApi()` default to the surface's installed slug, read once when the component initialises, so the verbs and invalidation a surface holds stay bound to the app it was mounted for, however the host mounts it; the explicit-slug forms installed apps already use keep working. Query keys are built from the path's segments and then its search params, so `invalidate('things')` now reaches `things?q=…` and `things/123`; it used to match only a key equal to the raw string. `useAppQuery` takes svelte-query options (`enabled`, `select`, `staleTime`, `placeholderData`…), as an object or a getter. `api()` and `appApi()` are rebuilt on `ui/src/lib/fetch-json.ts`: a non-2xx rejects with an `HttpError` carrying its status and the server's sentence, a 2xx that is not JSON says so, reads stop at 30s, and a write through `api()`, `appApi()` or `useAppApi()` takes `timeout` or `signal`. The SDK also exports `errorMessage`, `getStream`, `postStream`, `openStream`, `appQueryKey`, `useUserEvents` (the tab's one shared `/api/me/events` stream), the query-state trio `QueryState`, `QueryError` and `listQuery`, and the host primitives `SortHeader`, `AddRow`, `RenameField`, `RecordTitle` and `LibraryPane`. `talaria app new` writes a work surface that embeds no slug, renders its read through `QueryState` (a failed read shows "Could not load the items" with Retry, never "No items yet"), and catches both writes with an alert naming what failed. The client docs are corrected: `/api/agents` is `{ id, label, role, tiers }`, `Waiting` takes its required `label`, `submitOnEnter` handles Enter only (Escape-reverts is `inlineEditKeys`), and surfaces sit in the top dock's Apps group and the manage area behind the gear. `bun run check` now diffs `docs/sdk/reference.md` per entry point and per kind (fn, const, class, comp, type), not as one merged name set, and `scripts/check-docs.test.mjs` pins that parser. CI's ui job and `bun run gate` now also run the ui suite when `docs/sdk/` or `cli/src/cmd/app/` changes, because that suite compiles the docs' examples and the scaffold; a docs-only or scaffold-only edit used to skip it and pass. `apps/README.md` no longer hard-codes the slug in its client example. The dev server no longer watches the docs test's scratch `ui/.sdk-doc-examples-*` dir: its `tsconfig.json` made Vite clear its cache, which dropped the app runtime's SSR loader, so every app server answered "this app has no server" until a restart whenever the ui tests ran beside `talaria dev`. Verified: a new ui test (`ui/src/sdk/client-docs.test.ts`) compiles every `svelte` and SDK-importing `ts` fence in client.md, ui-kit.md and getting-started.md, plus every file the scaffolder writes, with the Svelte compiler and then svelte-check against the SDK (putting back the missing `label`, or a wrong `useAppQuery` call, fails it with the doc and line); `ui/src/lib/app-client.test.ts` drives a real `QueryClient`, showing `invalidate('things')` marks `things`, `things?q=ada`, `things/123` and `things/123?tab=notes` stale and leaves `thingstore` and other apps alone, and covers `HttpError` statuses, the deadline, a write timeout on `api()` and on a bound verb, and content-type beside caller headers; `ui/src/lib/app-hooks.test.ts` runs the hooks against a stubbed Svelte context and `createQuery`, showing all eight `useAppQuery` argument forms reach the right app, path and options, a getter path re-keys the read, `useAppInvalidate()` defaults to the surface's app, the slug-less forms throw outside a surface, and after the host moves a mounted surface to another app its query, verbs and invalidation still address the first (the old live-read code fails that test); a deliberate break of a client.md example in a docs-only diff made `bun run gate` select the ui suite, which failed naming the doc line; `cli` scaffolder tests assert no file embeds the slug and both writes catch. Live on the worktree stack, in Chromium: an app scaffolded as `contacts` and installed as `contacts-app` rendered its manifest name and empty state; with the search on "ada", adding "Adam Smith" sent `POST /items` then `GET /items?q=ada` and the filtered list showed both, while a non-matching add left it alone; with the `items` route throwing in `server.ts`, a fresh page got 500 "app crashed" and showed "Could not load the items" with Retry and no rows, and restoring the route and pressing Retry brought the list back from a fresh 200; with the app's database stopped, Add showed "Could not add the item"; a settings surface written with the old `useAppQuery(slug, getter)`, `appApi(slug)` and `useAppInvalidate(slug)` forms read and refreshed its list; and a surface calling `useUserEvents` left the tab with one `/api/me/events` connection. Live again after the review fixes, with two probe apps `slugcap-a` and `slugcap-b` enabled through `PUT /api/admin/apps`: a `useAppApi()` write with `{ timeout: 800 }` against a 5s route failed with `TimeoutError` after about 870ms (the previous code ignored the option and returned after 5110ms); a handler that awaited a slow write and then a second write while the dock moved the tab to `slugcap-b` sent both to `slugcap-a`, and `slugcap-b`'s server saw nothing (the previous code did the same here, because the host remounts the surface on every slug change); and running `client-docs.test.ts` beside the dev stack left `GET /api/apps/slugcap-a/hits` at 200 with no Vite tsconfig reload, where before the fix the same run turned it into a 404.

- **Added:** an app's MCP tool now learns who is calling and for whom, runs under a deadline, can answer structured results, and can be unit-tested with no host; the app gateway answers malformed and batched requests the way the Rust gateway does; and a changed tool catalog restarts the agents that carry it. The handler context gains `caller` (`name`, `id`, and `proven`, true only on the agent's own gateway key, false on the org-wide legacy key), `actingUserId` (a personal assistant's owner, else null), and `signal`, which aborts at the server's timeout (120 s unless an admin set one in Manage → MCP) or when the agent disconnects; a cut call answers a tool error at once and is recorded as cut off, or as cancelled when the agent left. Handlers can return `toolResult({ content, structuredContent, isError })`, and a tool can declare an `outputSchema`: its object return becomes `structuredContent`, every structured result is checked against the schema, and a result that breaks it is JSON-RPC -32603 naming the tool. `isUnresolvedHandle(value)` tells a handler that a `«secret:…»` handle reached it unresolved. The app gateway answers a body that is not JSON with -32700 and the Rust gateway's sentence and hexdump, a batch with -32600 per request (each `tools/call` in it recorded as refused), a non-object or method-less request with -32600, and, for an agent holding a tool subset, `resources/*`, `prompts/*` and `completion/*` with the Rust -32601, recorded under the method. When an app's probe writes a catalog that differs from the stored one, the api rolls the agents granted that server (talaria-apps `sync_app_mcp_servers`); an unchanged catalog rolls nobody. The new entry `@talaria/sdk/testing` exports `callAppTool(mcp, name, args, ctx?)`, which runs a tool through the gateway's own checks, deadline and result shaping, and `memoryStore()`; `TALARIA_APP_TESTS=<slug> bunx vitest run` from `ui/` runs an app's own tests. A platform stage can no longer call an app tool through the TS `callMcpTool`, which had no callers. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-apps` (only a different probe catalog is a change, key order is not) and the live test `app_mcp_sync_live` against the worktree database (a changed catalog and a description edit retool the row, the same catalog and an admin-disabled row do not); vitest for the wire twins (the Rust gateway's bodies, codes and offsets), the call core (results, schemas, deadline, a caller leaving, a handler that ignores its signal), the gateway route (caller and acting person, legacy key, timeout, disconnect, structured result, -32700, -32600, BOM, subset method gate, records), the testing entry and `memoryStore`, the docs' mcp.md examples run through `callAppTool`, and mcp.md's fences typechecked by the SDK docs compile test. Live on a worktree stack, with an app scaffolded by `talaria app new` and enabled in Manage → Apps, and agents calling the gateway on their own keys: a whoami tool answered `proven: true` with the agent's id, `actingUserId` set for a personal assistant and null for an org agent, and `proven: false` with a null id on the legacy key; with the server's timeout at 2 s a slow tool was answered at 2.0 s as a tool error and its handler saw a `TimeoutError`, and a client that hung up at 0.7 s left the handler an `AbortError` and a `cancelled` 499 row; an `outputSchema` tool returned `structuredContent` and a bad value got -32603; a locked secret without `talaria-app://<slug>` reached the handler as an unresolved handle and one listing it resolved; 46 malformed bodies got byte-identical -32700 sentences from the app gateway and the Rust gateway; a batch, `42`, a method-less object, a BOM-prefixed call and a subset agent's `resources/list` were answered and recorded as above. Adding a tool and then editing a description each rolled exactly the three carriers (granted directly, as a personal assistant, and through a team) and not an ungranted agent, while enabling a second app and restarting the host and api rolled nobody. The same calls through the production build, whose built `mcp.js` imports `toolResult` through the host's runtime shim, answered the same.

- **Fixed:** Hermes' command approvals now follow the agent's Talaria policy on the turns Talaria streams, and Nous-hosted connectors stay off. On a streamed turn (every chat, channel reply and work session) Hermes v0.22 treats the turn as attended. A dangerous terminal command skipped `approvals.unattended_mode`, the key the render pinned, and went first to Hermes' default `smart` guardian, an LLM that could approve `rm -rf` on an agent whose policy is deny. It then went to an `approval.request` frame that nothing read, and the turn stalled for up to 300 s while the session's next turn queued behind it. The render now pins `approvals.mode` as well: `manual` with `deny` for an ordinary agent, so no model approves anything, and `off` with `approve` for a Developer Agent. `approvals.timeout` is pinned to 60 s as the backstop. The fleet chat door taps every turn's stream and answers each request `deny` through the agent's own `POST /v1/runs/{id}/approval`, with the `{request_id, execution_generation, choice}` body that v0.22's session authority requires. It never answers `once`, not even for a Developer Agent. Under `mode: off` the only requests a Developer Agent still raises come from the gates Hermes never lets anything auto-approve: a write to a project's AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / SOUL.md, an untrusted MCP server's write tool, a saved card fill. v0.22 strips the `pattern_key` that would tell those apart from a command. Each refusal lands in the audit log as `agent.approval_denied`, with the agent, the redacted command, the run and whether Hermes took the answer. The render also pins `tools.connectors.enabled: false` and `nous.guest: false`. Hermes ships both on, and `manage_connections` was offered to every agent on the api-server toolset, so agents could reach third-party accounts through a Nous identity that bypassed the MCP gateway. Verified: `bun run check` and `bun run gate` (fmt, clippy and tests for `talaria-gateway`, `talaria-fleet-render` and `talaria-jobs`; CI's api job is the full-workspace proof line, since `api/Cargo.lock` gained the `talaria-jobs` → `talaria-audit` edge). Reproduced the bug first on a standalone `nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.22.4@sha256:7a69…a4cf` container carrying rc's approvals block and a scripted model: the `approval.request` frame went unanswered, the turn held, and the session's next turn queued behind it until the request was answered by hand. Then exercised the change in a worktree stack on that pinned image: hired an agent backed by the scripted model through the stack's own gateway, opened `terminal`, read the rendered `approvals` / `tools.connectors` / `nous` blocks back from `/opt/data/config.yaml` inside the container, and drove `/api/chat`. On the completions arm, `rm -rf` on a hermes-owned canary was answered `deny` by the door, with 0.6 s between the model's tool call and its next request, the command came back BLOCKED with the canary intact, and an audit row was written. The session arm (pinned sessions) behaved the same. `echo` ran with no prompt. A Developer Agent (`mode: off`) ran the same `rm -rf` with no request and the canary went. A Developer Agent asking to write `/tmp/hx-repo/AGENTS.md` raised Hermes' protected-instruction request (`<write to AGENTS.md>`, choices once/deny). An earlier draft of this change answered it `once`, and Hermes took that as consent; the write was then stopped only by the image's own `HERMES_WRITE_SAFE_ROOT`. Now it is refused within 10 ms, Hermes returns its own BLOCKED, no file lands, and the row reads `agent.approval_denied`. A Developer def still running a `manual` container (the window before a recreate) has its `rm -rf` refused too, with the canary intact. On the probe container, Hermes' defaults offered 19 tools including `manage_connections`, and the two pinned keys took it to 18. The hired agent's offer carried no `manage_connections` either.

- **Changed:** **An app installed from git can now come from a private repository, be updated to a newer commit with automatic rollback, and be uninstalled without losing its data; a manifest the rules refuse is turned away at install with the reason.** One manifest validator (a new `talaria-app-manifest` crate, mirrored by `ui/src/server/app-build/manifest.ts` and pinned to the shared fixture `api/tests/it/fixtures/app-manifest.json`) runs on install, update and discovery: a required `name`, the `surfaces` shape, an optional `slug` (held to the install rule and the reserved words), an optional `sdk` range the host checks against its SDK version (1.0.0, one constant on each side pinned by the fixture), and reserved `harnesses`/`triggers` keys. It is published as `docs/sdk/talaria.schema.json`. An installed directory whose manifest fails is listed in Manage → Apps as **broken manifest** with the reason, cannot be enabled, and can be uninstalled; before, a manifest without a name installed "successfully" and left an app nobody could see or remove. Install fetches the one commit into a staging directory, checks the manifest, takes the declared slug (else the repository's name, or an override), refuses a taken or reserved one, renames the tree into `apps/<slug>`, records the repository, ref and commit in a new `app_sources` table, and asks the host to build it rather than waiting on the file watcher. A github.com repository the GitHub connection can see is read with a repo-scoped token narrowed to a new read-only `REPO_READ_PERMISSIONS` (never widened on a refusal); another host's private repository is read with a workspace secret named in the install, whose Spendable-at list must name that host and whose spend is audited. The token reaches git only through `GIT_ASKPASS`, answered only for that host, with no credential helper and `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` — never in the URL, a command line or `.git/config`. `PUT /api/admin/apps {app, update: true, ref?}` (admin, audited as `app.update` or `app.update-failed`) fetches the new commit into `apps/.<slug>.next`, has the host build and probe it there while the live app keeps serving, swaps the two trees in one `renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE)` and keeps the old one as `apps/.<slug>.prev`; a version that fails to build or load, before or after the swap, is rolled back and the app stays enabled on the previous commit. `GET /api/admin/apps?updates=1` (admin) says, per app, whether its ref now points at a newer commit (`git ls-remote`), and Manage → Apps shows each app's repository, ref and short commit, **update available**, an Update button and the outcome. Uninstall now keeps the app's data (database files, `db.env`, the sealed password) unless `wipeData` is set, and a reinstall reattaches it; with `wipeData` the store is emptied while its database still runs, the database is stopped, and the data directory — owned by the database container's user — is removed through a throwaway container. The compose file and any update staging trees go either way, and the host's directory watcher stops an app's database when its directory leaves instead of deleting its data (and no longer writes a failed build pointer back for an uninstalled app). A fresh app database's first start now waits for Postgres over TCP, so an install's first build no longer fails with "database did not start: read ECONNRESET" while initdb's socket-only server is up. `TALARIA_APPS_LOCAL_SOURCES=1` (dev only, lifted from `ui/.env` by `talaria dev`) lets a stack install from `file://` or loopback `http://`. Verified: `bun run gate` passed (check; svelte-check 0 errors over 5588 files; ui vitest 143 files / 2188 tests; cli typecheck and 263 tests; and `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings` and tests, each `-p`, for the 15 api packages the stack touches), the migration replays against a scratch `postgres:16-alpine` with `schema.snapshot.sql` regenerated, and `bun run docs:api` renders `PUT /api/admin/apps` as its three variants. Unit tests: talaria-app-manifest, talaria-apps (including a mock smart-HTTP git server that demands a token: the secret reaches git through askpass and in no request line, a missing credential fails at once without a prompt, askpass refuses another host, a github.com repository gets the connection's read token and a refusal falls back to anonymous), talaria-users, talaria-github and talaria-routes-admin tests pass; the TS manifest, update, build and app-host suites pass. Live on a worktree stack, in `talaria dev` and again under `server-entry.ts` in production mode: an app scaffolded with `talaria app new` and committed to a local repository installed through Manage → Apps → Install from Git (built on install), enabled, and stored a record; a new commit showed **update available**, Update moved it from 6f3636f to f0fed9e with its record intact; a commit that broke the build was rolled back with the app still enabled on f0fed9e and its staged build removed; a commit that loaded only where it was staged failed its live probe after the swap and was swapped back; invalid manifests (unknown surface, `sdk: ^2.0`, no name) were refused with their reasons and left nothing in `apps/`; a hand-placed broken app was listed with its reason, refused enable and uninstalled; uninstall keeping data removed the container, code, build and compose file and kept `pg/`, `db.env` and the password, and a reinstall reported and reattached the record; uninstall with `wipeData` ran `truncate docs` in the running database, then stopped it, then removed the root-owned files through a throwaway container, leaving no data directory or password; a private repository on a local git host that demands a token installed only with a workspace secret listing that host (no credential: "terminal prompts disabled"; a secret locked to another host: refused by name), its spend was audited, and its updates, an up-to-date check, a commit-pinned ref and a switch back to `main` worked through the same secret; in production the app database container saw no stop or restart during an update.

- **Removed: five pieces of agent plumbing that Hermes v0.22.4 already covers.**
  - **`POST /api/search` and its resolver are gone** (`search_the_web`, `WebSearch` and the `CALL_MCP_TOOL` twin in `talaria-web-search`, plus their `talaria-jobs` wiring). They were left behind when the agent `web_search` MCP tool was removed on 2026-10-16, and nothing called them. Kept: `/api/admin/search`, which sets the `SEARXNG_URL` Hermes's own search reads, and `results_from_payload`, which research uses.
  - **The `log_usage` MCP tool and `POST /api/tasks/{id}/usage` are gone.** Every Hermes agent's model traffic is already metered at the gateway, so each self-report counted spend a second time, on token counts the agent guessed: once in the ticket rollup, again in the fleet totals and again in the agent's budget window. The GET rollup stays, and rows written before this change still count in it. No other caller of the POST exists: we checked ui, mcp, desktop, mobile, cli, the skills, plugin, the apps subrepos and the Oh My Pi / coding-account paths.
  - **Nothing execs into an agent after it comes up any more.** The post-health browser install was a no-op on v0.22.4: in Docker, `hermes tools post-setup agent_browser` only checks, and the image ships pinned Chromium. It is gone, along with its marker and the `TALARIA_BROWSER_INSTALL` brake. The per-up/per-roll `docker exec rm -rf` of replaced bundled skill packs is gone too. Instead, Hermes's own `skills_sync` defers any bundled skill whose name a skill in `/opt/skills` provides. New `himalaya` and `email-inbox-triage` signposts cover the two names that were missing. Before this change, those two IMAP skills loaded on a fresh volume until the prune ran. The signpost test and the `bun run check` invariant now require a signpost for every name in a replaced pack, where before one name was enough. A replaced entry now names one skill directory (`email/himalaya`, `email/email-inbox-triage`, `note-taking/obsidian`), never a category. The deleted `rm -rf` used to clear a whole category, so a sibling Hermes added there later was removed with it. Now that sibling fails the tripwire as unclassified, where under a category path it would have passed as replaced with no signpost holding its name. The chassis smoke also reads each live skill's frontmatter name, and fails when a skill under a replaced path carries a name the entry does not list or no signpost declares. The toolset panel no longer says that turning `browser` off skips a browser setup.
  - **The tool-offer pruning measurement is gone** (`talaria-decide` `tools.rs`, the `tool-prune` census site, the admin `toolShadow` switch and its checkbox). Its premise was that every turn carries the full toolkit. That is false on v0.22.4: Hermes's tool search keeps MCP schemas behind `tool_search` / `tool_describe` / `tool_call`. Every agent config now pins `tools.tool_search.enabled: on`, unless the def authored its own value. A def's legacy `tools.tool_search: false`, which Hermes reads as off, stays as written.
  - **Agents are pointed at their own `web_search` for quick facts.** The toolkit skill and the MCP `research` description, for agents that have their own web search, now keep `research` for cited work someone will rely on. A recon run refuses on an install with no workspace search provider, while the agent's own search still works.
  - **Verified:**
    - `bun run check` and `bun run gate`: ui typecheck plus 1,880 vitest tests, the mcp typecheck, and clippy plus 901 cargo tests across the 17 touched crates. The tightened signpost test fails when the `himalaya` signpost is removed, and so does the invariant.
    - A grep across the tree finds no remaining reference to any deleted symbol, apart from comments that record the removal.
    - The chassis smoke against the pinned v0.22.4 image (run under its own compose project name) passes: 58 packs, all classified, every replaced name held. In a second run, with the `himalaya` signpost moved aside and the inbox-triage entry's `names[]` set to a wrong name, it fails and names both skills, after parsing each frontmatter name from the image. `bun run check` fails with `hermes-skill-replaced-category` when `note-taking/obsidian` goes back to `note-taking`.
    - Live in the worktree stack on `nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.22.4@sha256:7a6920…`:
      - A hired agent came up healthy through Talaria's control `up` and `POST /api/fleet/reconcile`. Over both start paths, `docker events` shows only Docker's own healthcheck execs into the container.
      - Hermes's boot log deferred all 15 replaced bundled skills to external_dirs, `himalaya` and `email-inbox-triage` included. `hermes skills list` shows only the Talaria signposts for those names. `/opt/data/skills` holds none of the replaced packs, only the empty `email/` and `note-taking/` category descriptions.
      - On that fresh volume, with no install step and no marker, Hermes's own `browser_navigate` loaded https://example.com.
      - The container's config carries `tools.tool_search.enabled: 'on'`, and Hermes resolves it as `on`. With the toolkit connected, its log reads `MCP: registered 83 tool(s)` and then `tool_search activated (tier 1): 10 core/visible tools kept, 84 deferred (~19510 tokens)`. The served toolkit has no `log_usage` and carries the new `research` text.
      - A chat turn through the gateway answered 200.
      - `POST /api/search` answers 404. `POST /api/tasks/{id}/usage` answers 405 to both a session and the agent's key, and the ticket's GET rollup answers 200. `GET /api/admin/decide` carries no `toolShadow` and 11 sites.
    - Not exercised:
      - A roll. Blue/green rolls of running agents fail before cutover today, which the hx-rolls change fixes.
      - The admin panel in a browser. Its checkbox only renders with a decision provider configured.
    - CI is the proof line for the full workspace compile and test run.

- **Fixed:** `talaria deploy update` finishes on the CLI it just pulled, and it fixes a fragment-less COMPOSE_FILE export where it lives instead of warning about it on every run. The update loaded its code before `git pull` and finished in it, so a pull that changed the CLI ran the old logic against the new compose files: on a customer VM that was `no such service: searxng-config` and a failed update, then a clean second run. When the sync (`git pull --ff-only`, or the pinned branch's fetch and fast-forward) moves HEAD, the update now re-launches `cli/bin/talaria.ts deploy update` for the rest, and the child skips the sync and the drift warning the parent already ran. The COMPOSE_FILE repair used to fix only the run in hand, so its warning came back every time. Now a line in `~/.profile`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.zshrc`, fish's `config.fish`, `/etc/environment` or `/etc/profile.d/*.sh` whose value is exactly the broken list is rewritten to the repaired one, with quotes, `export`, comments and every other line kept. The run says which file it fixed. A shell opened before the fix gets one dim line until it re-reads its profile, and only an export the CLI cannot find or write still warns. The first update that pulls this change still runs the old code once. Verified: `cd cli && bun test` (the deploy suite with four new update tests; a new profile-export suite covering each shell's syntax, quotes and comments, other values left alone, an already-fixed file, an unwritable file, and composeFileEnv's three outcomes) and `bun run typecheck`. End to end with real git and a stub docker: a scratch clone running this CLI pulled a newer commit that changed the CLI. The newer commit's own log line printed and docker saw one `compose pull` and one `up -d`, with exit 0. The `.bashrc` export gained `docker/sidecars.compose.yml` with its other lines unchanged. A second run from the same shell printed only the dim line, a fresh shell printed nothing about COMPOSE_FILE, and a branch-pinned update re-launched the same way.

- **Fixed:** **An app's API and compiled client now admit only people granted the app, each app surface is its own grant, and the gate fails closed.** Before, `/api/apps/<slug>/*` checked only the work view `/x/<slug>`, so any member could call a manage-only or settings-only app, and a member granted only the work view could call the routes behind the app's Manage surface. A grant for only an app's Manage surface did nothing: the route gate, the nav and the gateway all denied it as a child of the denied work view. `/app-builds/*` served every build file with no session at all, including the compiled `server.js` and `mcp.js` and the `current.json` that names the build key. Now:
  - `GET /api/auth/session` serves `appGrants`, the app views the person holds (person and team grants together, from `talaria_users::view_grants`). The app gateway, the `/app-builds/` door, the nav, the manage sidebar, the route gate and the settings tabs open an app view only when that list names it, never because a view is missing from `deniedViews`. An admin holds every app by role and gets an empty list.
  - When the Rust api cannot read the enabled apps (a malformed `apps_enabled` setting, or an apps directory it cannot list), a member's session still answers 200 with their core `deniedViews` and `perms`, and serves `appGrants: null` with `appsUnreadable: true` instead of leaving the app views out. Every app reader treats that as no app at all: the nav, the route gate and the settings tabs show no app, and both app doors answer 503. The rest of Talaria stays open, and Rust's `require_view` still answers for core views such as `/teams` and `/observability`. The TypeScript host reads `apps_enabled` by the same rule and answers 503 too. An admin's session skips that read, so Admin → Apps stays reachable, and toggling an app there rewrites the setting. The TS session reader throws, and the gate answers 503, when `deniedViews`, `appGrants` or `perms` is missing or is not a list of strings, unless `appsUnreadable` is true. A `talaria.json` that isn't valid UTF-8 is not an app on either host.
  - The gateway passes the app `ctx.access { admin, work, manage, settings }`, `ctx.perms` and `ctx.can(perm)`. A settings tab follows the manage grant, and an app that ships settings without a manage surface has `/x/<slug>/manage` to grant. Admin → People and Manage → Teams name each app view for the app and what it opens, for example "CRM · work" and "CRM · settings". Teams can grant app views. A person's or a team's manage-view list takes up to 200 views of up to 80 characters.
  - `/app-builds/` serves only `app.js`, `app.css` and `assets/**`, behind the same gate, as `private` cache, and only under the key the app's current, ready build pointer names. An older key answers 404, because builds made before this change keep their server and MCP chunks under `assets/`. The server and MCP builds now write their split chunks to `_server/` and `_mcp/`, outside what the door serves. A successful build removes the app's superseded key directories.
  - One fixture, `api/tests/it/fixtures/app-grants.json`, pins the TypeScript grant rule to the Rust one, and both test suites read it.

  Verified: `bun run gate` passed: check, svelte-check (0 errors), the full ui vitest run (127 files, 1947 tests), and clippy plus cargo tests for `talaria-api`, `talaria-routes-admin`, `talaria-routes-fleet`, `talaria-routes-integrations`, `talaria-session`, `talaria-settings` and `talaria-users`. That run includes the new `app-grants.fixture`, `app-gateway` (the route hands `access`, `perms` and `can` to the app), `app` (`/app-builds/` reaches the door undecoded) and `app-build/status` (current key, pruning) suites, `authorizeApp`'s 503 cases, and the `appGrants: null` cases for the gate, the nav, `isViewDenied`, `appAccess` and `rustSession`. The shared fixture has an `appsUnreadable` viewer that both runtimes read. The ignored live test `live_view_grants_list_a_settings_only_app_and_withhold_apps_it_cannot_read` passed against the worktree database: with a malformed setting or an unlistable directory, a member's core denials are unchanged and no app grant is held. On the worktree stack under `bun talaria dev`, I tested two probe apps. `grants-probe` has work, manage and settings surfaces and a server with a dynamic `import()`. `prefs-probe` has a settings tab and a server. Both builds were run with the host's builder. The callers were an admin, a work-only member, a manage-only member, a member granted the manage view through a team, a member granted only the settings-only app, a member with nothing, and no session. Results:
  - **API.** Each admitted caller's `appGrants` and `ctx.access` matched its grants. The manage route answered 403 to the work-only member and 200 to the manage-only and team members. The member with nothing got 403 everywhere, and no session got 401.
  - **Builds.** `app.js` and `app.css` followed the same rule. `server.js`, `mcp.js`, `current.json` and the server's `_server/lazy-*.js` chunk answered 404 to everyone, the admin included.
  - **Fail closed, apps only.** A later run used a probe app `scope-probe` (a work surface and a settings tab) and three callers: an admin, a member granted the app plus `/teams` and `/observability`, and a member with nothing. With `apps_enabled` set to `"scope-probe"`, `{"scope-probe": true}` or `["scope-probe", 7]`, and again with the apps directory at mode 000, every caller's session answered 200. The members got `appGrants: null` and `appsUnreadable: true` with their core `deniedViews` and `perms` unchanged. Every app door (`/api/apps/scope-probe/whoami` and the current key's `app.js`) answered 503. `/api/fleet` (`/observability`) still answered 200 to the granted member and 403 to the member with nothing, and `/api/me/threads` and `/api/boards` answered 200 to both. In Chromium, both members loaded the Inbox, and the granted member loaded `/observability` and `/teams`. Neither member saw the app in the nav or got its settings tab, and `/x/scope-probe` sent them to the Inbox. There were no page errors. With a valid list restored, the granted member's nav, settings tab and app route came back.
  - **Current key only.** With the probe's build current at `2ae625d836587dd5`, a hand-made pre-PR key directory `00000000deadbeef` held `app.js` and a server chunk under `assets/`. The admin and the granted member got 200 for the current key's `app.js` and `app.css`, and 404 for the old key's `app.js` and its `assets/` chunk. The member with nothing got 403 and no session got 401. A source change and a rebuild moved the pointer to `fb28554229a78d90` and removed both older key directories. The new key's `app.js` answered 200 and the previous key 404.
  - **Pages.** In Chromium, the manage-only and team members reached `/x/grants-probe/manage` and got its Manage link, and were sent away from `/x/grants-probe`. The work-only member was the reverse. Settings tabs followed the manage grant: Probe for the manage-only and team members, Prefs for the prefs member, both for the admin, none for the others. Admin → People offered "Grants probe · work", "Grants probe · manage" and "Prefs probe · settings", and Manage → Teams showed the same three names.

- **Fixed:** Federation seals the credentials written inline in an imported agent's config instead of storing them as written. `federate_one` used to store the source `config.yaml` whole as `raw` in `agent_versions`. A platform token, a named provider's key or an `Authorization` header sat in Postgres in plaintext, came back from the versions and history reads, and was re-emitted into the 0644 `config.yaml` the render writes. Now `talaria_agent_secrets::plan_config_seal` walks the raw config the way the render does, before anything is written. Each literal under a credential key that the render would emit becomes a per-agent secret named for its path (`CONFIG_PROVIDERS_LAN_PROXY_API_KEY`), sealed with the secretbox. Credential keys are read on the key's last word: `api_key`, `*_token`, `*_secret`, `password`, `private_key`, `encrypt_key`, `*_aes_key`, `Authorization`, `X-Api-Key` and the like. The config keeps a `${CONFIG_…}` handle in its place, which the render delivers through the agent's `secrets.env` and Hermes expands when it loads the file. Three kinds are dropped instead, because Talaria supplies that credential itself: a model spec's `api_key` becomes the gateway's `${LLM_API_KEY}`, an authored MCP server's inline credentials go, and so does the API server's own `key`, which Hermes replaces with the render's `API_SERVER_KEY` anyway. References (by Hermes's own `${…}` pattern), empty strings, non-strings and the top-level `secrets:` block stay as written; Hermes reads that block unexpanded, and it holds secret-manager references. A literal no env line can carry (multi-line, or over 8 KB) refuses that agent before any endpoint, key or def exists, and the error says plainly that Talaria cannot deliver it. A hire from a template copies the template's sealed secrets, as ciphertext, only when the hirer manages the template or is an admin. Otherwise the clone is hired without those settings, and its first version's note names each one. The federate result lists what was sealed and what was dropped per agent, and the modal shows it. `secrets.env` lines are now quoted where compose would otherwise rewrite the value: a `$`, a `#`, leading or trailing space, or an opening quote. Single quotes are used only for a value with no `'` and no `\`. Anything else is double-quoted with `\`, `"` and `$` escaped, because compose reads a final `\'` as an escaped quote and would refuse the whole file. Before this, a per-agent secret `pa$word` reached the container as `pa`. Plain values are written byte for byte as before. `docs/ENCRYPTION.md` and `docs/user/admin-agents.md` describe it. Verified: `bun run gate` (check, ui typecheck and tests, and fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and tests for the touched crates). Unit tests cover the credential-key rules, sealing, the dropped spec key, MCP credentials and API server key, the left-alone `secrets:` block, stray `${`, nested specs, a spec at the root, names for long and clashing paths, refusals, handle discovery, withholding, and the env-line quoting. All 27 quoting cases, trailing backslashes included, read back exactly from `docker compose config` and from a real container's `env` (compose v5.5.1). Exercised on this branch's own stack, with agents on the pinned `nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.22.4@sha256:7a69…a4cf`. A roster with a feishu `encrypt_key`, a wecom `encoding_aes_key`, a webhook `secret` holding a stray `${`, an API server `key` in both spellings, a 1Password `secrets:` block and the dashboard password `pa$wo\rd #\` federated to four sealed secrets and two dropped paths. A `pg_dump` grep for the six literals found none. After reconcile the container came up healthy (`/health` 0.22.4), and Hermes's own `load_config()` resolved all four handles to exactly the original literals. The `secrets:` block reached Hermes unchanged, and the API server took the render's key (200) and refused the dropped literal (401). A hire from that agent as template copied identical ciphertext for an admin and for a member who manages it. A member who does not manage it got none: no rows, no handles, a note naming the four paths, and a healthy container with no `CONFIG_` in its env. A multi-line `private_key` was refused by path, leaving no def. An earlier run on this branch proved a named provider's key and a dashboard password with `$$`, ` #` and `'` end to end the same way. Not exercised: the modal's new lines in a browser (svelte-check only), a hire nobody can be traced to (the create route always names the hirer), and an LLM call (none was needed to prove delivery). Rows written before this change keep their literals; sealing them needs a pass that also rolls each agent it touches, which is left as a follow-up. CI is the compile and test proof for the rest of the workspace (the lockfile changed).

- **Fixed: Hermes sessions survive agent restarts.** A turn lost in a crash is repaired instead of wedging the session, a session that is gone is replayed instead of held, and a resumed turn the agent is still running is picked up instead of sent twice. This covers pinned conversations and every work session. Hermes v0.22 marks a turn that was running when its container died non-gracefully (an OOM, `docker kill`, a host crash) `unknown`. It then refuses every later turn on that session with `unknown_execution`, and leaves each refused turn queued. Talaria showed that refusal as the reply to the auto-resume and to every message after it, forever. The session arm now repairs it in place. It withdraws the refused turn (`POST /v1/runs/{id}/stop`), acknowledges the lost one with `hermes sessions discard <session> --yes` inside the agent's container, and sends the turn again. The discard is needed because `/v1/runs/{id}/resolve-unknown` answers 404 for a session turn once the container has restarted. Hermes' own boundary row ("This turn did not complete…") tells the agent the first attempt did not finish. Second, a session that has carried turns is now looked up rather than re-created. A deleted session (whose id Hermes refuses to reuse, `409 session_deleted`) used to hold every turn for two minutes and answer "restarting" while the agent was up. After a lost state volume, the next turn went into the empty session Talaria had just created and answered without the conversation. Both now replay the full history at once, on every later turn too. A work session starts its session again instead, since its steps carry no history. Third, the auto-resume asks `GET /v1/runs/{id}` before it re-sends. A v0.22 session turn keeps running when its stream drops, so a turn the agent still holds is followed to its end and its reply lands on the same row. A run that ended `failed` meanwhile lands as the error row its live stream would have made and is not sent again, because Hermes' `failed` also covers a turn that did real work and stopped short. Only a run the agent does not know, or one it fenced as `unknown`, is sent again. Pinned sessions stay off by default: on a session a per-message tier runs the main model, and the session arm's usage frame (`input_tokens`/`output_tokens`) is not read, so its turns are ledgered as estimates. Verified: `bun run gate` (check, then clippy and tests for talaria-gateway, talaria-chat-persist, talaria-harness, talaria-conversations, talaria-fleet-docker and talaria-jobs), with new tests for the lost-turn watcher, the session answers, the run projection and the discard command. In this worktree's stack, on `nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.22.4@sha256:7a6920…a4cf`, with a pinned agent on a scripted model behind the stack's gateway, the first three cases were reproduced on rc and then exercised after the fix. **Kill mid-turn** (`docker kill`, then start): on rc the resume and the next message both answered `(agent error: unknown_execution)`, and Hermes held three admissions (`unknown`, `queued`, `queued`). After the fix the resume withdrew the refused turn (`cancelled`), discarded the lost one (`interrupted`), and completed on a new run. The model saw the first attempt, Hermes' boundary, and the resent message, and the next message answered in 0.4 s with the whole history. **Deleted session:** on rc the next turn took 2 min 5 s and landed "Sessie is restarting (or down)…". After the fix it took 0.66 s and replayed the full history, and so did the turn after it. **Lost volume:** on rc the third turn answered from an empty session ("SEEN 1 user turns: volume hello three"). After the fix it replayed all three. **Frozen container** (`docker pause` until the 60 s idle ceiling fired, then unpause; not reproduced on rc, where the resume re-sends unconditionally, and a standalone v0.22.4 container finished a session turn after its client hung up): the resume reattached to the same run (`run_c5620840…`, one admission, one copy of the message in Hermes) and landed its reply, and the next turn saw each message once. **Failed while frozen** (a scripted provider refusal, the container paused until the 60 s idle ceiling fired, then unpaused so the run ended `failed` before the 15 s resume): the resume picked up `run_48419c8a…` instead of re-sending, and the row landed Hermes' reply plus "(agent error: the run failed)". Hermes holds one admission for that message (`failed`), the model saw it once, no chain fired, and the next turn saw all three messages once. The work-session paths (the shared repair, and restarting a lost session) are proven by compile and unit tests here; CI runs the full workspace.

- **Changed:** Manage is a place now, with an overview, instead of a pane that slid out over whatever you were doing. The gear moved out of the row of work views to the right of the top bar, beside the assistant and next to the account menu that holds Settings and Admin. It goes to the new `/manage` overview, and so does the user menu's Manage entry. Every manage page (Agents, Teams, Models, MCP, Templates, Agent Studio, Observability, Apps, and each app's manage surface) keeps the Manage sidebar docked on its left. The sidebar has no pin and no overlay, and it is absent from work views; below `md` its rows become a strip across the top. The overview shows four things:
  - **Needs attention.** The instance's own alerts, worst first, each linking to where it is fixed. Shown to admins and people granted Observability.
  - **Tiles.** One per area the viewer has been granted, each opening its page:
    - agents up, with the down, degraded and warming beside it;
    - spend today and this month;
    - model providers, with any missing a key and any model role left unrouted;
    - MCP servers needing attention;
    - enabled apps and failed builds;
    - teams, templates, and skills with their open suggestions.
  - **Controls, for admins.** Roll every agent (with the same confirm and "also stopped" option as the Agents page), start stopped agents, and check every MCP server now instead of at the hourly pass.
  - **Recent changes.** The newest rows of the audit trail.

  A tile renders, and sends its request, only when the viewer holds that view and the endpoint's own permission. A member with no manage grants gets no gear and an empty state.

  Verified: `cd ui && bun run typecheck` (0 errors, 0 warnings), and `bunx vitest run` for the new `manage-area` suite and `nav-sections`. In Chromium against the worktree stack, as an admin at 1440×900:
  - the gear sat in the right cluster, lit on `/manage`, `/agents`, `/models` and `/observability` and unlit on `/work`, where no sidebar showed;
  - clicking it from `/work` opened the overview with the sidebar docked at 208px;
  - a sidebar row opened Observability with the sidebar still there;
  - all eight tiles rendered with live numbers;
  - Roll all showed its confirm and answered "Nothing to roll.", and Check now answered "No external servers to check.";
  - Start stopped rendered the started agents from an intercepted answer, because a real call would start containers on the host.

  At 390×844 the rows became a strip and nothing scrolled sideways. As a member granted Agents and Templates, the sidebar listed Overview, Agents and Templates, two tiles showed ("none you manage" for an empty roster), the controls and alerts panels did not render, and `/models` redirected home.

- **Every LLM call an agent makes is now metered at the gateway relay, one `usage_events` row per upstream call, and attributed to the conversation, channel, run or ticket that drove it — the per-turn ledger rows, the Redis turn register and the relay's skip are gone.** Before, while any Talaria-driven turn was open the relay skipped every call on the agent's key and the flow wrote one row from Hermes' main-loop counters, so auxiliary calls (titles, compression, vision, web_extract, session_search), delegated subagents and any cron that fired mid-turn reached no ledger, and a budget could not see a turn until it ended. Now every agent's config.yaml carries a `providers.talaria` entry on the same gateway URL its specs use (`session_affinity_header: x-talaria-session`, `key_env: LLM_API_KEY`, `discover_models: false`; rendered only while the brain is the gateway), so Hermes stamps its conversation key on every call. The specs keep `provider: custom`, and inside a v0.22.4 container the runtime provider stays `custom` (direct-alias), so anything keyed by it is unchanged. On a turn Talaria drives, Hermes' key is its own `gwk_…` digest of the session's route, so two records join it to the flow: the chat transport records the conversation it drove (`usage_attributions`: the session id it created, or the completions arm's `X-Hermes-Session-Id`, with source, `ref_id`, `task_id`), and the agent's talaria-events plugin reports from inside the turn which conversation its key names (new `pre_llm_call` hook → new `POST /api/agents/affinity`, agent's own credential only → `usage_affinity_keys`). The plugin keeps reporting a pair at each turn until the door has answered 2xx, so a report lost to a timeout, an api restart or a full queue is sent again, and its backfill claims the calls booked before it. The relay copies the flow onto each row in the insert, and whichever record lands second backfills the rows already booked. A cron fire carries `cron_<job id>` and is booked `unattended` per job; a call with no key is `unattended` under the agent. Rows keep the key (`usage_events.affinity_key`). `gateway_unmetered_keys` now defaults to empty and fleet-brain no longer forces the personas' key onto it; a migration removes that one entry, which every earlier render wrote, from a stored list, so the fleet-wide key agents fall back to when their own keys cannot be minted is booked again. A key an operator lists there is booked nowhere. An agent rename now carries its attribution records with it. A fleet an operator pointed at a raw upstream (a non-gateway `LLM_BASE_URL`) never reaches the relay, so it now books no agent spend; before, each chat, channel and harness turn wrote one row from Hermes' main-loop counters. The cost views' `generations` now count upstream calls rather than turns. Also fixed: LLM budgets never bound. `spend_since` sent its window as a `bigint` to `make_interval`, which takes only `int4`, so every read failed and `check_budget` failed open. Every configured budget now binds, an operator key's included. Verified: `bun run gate` green (check; ui svelte-check and 1,880 vitest tests; clippy `-D warnings` and cargo tests for the touched crates). Three new `#[ignore]`d live-DB tests in `talaria-gateway` (`usage::live_db`, run by CI's live-tests job) passed against the worktree Postgres: `spend_since` reads its window, a relay row takes the flow recorded for its key in the insert, and the second record backfills only the last day's `unattended` rows. The `spend_since` test fails with the old `bigint` bind ("function make_interval(hours => bigint) does not exist"). The schema snapshot was regenerated and re-checked (`applied: 0 … schema matches snapshot`), and `bun run docs:api` was rerun. CI's api job is the proof line for the whole workspace (`Cargo.lock` moved: the gateway crate drops `redis`). Exercised in the worktree stack on the pinned `nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.22.4@sha256:7a69201726bc…`, against Z.ai `glm-4.7-flash` through the stack's gateway. Inside the container, `/opt/data/config.yaml` carries the entry. Hermes' own `get_custom_provider_session_affinity_header` returns `x-talaria-session` for the spec's base URL, and `resolve_runtime_provider` answers `custom`/`direct-alias`. Every turn was then booked with the right attribution. A completions chat turn gave two rows (main loop + title), both `chat` with the conversation as `ref_id`. A pinned session turn was attributed the same way. A delegation turn gave four rows: the subagent's call carried the parent's conversation id. A channel reply was booked `channel` with the channel id. A work session on a real ticket gave 21 rows, each with the ticket as `task_id`, and the ticket's usage rollup priced them. A cron run-now landed as `unattended` under `cron_45fe2d12cf73`. An operator key's forged header was ignored (`gateway`, no key). `/api/cost` per-agent totals include the auxiliary and subagent rows. With `llm_budgets.agents["meter-metering"].tokens = 100000`, the agent's own key got `429 budget_exceeded` (414,951 of 100,000), which it did not before the fix. A chat turn on an agent over its budget now fails, and slowly: Hermes honours the relay's `Retry-After: 300`, retried twice, and the turn ended after 600 s as an error message carrying the budget sentence (and Hermes' own "resets in ~5 min"). Lifting the budget let the next turn through at once; Hermes did not bench the key. After the review fixes, re-exercised in the same stack: the app's migration runner turned a stored `["ops-own-key", "fleet-gateway"]` into `["ops-own-key"]`; a re-render put the new plugin in the container; a new conversation reported its `gwk_` key once and not on its next turn; and with `usage_affinity_keys` write-locked past the plugin's 4 s timeout during a turn, that conversation's next turn reported the pair again and the turn after did not, with all of its rows booked `chat`. A local run against a door that answered 500 then 200 showed the same: reported twice, confirmed once, the private `confirms` field never on the wire. Not exercised live: compression and vision auxiliary calls (they share the title call's path in Hermes source), and an agent on a Hermes image older than v0.21.4 (it sends no header, and its calls would be booked `unattended`).

- **Fixed:** A Developer Agent's Oh My Pi can authenticate to the Talaria gateway from the agent's own terminal, and per-agent secrets stop colliding with Hermes's names. Before this change, three things stopped omp, and the doctor's `--version` probe could see none of them. Hermes strips `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`OPENAI_BASE_URL` from every command its terminal runs, and `terminal.env_passthrough` cannot put them back, so the workbench key never reached omp. The rendered `apiKey: "$OPENAI_API_KEY"` was sent as that literal text, because omp reads an `apiKey` as a bare env-var name. And Hermes's terminal runs commands from a login-shell snapshot whose PATH Debian's `/etc/profile` resets, so `bun` in `/opt/data/.local/bin` was not found and omp exited 127. Now the key rides `TALARIA_WORKBENCH_API_KEY` (no `OPENAI_*` in the sandbox env), and the render writes `models.yml` naming it, mounted where omp reads it. omp converts a `models.json` into `models.yml` only once, so later renders never reached it. The boot hook links `/usr/local/bin/bun`. `doctor` runs its probes in that same login shell, and after `--version` it makes one model call through omp with every name Hermes strips unset first, so an omp that starts but cannot authenticate reads as broken. It skips that call, and says so, when the agent's jobs run on a coding subscription, or when the steps before it have used most of the 300 s Hermes gives an MCP call. A render leaves an older `models.json` in place, because a container created before it still binds that file. Per-agent secrets: names Talaria stamps or owns (`TALARIA_*`, `LLM_*`, the omp/git/Playwright env) are refused, and so are Hermes runtime settings (`HERMES_*`, `TERMINAL_*`, `GATEWAY_*`, `API_SERVER_*`, `AUXILIARY_*`) the container's process settings (`PATH`, `HOME`, `LD_*`, `PYTHONPATH`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `BASH_ENV`, `S6_*` …), and the 450 names Hermes v0.22.4 strips. That last set is a snapshot generated from the pinned image, with its refresh command in the file's header. A secret saved under such a name before this change still loads, and the Secrets tab now marks it with the reason. The render lists the remaining secret names in `terminal.env_passthrough`, so they reach `execute_code` as well as the terminal. Setting any per-agent secret also no longer fails with `invalid input syntax for type uuid`: the email in a TEXT column had been cast to uuid since the Rust port. The workbench-driving and subagent-driven-development skills point UI checks at `browser_exec` instead of `npx playwright`. On v0.22.4 that Browser Use CLI tool is the agent's only browser tool, because Hermes enables it by default in place of the `browser_*` tools. The subagent skill drops the `toolsets=` arguments `delegate_task` ignores and no longer claims subagents lack a file tool. The optional workbench image drops its Playwright layer, which the runtime `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` hid. Verified on the pinned `nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.22.4@sha256:7a6920…` in this worktree's stack, with a real gateway endpoint, a Developer Agent rendered and run by Talaria, and commands run through Hermes's own `LocalEnvironment` (the terminal tool's backend) inside the container. **Before:** the container env held `OPENAI_API_KEY` (a `tlk_` key) but Hermes's terminal env did not. omp there exited 127 (`env: 'bun': No such file or directory`). With bun linked by hand it answered `401 invalid API key`, the same 401 it gave under `docker exec` with the key present (the `$` literal). The volume held the `models.yml` omp had migrated at its first run, with `apiKey: $OPENAI_API_KEY`. `doctor` said "runs — omp/18.8.5, auth through the Talaria gateway". **After:** Hermes's terminal env carries `TALARIA_WORKBENCH_API_KEY` and `FIGMA_TOKEN`, and no `OPENAI_*`. `bun` resolves at `/usr/local/bin/bun`. omp 18.12.6 replied `OK`, and the gateway wrote a `usage_events` row on `api:workbench-gateway`. `doctor` reports "reached the Talaria gateway" with reply `OK`. With the old `$OPENAI_API_KEY` line put back in the mounted `models.yml`, it reports "CANNOT REACH THE TALARIA GATEWAY: omp exited 1: 401 invalid API key". `PUT …/secrets` answered 200 for `FIGMA_TOKEN` and 400, with the reason, for each of `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `TERMINAL_ENV`, `HERMES_HOME`, `TALARIA_WORKBENCH_API_KEY`, `LLM_API_KEY` and `PI_SMOL_MODEL`. The container's `config.yaml` carries `terminal.env_passthrough: [FIGMA_TOKEN]`. Hermes's `execute_code` env builder passes `FIGMA_TOKEN` with that list and drops it without one. The gateway logs "Single-profile install", so the value resolves from the process env. Hermes's own tool list for the agent, computed in the sandbox, offers `browser_exec` and no other browser tool, with the agent on a model that cannot see images. `browser_exec` opened a page served on localhost in the sandbox, read its heading, clicked its button, and `capture_screenshot()` saved a PNG. `doctor` on the gateway plan reached the gateway in 12 s. With the agent given a primary coding account (rows written straight to the database), `doctor` skipped the call and named the subscription, and no usage row was written. A render with an older `models.json` beside `models.yml` left the file there. A row stored before the rule (`TAVILY_API_KEY`) still went into `secrets.env`, stayed out of `env_passthrough`, and came back from the list with `refused`, and the Secrets tab showed the reason under it. `PUT` refused `PATH`, `HOME`, `LD_PRELOAD`, `PYTHONPATH`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `BASH_ENV`, `S6_KEEP_ENV` and `AGENT_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE_PATH`, and accepted `LINEAR_API_KEY`. Doctor's time budget is covered by a unit test only. `bun run gate` passed (check, plus fmt, clippy and tests for the six touched crates); CI is the full compile and test line.

- **Fixed:** Fleet agents now run Hermes' own loop guard, reasoning effort, persona tiers and title switch, configured by the render, instead of Talaria's copies that had drifted from Hermes. Five changes. (1) Each `config.yaml` turns on `tool_loop_guardrails.hard_stop_enabled`. Hermes counts `api_server` as an attended platform, so its hard stops were off on every agent. The guard that talaria-chat-persist ran on the stream is deleted. It matched calls on a display preview and an always-empty result hash, so it stopped legitimate work: five `cargo test` reruns on the pinned arm, or a false "Repeating the same call" chip after three MCP calls on different tickets on the completions arm. The person's own stop and steer, and the work-session thrash brake, are unchanged. (2) A turn's effort pick now travels as `model_options.reasoning_effort` on both persona arms. Hermes' API server ignores a top-level `reasoning_effort`, so every pick and every configured default ran at Hermes' `medium`, and the session arm carried no effort at all. The render writes each model's configured, vouched effort as `agent.reasoning_overrides`. It marks a model with no vouched levels `model_overrides.<provider>.<id>.supports_reasoning: false`, keyed by the provider id the model's routed spec names (`custom` today), so Hermes sends no effort for it instead of filling in `medium`. This is a behaviour change for every fleet model that neither its provider's catalog (in practice OpenRouter-style catalogs that publish `reasoning.supported_efforts`) nor an admin vouches levels for: its cron, channel, harness and session turns stop carrying Hermes' `medium` and run at the provider's own default, the same as Talaria's own chat already did for it. An operator restores effort by declaring the model's levels on the endpoint modal (`model_efforts`): that alone brings back Hermes' `medium`, and a level configured on the agent is rendered for that model. If the render cannot read the catalog or the endpoint roster, it leaves the reasoning block out rather than marking every model unvouched. The persona transports (Rust and the TS twin) no longer send `temperature` or `response_format`, which Hermes never reads. A JSON request to a persona now comes back `contract_dropped`, so the runner relies on its prompt anchor, the way it does on a gateway that strips the parameter. (3) Persona tiers render as `platforms.api_server.extra.model_routes` (`<persona>-<tier>` → the tier's upstream id). Without the route, a tier turn on the completions arm ran the main model and was metered as the tier. (4) `auxiliary.title_generation.model_upgrade_enabled: false` drops Hermes' background title call. Hermes still keeps its free instant title, and nothing in Talaria read the model-written ones. Verified on a worktree stack running the pinned `nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.22.4@sha256:7a6920…` image, with a recording mock upstream behind Talaria's gateway. Hermes' own loaders in the container read back `hard_stop_enabled=True`, `{effort: high}` for the main model and `low` for the tier, `None` and `supports_reasoning=False` for the unvouched model, and `model_upgrade_enabled=False`. `GET /v1/models` on the env-enabled API server listed `hxr-render-deep → hx-tier`. At the upstream: a direct call with no effort reached the main model at `high`; the tier alias reached `hx-tier` at `low`; `model_options` `medium` arrived as `medium`; a top-level `reasoning_effort`/`temperature`/`response_format` arrived as `high` with neither of the other two. The unvouched model got no `reasoning_effort`, and the same agent re-pointed at a vouched model with no configured level got Hermes' `medium`. Through `/api/chat`, an explicit `low` arrived as `low` on the completions arm and on a pinned session, a `deep` tier turn on the completions arm reached `hx-tier` at `low`, and its ledger row says `hx-tier`. A conversation that made the mock return the same tool call each time was halted by Hermes after five calls ("I stopped retrying because I kept running skills_list 5 times…"). The row landed complete, with no chip and no stopped stamp. Each chat turn made exactly one upstream call, so no title call. (5) A pinned (session-arm) conversation runs its agent's main model when a message picks a tier, because the session route carries no model and Hermes pins a session's model at its first turn. Those turns were booked and priced as the tier. They are now booked as the main model, and the tier's effort is not sent to the main model. Verified on the same stack: on a pinned conversation, a `deep` turn with `low` and a `deep` turn with no pick both reached `hx-main` at its rendered `high` and booked `llm_model = hx-main`; a re-render after these changes wrote byte-identical configs for both agents. `bun run check`, `bun run gate` (svelte-check, vitest 1881, clippy and cargo tests on the seven touched packages), the TS transport suite, and new unit tests for the render, the per-target effort lookup and the session booking. CI is the full compile and test line. Honouring a per-message tier on a pinned session is not done; it needs a design decision.

- **Changed:** the skills marketplace reads Hermes' own official skills index and runs Hermes' Skills Guard before every install; the toolset switches are now exactly Hermes' own, and a skill's frontmatter description is what the library shows. The marketplace used to scrape a third-party site's HTML for a ranked list of repos. Any member could make the server download any repo's tarball, and an editor could install every SKILL.md in it, unscanned, into roots every agent loads. Now the `skills-index-refresh` job mirrors Hermes' `skills-index.json` (the index Hermes' own skills search reads, rebuilt daily) into `skills_index_entries` every six hours. It keeps the ~20k rows Talaria can install (Hermes' official optional skills, its curated GitHub taps, skills.sh), and only a row whose identifier names the repo its files come from (official rows must be Hermes' own `optional-skills/`). It sends the last ETag, so most runs are a 304. The picker searches that table, one card per skill, with Hermes' trust level on each. Install takes a catalog id only. It fetches that one skill directory from GitHub at a pinned commit (two API calls, then raw files; never the repo, which runs to 245 MB for some catalog skills). It follows an official catalog stub to its upstream repo, scans it as Hermes' own install does (source `official`, so no finding is softened as a community one), and judges it as trusted, which is what Hermes says it intends. Then it runs Hermes' unmodified `scan_skill` and `should_allow_install` in a one-shot `docker run` of the fleet's own Hermes image (the chassis template's image when no chassis exists yet; no image at all fails closed): no network, read-only, all capabilities dropped, as nobody. At most two scans run at once, the same skill is scanned once however many clicks ask, and a scan that times out has its named container removed. A blocked skill is a 422 carrying the report and nothing is written. In the picker, a clean scan installs on the click. A skill the policy allows but whose scan found anything opens the report first and installs only on its **Install** button, as Hermes' own install shows the report and asks. A blocked skill opens the report with no button. The fetch-and-scan route (`detail`) now needs `owner` and edit rights there, and only serves catalog ids. Unrelated: `GOVERNED_TOOLSETS` drops the composites `safe`, `debugging` and `search`, the `coding` posture, and the GUI-only `project` and `desktop_ui`. Closing a composite closed its member tools while their rows read open, and the others closed nothing. A stored, org-floor, env or API-supplied retired name expands to the governed toolsets it closed (`search` reads as the stricter `web`), and a migration rewrites stored rows the same way. `scripts/hermes-toolsets.json` snapshots Hermes' `CONFIGURABLE_TOOLSETS`: a cargo test holds the list to it, and the chassis smoke holds it to the live image. The skill library serves a frontmatter `description:` as written, parsed the way Hermes parses it, and asks the summarizer only about skills that have none. Verified: `bun run gate`; `cargo test -p talaria-skills-marketplace` (21 tests: the index parse against rows copied from the live index, including gzip, dedupe, traversal, odd types and identifier/repo provenance; member selection, caps and slug lookup; stub pointers; compose-style image interpolation with every `-`/`+`/`?` form; the chassis → template → fail-closed image fallback; the hardened, named scan argv; the verdict parse), `-p talaria-agent-defs` and `-p talaria-agent-skills`; the migration array replayed on a scratch postgres:16 with the snapshot regenerated, and both toolset rewrites run on sample rows; svelte-check and the toolsets UI test. In the worktree stack, on `nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.22.4@sha256:7a69…a4cf`: the job mirrored the real index in 3.5 s (19,657 installable of 101,555 rows; official 153, GitHub 1,093, skills.sh 18,411, 49 by-slug), and the stored ETag answers 304. With the scheduler off and the mirror emptied, the first search synced it inline (3.4 s, 19,656 rows from the day's rebuilt index), and searches after that took about 45 ms. `detail` refused an anonymous caller (401), a member on the shared root (403), a missing owner (400) and an id outside the catalog (404). `official/security/1password` scanned safe/builtin on the pinned image and installed into the shared root. A second install answered `exists`, and inside the agent container `/opt/skills/1password` is present and `hermes skills list` shows it enabled. The real catalog skill `skills-sh/openhands/extensions/ssh` scanned dangerous/community (32 findings, from `~/.ssh` references to persistence patterns). Its install answered 422 and wrote nothing, and the picker showed the report worst-first, led by the critical `authorized_keys` finding (screenshots taken). `official/creative/archify` was followed to `tt-a1i/archify` and allowed as trusted with a caution verdict (62 findings). After the review's fixes, a forced full re-sync kept the same 19,656 rows (the provenance rule drops none of today's index). Every official stub was scanned at once, with impeccable requested three times: `docker events` showed 10 scan containers for the 10 distinct skills that reached a scan (brag stops at the 2 MB file cap first), never more than 2 at a time. Of the four that are still stubs at HEAD (archify, brag, brag-slim, impeccable), none has a doc-only `sudo_usage` or `bind_all_interfaces` finding, so scanning stubs as `official` moved no verdict today. In the browser: dream-loop (clean, builtin) installed on one click. Archify opened "Read before installing" with its 62 findings and posted no install until its button was pressed, then installed. The openhands ssh skill opened "Not installed" with no install button (screenshots taken). A PATCH of an agent's toolsets with `safe` and `coding` stored `web, vision, image_gen`, the rendered `config.yaml` carried them, and after a restart the agent's own `/v1/toolsets` reported all three disabled.
