The shell's other fixes: a notification is posted off the main thread, so a slow notification server cannot freeze the app (30 s before, 2 s now). A notification click no longer splits the window between stacked webviews. A corrupt `instances.json` or `settings.json` is moved aside and reported instead of crashing at startup. A relaunch into an unreachable instance shows the reason and a Retry on the launcher, plus Open anyway for an instance the shell's own check cannot see but the page can (a sign-in gate, a system proxy), and on Linux a page that fails to load mid-session returns there too. The page also survives a `mailto:` link or a download, where WebKit used to replace it with "The URL can't be shown". The add probe now allows 5 s to connect and 20 s in total, so a valid instance that answers in 10 s is added and a black hole fails in 5 s, not 8.5. Each failure says what went wrong, and Cancel and Escape stop a probe in flight without the instance landing later. The add error belongs to its dialog. The launcher follows switches and titlebar changes made inside instances, and the instances follow each other's titlebar choice. Remove is reachable by keyboard and both modals trap focus and close on Escape. A relaunch reopens only an instance you were in. A removed instance's data dir stays gone: the registry records the removal, and the next launch deletes the dir again if WebKit re-created it. No other data dir is deleted, so a damaged registry never costs the sessions of the entries it lost. The update check gives up after 10 s with plain copy (was 30 s, then an opaque error). The window fits a small or high-scale screen. A nameless instance no longer shows its host twice. Verified on a headless WebKitGTK 2.52 rig (mutter, tauri-driver, compositor screen capture), against the production build and, for before/after, the unmodified rc build on the same host. All 18 add kinds went through the real dialog. Cancel was tested by click, by dispatched Escape and by a real key. Five corrupt-file cases were launched, including a direct launch, and a recovered registry was relaunched twice more with a lost entry's data dir beside it, which survived. Each relaunch case was run: resume, vanished, black hole, a page whose beacon answers but whose page fails, and a mid-session failure. Keyboard order and the focus trap used real keys. The notification click and a 30 s-slow server were tested against a mock D-Bus service. The worktree's real Talaria UI was opened, Ctrl+Shift+H was tested on it, and an OS-titlebar change was made while it was hidden: rc's ui shows a double titlebar there, this one does not. macOS and Windows were not run. `bun run gate` was green; CI is the full compile and test line.

- **Fixed: a disabled field looks disabled, the agent roster and the memory's Whole file view no longer stick on skeletons, a devbox's app can open its app databases, and an app's database no longer answers for the platform's `postgres` on the image's network. Round 5: four more surfaces leave their skeletons, an idle empty page or brief no longer keeps the main thread busy, and an MCP package served over HTTP starts and answers, in a devbox too, and still after the box's container is recreated.**
  - **F23.** The `Input`, `Textarea` and `Select` primitives had no disabled state, so a viewer's task title, a field held during a save and a setting switched off all drew like fields that took typing. They take `disabledControl` (`components/ui/control.ts`): the shared `dimDisabled` plus a not-allowed cursor. Combobox's trigger and the chat chrome's rail chips draw the same string.
  - **F17.** svelte-query passes a change to a component only when it touches a prop the component has already read. The roster gated on `defs.isLoading || containers.isLoading`, which never read the containers' flag while defs loaded, and its banner had already read the containers' `isError`. So when `/api/fleet/containers` answered first, the later read of `isLoading` got the value from before the answer, and the roster kept its skeletons for good. `anyLoading` / `anyPending` (`components/ui/query-state.ts`) read every flag before combining. The roster and the four other two-query gates (the boards sublist, Models → Roles and Access, Artifacts) go through them, and a unit test fails any new `a.isLoading || b.isLoading`. The same stale read held the agent memory's **Whole file** view on its skeleton whenever the read landed while **Entries** was showing, for fleet agents and the personal assistant: `useMemory` now notifies on every change.
  - **F21.** Inside a devbox the app dialled an app database at `127.0.0.1:<published port>`, the box container's own loopback, so no app's store could open. The box compose sets `TALARIA_APP_DB_NETWORK` to the box's own network: the app DB joins it with no published port, and the app dials it by container name. `TALARIA_DEVBOX` carries the box's name instead of `1`, so two boxes running one app get two databases. A host-run app dials the loopback port as before.
  - **An app DB is no longer a second `postgres`.** Its compose service was named `postgres`, and compose aliases a service by its name on every network it joins. On the image's `internal` (and a box's network) that is the platform's own database, so a lookup of `postgres` answered with both, and the platform's connections could reach an app's database and fail its password. On rc that is live for every image install with an app. The service is now named for its container. One made before this keeps the alias while it runs (`restart: unless-stopped` keeps it running), so host boot recreates each one under its own name, by docker alone and from the password in its `db.env`, before anything reads the platform's database; `appSql` checks first too. The data is a bind mount and stays.
  - **No two databases on one cluster.** A box's app now asks for `talaria-appdb-<box>-<slug>` while its database from before, `talaria-appdb-1-<slug>`, still runs on the same data directory, and starting the new one put two postmasters on one cluster. Before it starts an app DB, the host looks for other app DB containers with that app's `pg` directory mounted. In a box it stops and removes the box's own `talaria-appdb-1-<slug>`. Any other running one is refused with its name, rather than joined.
  - **`talaria box rm`** removes the box's app databases: those on its network, and those with a mount in its state (a box's databases from before the network). It empties the box's state from a root container on the box's image (`--pull never`: the image is built here and named on no registry), since an app database owns its files and the removal used to die on them with EACCES. If the directory still outlives that, it says so and exits 1 instead of printing `gone`.

  Verified:
  - **Gates.** `bun run gate` passes on the final tree, rc merged: `check`, svelte-check (5644 files, 0 errors), vitest (163 files, 2514 tests, the new suites among them), the cli's `tsc` and `bun test` (447 pass, 10 of them new in `lifecycle.test.ts`), and `cargo test -p talaria-mcp` (75) with `cargo clippy -p talaria-mcp --all-targets -D warnings`. The roster's containers-first cases and the four Whole file cases were run again on the merged tree, and all settled. CI is the full proof line.
  - **F23, in Playwright** on this worktree's stack, each surface shot disabled and enabled, with the field's computed style read back. On rc every disabled field read `opacity 1, cursor default`, the same as an enabled one. With this change all 11 read `opacity 0.5, cursor not-allowed`, and the enabled ones are unchanged. The surfaces: TaskDetail's title, estimate, start and due date for a board viewer; the Labels and Statuses rename fields (the modal opens only for an editor, so the disabled state was reached the one real way, by demoting the editor while the modal was open); TicketMuseBar while a held `/api/muse` request ran; the memory's entry Textarea and its "Remember something" field while their save was held; MaxChildrenControl while its PATCH was held; AdminOutreachPanel's interval with check-ins off. On the viewer's task page every disabled select, input and combobox trigger reads the same. Every other disabled `Input`/`Textarea`/`Select`/`Combobox` in `ui/src` goes through these primitives.
  - **F17, in Playwright** with `/api/fleet/defs` and `/api/fleet/containers` held back by route interception (8 × 8 delays from 0 to 2.5 s, plus SPA return, reload and a view toggle mid-load). On rc the roster stuck on skeletons in every scenario where containers answered first (32 to 40 of 79 across runs). With the fix, 78 of 79 settled at normal CPU. The 79th (an SPA return with no delay) had no skeletons left but its tiles were still fading in when the 2.5 s window closed, with the host at load ~20; its 15 reruns settled. At 4× CPU throttle, 63 of the 64 delay pairs settled within 5 s; the 64th was mid-transition when the window closed, the screenshot taken just after shows the roster, and its 3 reruns settled in 1.1 to 1.3 s. The Whole file view: on rc it stuck in 3 of 4 cases (each one where the read landed before the switch), and 0 of 4 with the fix. The four other gates settled in all 30 runs both before and after (6 delay pairs each, with the real responses passed through): they were latent, not live, and are converted so the rule holds everywhere. New runes-environment unit tests run real svelte-query queries in the roster's shape: the `||` gate stays loading (kept as a fact), `anyLoading` and `anyPending` let go in either order, and a `data` read made after `useMemory`'s answer gets it (that test fails without the fix).
  - **F21, in real devbox containers** made from `docker/devbox.compose.yml` the way `talaria box new` makes them, with the box's `ui/.env` from its own `boxUiEnv`. Two steps were left out: `box new` brings up the primary's postgres, and its dry run here says it would recreate the owner's `talaria-postgres-dev`; and the seed from the primary, since the probe migrates the box's empty database. The box did not join the shared embeddings network either. The probe opens an app's store through `storeFor` (`app-store.ts` → `appSql`) inside the box. On rc's template the box named its database `talaria-appdb-1-f21probe`, published it on `127.0.0.1:32815`, and failed with `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:32815`. With the network alone, the second run failed with `password authentication failed`: `postgres` resolved to both the box's database and the app DB. With the service renamed, 6 of 6 runs wrote and read back a document, the app DB's only alias is its name, `postgres` resolves to one address, and the app DB is on the box's default network only, not its fleet network. A second box running the same app got its own `talaria-appdb-fixui-f21b-f21probe` (count 1, while the first box's reached 9), and neither box resolves the other's. A host-run app (this worktree) still put its app DB on the bridge with `127.0.0.1:32816` and wrote and read back twice. `bun talaria box rm --force` removed both boxes: no containers, networks, volumes or directory left, the postgres-owned cluster included. rc's `runRm` on a staged box holding such a cluster threw EACCES and left the directory; this one removed it.
  - **F21, the image's path**, without building the image: an app container (`TALARIA_INSTALL=image`, the `HOSTNAME` self-inspect choosing the network) on a network named like the image's `<project>_internal`, beside a platform database aliased `postgres`. A running app DB made by rc's own `app-db.ts` carried the alias `postgres`, `getent ahosts postgres` gave two addresses, and 7 to 14 of 20 fresh platform connections to `postgres` failed `28P01` across five readings. The PR's head before this fix reused it as it was (13 of 20 failed). With this change the first store call recreated it (a clean shutdown, `database system was shut down at`), the document rc wrote read back, the alias is its own name, `postgres` resolves to one address, and 20 of 20 platform connections succeed; a second call recreated nothing. An exited one went through `spawnContainer`'s existing remove-and-retry, with its data. Host boot's own pass (`startAppBuilds()` over an installed app whose rc-made DB ran) recreated it before the build, which failed there for want of an api, and the store call after reused it with its data. A second instance on the same app-data directory: the PR's head started a second postmaster on the cluster (two containers running on one `pg` directory, both ready); this change refuses with the running one's name and leaves it serving.
  - **F21, a box made before this, then started on this branch's template** (`compose up -d`, what `box start` runs), in a real box from the same harness as above. On rc's template rc's code made `talaria-appdb-1-boxapp`, `-boxhead` and `-boxleft` on the bridge (each unreachable from the box). After the switch, the PR's head opening `boxhead` started `talaria-appdb-fixui-f21c-boxhead` beside the still-running `talaria-appdb-1-boxhead`: two on one cluster. This change opening `boxapp` stopped `talaria-appdb-1-boxapp` first, then wrote and read back on one. The PR head's `box rm` filter found two of the box's four app databases; this one found all four (two by the network, `talaria-appdb-1-boxleft` and `talaria-appdb-1-boxhead` by their mount), and `bun talaria box rm --force` left no container, network, volume or directory. `docker run --pull never` on an image the daemon lacks fails at once, with no pull. The product image itself was not built, and `deploy-smoke` was not run with an app installed.
  - **N5: four more surfaces left their skeletons only by luck.** F17's stale read was not only `a.isLoading || b.isLoading`. A sweep of `ui/src` found 26 short-circuits across two queries' flags, in 19 files: `||`, `&&`, `??` and ternaries over `isError` too, multi-line `$derived(...)`, `$derived` aliases, a compound alias (`const fleetFailed = $derived(fleetQuery.isError && …)` read as `fleetFailed || threadsFailed`), and a `listQuery` result's `pending`, `failed` and `notice`, which are its query's flags under other names. Four stuck for good under route interception. The board page stuck when the archived list failed before the active one answered. Board settings → Agents stuck when `/api/agents` answered before the board's policy. Board settings → General's templates stuck when the board's bindings answered before the library. Admin → Retrieval's brain binding pickers stuck on their bars when `/api/users` and `/api/teams` answered before `/api/agents`: the gate was `agentsQuery.isPending || usersList.pending || teamsList.pending`, and the directories' notices had read only their `isError`. Each now reads every flag first: `anyLoading` and `anyPending`, plus new `anyError`, `anyFailed`, `firstError` and `firstNotice`, or `[...].includes(true)` where the flags are of different kinds. So do the latent sites: the boards sublist's stale notice, `StaleBoardNotice`, `AgentsTile`, `PermissionsModal` (its principals gate and its editors branch), Models → Roles, Settings' preferred model, Files' failure notice, the board page's lookup error and facet notices, the ticket link's modal, the dock's boards search, a channel's degraded-read notice, the Comms sidebar's sections, a KB doc's attachments and the Work view's files pane. The source-scan test reads a `listQuery` result's flags as its query's, a `$derived` as the queries its body reads, and an eager helper as one read of all its queries; it flags a short-circuit whose deciding side reads one query's flag and whose other side reads a query the deciding side did not; it skips comments; and it pins each shape with its own case, PermissionsModal's and CollectionRow's original gates among them. Verified: 12 of 12 runs stuck on #624's code and 12 of 12 settled with this, three runs per case. A runes-environment test in the retrieval row's exact shape (the agents read plus two `listQuery` directories, their notices read on their own) stays on its skeleton with the `||` gate and lets go with the eager read in three orders. The 12 pages and states holding the latent sites load and reach their content with no page errors. The scan finds 26 sites on #624's base, 13 on its head before this round's review, and none now.
  - **N11: an idle page with nothing to show no longer burns the main thread.** Measured in Chromium on every page and state that mounts a `DitherEngine` field (Playwright with CDP `Performance.getMetrics` and counted canvas calls, 1440×900, DPR 1, 10 s quiet windows). A full-pane `EmptyState` kept the main thread 22–40% busy while nothing on the page changed: about 50 rAF a second, 120k–200k `fillRect` and as many `clearRect` a second, and up to 63 long tasks in 10 s. That held on Home, Work, Knowledge, Files, Agents, Teams and Apps. An idle brief's `BriefHero` kept it 21% busy. The empty state's vignette no longer shimmers and the brief's crest no longer drifts: a speed-0 wave is now a still field in the engine. So each is painted once, and repainted on a resize, a theme flip or a source change, the way #625 painted the desktop launcher. Reduced motion was already still. All seven empty states and the brief now measure 0% busy, with no rAF, fills or long tasks. The fields that move because work is in flight keep moving, at an unchanged cost and an unchanged look: a board with 2 live and 2 queued cards at 11%, the list view's strips at 29%, the agent design splash at 54% (66% before, its empty page behind it included). Found while comparing screenshots, and left as it is: the engine's incremental rewrite clears a dot over its own fractional rect, which antialiases, so a live field creeps brighter than a full rebuild of the same frame over its first seconds (4–7 times the alpha, measured on a working card's wash and a streaming tail). Clearing whole device pixels ends that, and makes every live field look fainter than it does today. That is a change of look, so it waits for the owner's call (the PR body has the numbers and the one-commit way to take it). Verified: the numbers above. Work's empty field, read off its canvas: before, its alpha grew from 1.46 times a one-shot build of the same frame at 1.5 s to 8.7 times at 5 s and 20.6 times at 15 s; now it holds 1.17 times from 1.5 s on (its fade-in's rewrites), and reduced motion paints the one-shot build, as before. `dither-engine.test.ts` (new) pins a still field parking, a speed-0 wave included, and a moving field keeping its loop until reduced motion parks it.
  - **N8: an MCP package served over HTTP starts, and answers inside a devbox.** There were two faults on one path (`talaria-mcp/src/pkg.rs`). First, `ensure_http` appended `--network talaria-mcp-<instance>` after the image, so docker handed it to the package's own command. A package that rejects unknown arguments exited at once (node: `bad option: --network`). One that ignored them ran on the default bridge, off the network the image's api dials it on. `pkg_argv` now puts the network with the flags. Second, in a box the api dialled the package's published port on loopback, which is the box container's own. Now the box (its compose sets `TALARIA_DEVBOX`) joins the package network by its own hostname and dials by container name, as the image does (`dials_by_name`). A host-run api keeps the loopback port. Verified in a real box built as F21's proof built one (`fixui-n8`, this branch's template). The probe calls `pkg::ensure_http` and sends MCP `initialize`. It ran in the box's own network namespace with the box's `HOSTNAME` and `TALARIA_DEVBOX` (a host-built binary needs glibc 2.39, and the box has 2.36), and `curl` dialled the same URL from inside the box. Before, a node package never started, and an `sh`-wrapped one ran on `bridge` behind `http://127.0.0.1:32866/mcp`, which refused both the probe and the box. With this change both ran on `talaria-mcp-fixui-n8`, the box joined it, and `http://talaria-mcp-fixui-n8-n8box:8080/mcp` answered `initialize` with 200 to the probe and to `curl`. On the host the same probe answered over `127.0.0.1:<port>` for both packages. A package also outlives the api container that started it (it has no compose label, and `box stop`/`start` leaves it running), so a recreated box container, or a replaced image container, was on none of its networks and the name did not resolve. The api now remembers, per process, the package networks it has joined, and its first relay to a package that is already running joins first: one join per api process, nothing after. Verified with the same probe from a stand-in api container (a throwaway `ubuntu:24.04` on its own user-defined network, `HOSTNAME` its id, `TALARIA_DEVBOX` set). The first relay started the package and joined. After the stand-in was recreated, #624's head returned the name URL and `initialize` failed with a DNS error; this change joined and answered 200, from the same package container. `cargo test -p talaria-mcp` (75, four new) and `cargo clippy -p talaria-mcp --all-targets -D warnings` pass; CI is the proof line for the workspace.

- **Added: an admin can disconnect the org's OAuth account from an MCP server.** Until now only deleting the server dropped an org connection. The server card's menu now offers **Disconnect org account** to admins (`DELETE /api/mcp/servers/{id}/oauth`, refused server-side to everyone else, a member who holds `agents.manage` included). It drops the sealed org tokens, clears a pending reconnect flag, and is audited as `mcp.oauth_disconnect` with the admin as the actor. The change applies in place, like the connect it undoes: the gateway answers for the server in-house again, the server's carriers re-list it on the gateway's list-changed notice, and nothing restarts. Verified live on a worktree stack with the repo's OAuth 2.1 stub (`scripts/e2e/mcp-stubs.mjs`, DCR and PKCE) and an agent on the pinned `hermes-agent:v0.22.4`, under a scripted mock model: after the org connect, a turn's `shout` reached the stub. A member holding `agents.manage` and the MCP view saw no Disconnect entry in the menu, and the route answered them 403 and kept the token. The admin's click went through the confirm (Playwright screenshots) and answered 200; the token row was gone and the audit row named the admin. Bob's next keepalive got the notice, Hermes re-listed the server, and his next call answered "The workspace's OAuth Org Stub connection isn't set up yet" with nothing reaching the stub. His container's id and start time did not change. `bun run gate` was green; CI is the full compile and test line.

- **Fixed: the app image builds again — the SDK kit's two inputs outside ui/ are back in the build context.** #604's kit build reads `cli/src/cmd/app/skeleton.ts` (the skeleton its scaffold shares with `talaria app new`) and `docs/sdk/talaria.schema.json`, and `.dockerignore` left out `cli` and `docs` whole. `bun run build` passed everywhere except inside the image, which no PR job builds, so every rc deploy from #604's merge on failed (`Could not resolve: "../../../cli/src/cmd/app/skeleton"`) and the promotion waited on a green deploy that could not come. `.dockerignore` now re-admits exactly those two files, and a new invariant, `image-build-input-ignored`, fails `bun run check` when the ui build (its non-test sources, plus the scripts its `build` runs) imports or reads a file outside ui/ that `.dockerignore` leaves out. Verified: the invariant names all four sites (pack.ts:94 and :95, scaffold.ts:6, build-sdk-kit.ts:218) against rc's `.dockerignore` and passes with this one; the image builds the way rc-deploy builds it (rc's api package, `docker build` of this branch), and `scripts/deploy-smoke.mjs` passes against it.

- **pr-watch takes the CI workflow's name from the PR's own repository, and the PR template asks for a `changelog/` file instead of a hand edit of `CHANGELOG.md`.** Before green, the watcher requires a finished run of the CI workflow for the PR's head. It used to read that workflow's name from the `ci.yml` in its working directory. So `--repo owner/name`, or a `--pr` URL from another repository, waited on a workflow that repository never runs, or silently guessed `CI` when the working directory had no `ci.yml`. The target repository is now the one the PR's URL names (gh returns that URL for the PR it found), or `--repo` when there is no URL to read. The name comes from that repository's `ci.yml` at the PR's head, read from GitHub. A `pull_request` run reads the merge commit's copy, which has the head's name unless the base renamed the workflow after the branch point. `gh run list` and the failed-job logs now query that repository too. If GitHub cannot answer, this checkout's `ci.yml` is used only when one of its remotes is the target; otherwise the watcher assumes `CI`. Either fallback is stated in the pending reason, the proof line and `--json` (`ciWorkflow.source`, `ciWorkflow.note`). A failed read is not cached, so the next poll tries again. `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` now asks for `changelog/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md` and says `CHANGELOG.md` is written only by the release roll. The `## CHANGELOG entry` heading that judge-pr reads is unchanged. Every `gh` read now names the PR's host. Each `gh api` call (the `ci.yml`, the branch's head and the compare) gets `--hostname`, and `gh run list` and `gh run view` get `--repo HOST/OWNER/REPO`. Before, the branch-head and compare reads named no host, so gh sent a GitHub Enterprise PR's reads to github.com, and a `GH_HOST` naming another host moved a github.com PR's reads (its runs included) there. Closes follow-ups R25 and S21.

  Verified:
  - **Gates.** `bun run check` and `bun run gate` pass. `scripts/hooks/pr-watch.test.mjs` now has 45 checks (up from 32), and `scripts/judge-pr.test.mjs` has 19 (up from 18). Both also pass under node.
  - **Tests.** The new checks cover:
    - every repository spelling gh and git use;
    - the PR's URL taking precedence over a `--repo` that disagrees, and `--repo` used when there is no URL;
    - the read at the PR head, including the exact `gh api` call, and the cwd's `ci.yml` left unread;
    - a GitHub Enterprise host;
    - each fallback and the note it carries;
    - the host on every `gh api` call (github.com included) and on every `--repo`, and a GitHub Enterprise PR's compare and branch-head reads sent to its own host.
  - **End to end.** One check runs the real watcher in a scratch git repository with a fake `gh` on PATH. The scratch `ci.yml` says `Local CI`, and the target's says `Pipeline`. The watcher goes green on `Pipeline`, both with `--repo` and with a bare PR URL, and sends `--repo` to `gh run list`. With the target unreadable, it reports a stated `CI` guess and never `Local CI`. With a remote that names the target, it uses `Local CI` and says so. With `--repo wrong-org/wrong-repo --pr <other-org/other-repo URL>`, the fake gh serves the URL's PR, as real gh does (checked: `gh pr view https://github.com/outcrop-labs/talaria/pull/620 --repo cli/cli` answers with #620's URL). The watcher reads `other-org/other-repo`'s `ci.yml`, sends that repository to `gh run list`, and goes green on `Pipeline`. The previous head of this change read the flag's repository there and waited on a guessed `CI`.
  - **The host, end to end.** A second check runs the real watcher off the PR's branch, so all of its `gh` reads happen, against a fake `gh` that picks a host the way gh does (`--hostname` or `--repo`'s host, else `GH_HOST`, else github.com) and answers only on the PR's host. A GitHub Enterprise PR, and a github.com PR under `GH_HOST=ghe.example.invalid`, both go green, with `--hostname <host>` on both `gh api` reads and `--repo <host>/<owner>/<repo>` on `gh run list`. Mutations: dropping the host from the branch-head read, from the compare, from github.com, or from `--repo` failed 2, 2, 5 and 2 named checks.
  - **The host, live.** Run from this worktree against #616 with `GH_HOST=ghe.example.invalid`, the previous head printed `pending … could not read the pushed head of wt/fu-devtools: error connecting to ghe.example.invalid`; this one printed `green … CI run settled, mergeable=MERGEABLE at 9a0c0a054124`. Without `GH_HOST` it is green too, with the CI name read from GitHub. A real GitHub Enterprise host was not available; that case is covered by the fake `gh` only.
  - **Mutations.** Each change below was made on a scratch copy, and named tests failed for each:
    - the cwd's `ci.yml` winning (the reported bug): 6 tests failed;
    - runs not sent to the target repository;
    - a fallback with no note;
    - the local copy used without a matching remote;
    - the PR URL not treated as a target;
    - `--repo` winning over the PR URL: 2 tests failed.

    The template test fails on rc's checklist line.
  - **Before and after.** Same fake setup, from a clone whose `ci.yml` says `Local CI`. rc's watcher printed `pending — no Local CI workflow run … yet`. This branch's printed `green … Pipeline run settled`.
  - **Live.** The watcher ran against #615 on GitHub, from a directory that is not a checkout (so it has no `ci.yml`), with `--repo outcrop-labs/talaria` and again with a bare PR URL. Both printed `green`. The JSON read `ciWorkflow: {name: "CI", source: "outcrop-labs/talaria@e6742a8dfa7c", note: ""}`, so the name was read from GitHub at the PR head, not guessed.

- **Fixed: the MCP gateway no longer logs an upstream error for the probe Hermes sends before every connect. A terminal-less agent whose browser is a CDP endpoint supplied as a `BROWSER_CDP_URL` secret keeps its browser.** Before each `initialize`, Hermes v0.22.4 probes an HTTP server's URL (`_preflight_content_type` in tools/mcp_tool_transport.py) so that a URL pointing at a web page fails fast. The probe is a HEAD (a GET on 405 or 501) carrying the server's configured headers, httpx's default `Accept: */*`, and no session. A streamable-HTTP server answers it 406 (*Client must accept text/event-stream*) or 405, and Hermes goes on to connect. The gateway relayed that answer and logged `WARN [upstream] mcp-gw-get:<server> 406` (or `405`, twice for the toolkit) on every agent start and every reconnect. That one shape, answered 405 or 406, now logs at debug. Anything else still logs at warn: a request with a session or one that asks for `text/event-stream` (a real notification stream), a probe answered with any other status, and an upstream that cannot be reached. Separately, the render closes the `browser` toolset for an agent whose terminal is closed when the browser its config picks is one Hermes runs locally, without its private-address check (#621). It read a CDP endpoint only from `browser.cdp_url`, so a def with `backend: off` whose endpoint arrives as a `BROWSER_CDP_URL` secret had its browser closed. Hermes reads that env name first (`_get_cdp_override_raw`) and keeps its check for it. The render (`hermes_browser`) and the toolset grid's note (`authoredBrowser`, given the agent's secret names when the viewer may read them) now read that secret as the CDP endpoint, the same as `browser.cdp_url`. A hosted provider's credentials (`BROWSER_USE_API_KEY`, `BROWSERBASE_API_KEY` with `BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID`) are not read, because they cannot be an agent's secret: they are refused on write and skipped at materialize, so Hermes's auto-detect never finds them in an agent's env. A new test pins that, so the render has to start reading them if the rule ever changes. Camofox closing on a terminal-less agent (#621 decision 8) is unchanged.
  - **Verified (probe):** the pinned `hermes-agent:v0.22.4` agent on a worktree stack, connected through the gateway to a real streamable-HTTP server built on the MCP SDK 1.29 that logs every request it receives. **No real model was called.**
    - On rc's gateway, an agent restart logged `WARN [upstream] mcp-gw-get:probecap 406: {… Not Acceptable: Client must accept text/event-stream …}` and `mcp-gw-get:talaria 405` twice. The server saw `GET /mcp accept="*/*" session=-` → 406, then `initialize`, `notifications/initialized` and `tools/list`.
    - On this branch, the same restart logged only `DEBUG … the agent's preflight probe: upstream answered 406` (and 405 for the toolkit), and Hermes connected the same way.
    - Through the gateway with the agent's own key: the probe shape answered 406 logs at debug. A stream request with an unknown session (400), a stream request to the toolkit (405), a probe-shaped request carrying a session (406), and a probe while the server was down (unreachable) each still logged at warn.
  - **Verified (browser):** the same agent, terminal closed, with `browser: {backend: off}` written as its version, then rendered through `POST /api/fleet/render`, reading back the agent's `config.yaml`:
    - On rc, with a `BROWSER_CDP_URL` secret (it reaches `secrets.env` and `terminal.env_passthrough`), `browser` was still in `agent.disabled_toolsets`.
    - On this branch, with that secret the browser stays open. Without it, or with only `BROWSERBASE_BASE_URL`, it is closed.
    - `cloud_provider: camofox` is closed without the secret, and left alone with it, as Hermes's `is_camofox_mode` gives way to a CDP override.
    - The secrets route refuses `BROWSER_USE_API_KEY`, `BROWSERBASE_API_KEY`, `BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID` and `CAMOFOX_URL`, and accepts `BROWSER_CDP_URL`.
  - **Tests:** unit tests cover every case of the probe predicate (`only_the_preflight_answered_405_or_406_is_quiet`), the CDP secret in the render (`hermes_default_and_a_remote_browser_are_left_alone`), the refused credential names (`the_browser_selecting_names_a_secret_can_carry_are_the_ones_read`), and the grid's reading and note (`toolsets.test.ts`).
  - **Gates.** `bun run gate` passed. It ran check, svelte-check and the ui vitest, plus clippy `-D warnings` and `cargo test` for `talaria-fleet-render` and `talaria-routes-fleet`, with `-p` only. CI runs the full surface jobs.

- **Fixed: rolls and agent controls say what really happened.** A roll whose fresh container boots slower than the roll's three-minute health wait no longer ends `failed`: its roll-picture row stays *rolling*, noted *still starting* (the roster's chip reads **starting**), and turns `done` when the container reports healthy, or `failed` with the reason only if it is not up within twelve more minutes or stays down for 30 s on its own; a stop or retire asked while it starts turns the row `idle` at once instead, and a wait docker never answers says so rather than calling the container not running. A *starting* agent's roll has let go of its locks, so its **Roll** control and **Roll all** stay enabled (the picture's `rolling` flag leaves it out), and a row whose watcher died with an api restart drops off the picture once the late wait could no longer be running. The roster reads each agent's own row, so an agent left out of a shared department no longer wears the runner's chip; an apply that rolled such a container answers applied, with a note, and the control route, the fleet roll and the MCP queue audit `roll_failed` only for a late wait that fails. A stop or retire sent to a legacy `-b` agent while its roll moved it home used to stop nothing (it addressed the home service, which had no container yet) and the roll then started the home container: the move now holds a per-department lock every control verb waits for, and a stop that arrives during it leaves the agent in `-b` and stops it there. The fleet roll queues one roll per department, the agent that runs in its container, and names an agent left out of a shared department as skipped (the left-out agent's roll used to take the department and the runner's was audited as failed); the roll picture reads that agent idle. The config seal reports `rolled: false` for an agent that stopped between its report and its roll, and removes that stopped container like any stopped one, so its next start holds the sealed secrets. `POST /api/fleet/defs/{id}/mcp` answers a roll step that throws with 200 `applied: false` and `warning: "the roll failed — …"`, as the edit route does, instead of a bare 400 after the change was saved. A **Save & apply** with nothing changed now says whether the agent runs the current version (`inEffect`): a version saved without an apply, or one whose roll did not land, keeps even a freshly opened form open with *Version N is not applied:* and why; a running agent on the current version, or a stopped one, closes quietly as before. A control answered 202 (the verb outlived the route's 210 s answer) leaves a *still stopping* / *still starting* note on the agent's row until the roster shows the new state. The generated reference reads the control route's real answer shapes (the generator falls back to the `Json(json!({…}))` shapes of a handler's same-file helpers), which also fills in `PUT /api/admin/model-roles`, `/api/me/assistant`, `POST /api/boards/{id}/agent-requests` and `POST /api/secrets/share`. Verified on a worktree stack with three agents on the pinned Hermes image and a scripted mock model (no real model calls), each item first reproduced on rc's own binary: a roll onto a Hermes image that boots 240 s late read `failed` on rc for good after the container came up healthy, and with this change read `still starting` at 180 s and `done` when it came up, with no `roll_failed` audit; a Save & apply onto it answered `applied: true` with the still-starting note in 189 s; a roll onto an image that never boots ended `failed` after the late wait. With a real legacy `agent-ops-b` slot and the move's image pull held by a docker shim, a stop on rc answered 200 in 0.2 s and the agent ended running in its home container; with this change the stop waited for the move, the agent stayed in `-b` and stopped there, and a stop already in flight when a roll started left the slot untouched; a plain roll still moved `-b` home. A fleet roll over a seeded pair queued `pipdup` and `pipz` on rc (and audited the runner's roll as failed), and with this change queued only the runner. A seal whose agent was stopped during its held roll said `rolled: true` on rc and left the container without the secret; now `rolled: false, removed: true` (audited `removedStoppedContainer: true`), and the next start held it. The MCP route's thrown roll answered 400 on rc and now 200 with the warning, the assignment written. Every no-op Save & apply case read back: in effect, stopped, never applied, a roll that did not land, docker silent, a left-out agent; the form kept open and closed in Playwright. A start whose image pull was held past 210 s showed nothing on rc's UI and *still starting* with this change, cleared once the agent ran (screenshots). F1 and F5 needed no change: on rc, rolling def edits leave a `start: false` hire and a stopped hire stopped, and every personal-assistant edit (personality, name, handle, model tier) applies to a running assistant and leaves a stopped one stopped. #614's per-server tool-list counts were exercised live from every team change (agent add and remove, member add and remove, team delete) and from an app catalog change: each moved only the team's or the app's server count, and the agent's next keepalive carried `tools/list_changed` and Hermes re-listed. `bun run gate` was green (check, svelte-check, vitest, clippy `-D warnings` and cargo tests for the touched crates); CI is the full compile and test line.

- **Fixed: Stop now halts a completions-arm chat turn in the agent itself, not just the stream. A malformed id in a route path now answers 404 instead of a 500 or the database's own error text. Two smaller fixes: agent transport errors share one wording that never names the agent's address, and the abandoned-turn guard's log says whether a turn was interrupted mid-run or cancelled while still queued.** Before, `POST /api/conversations/{id}/stop` answered `hermes: false` for a turn on the completions arm (the chat default). The client hung up its copy of the stream, the server's drain kept reading, and the agent worked and spent until the end of a reply nobody wanted. While the drain holds the turn's request open, the completion id its stream names (`chatcmpl-…`) is also the turn's Hermes run id. So the drain now records it (talaria-chat-persist `open_completion`), and the stop posts `POST /v1/runs/{id}/stop` for it. That interrupts a running turn, or withdraws one still queued in its Hermes session. A stop Hermes cannot place yet is sent again within the control window. Hermes ends the stream with a `cancelled` finish, which the parser now reads the same way as a session's `run.cancelled`: the row lands `complete` with `stopped: true` and keeps the words streamed so far. Thirty-nine route methods that cast a path id with `$N::uuid` used to answer 500 for a malformed id (an admin passed every gate in front of the cast). Eight more passed the database's error text through as a 400: an agent's cron list, cron create and cron-job actions, its secret write, and its memory. Two answered 200 for an agent that cannot exist (its secrets list and delete), and the agent's Google connect would have answered 500 once Google is configured. All 50 now answer 404. On most of them that is also the answer for a well-formed id that names nothing. Where a route answers such an id its own way (a 403 that never says whether the row exists, an empty list, an idempotent ok, or *not a running managed agent*), a malformed id still gets the 404: no row can have it, so the 404 tells a caller nothing the 403 hides. Each gate runs after the route asks who is calling, so a caller with no session hears what it hears for any other id. They are listed in the PR. The uuid shape check now lives in one place, `talaria_params::uuid_shaped`. It is Postgres' own uuid input rule, so the old `Uuid::parse_str` gates stop passing the `urn:uuid:` form the cast refuses. The two private copies (talaria-conversations' `uuid_shaped`, talaria-routes-comms' `could_be_uuid`) are gone. Six of them (`GET` and `POST /api/fleet/defs/{id}/mcp`, `PATCH /api/fleet/defs/{id}`, its `edit` and `rotate-key`, and `POST /api/fleet/agents/{id}/control`) were held back while their files belonged to #614. That PR has now landed, and they are gated too. The approval door and the abandoned-turn guard used to build their own agent transport errors. They now use `fleet_chat::transport_error`, so an `agent.approval_*` audit row or a stop refusal never names the container's dial URL. The Rust harness's `LedgerAttribution.tier` had no reader anywhere in api, ui, mcp, desktop, cli, mobile, scripts or the client apps, so it is gone. The guard logged a turn cancelled while queued as `(chatcmpl-…: stopped)`, because Hermes answers that stop with `null`. It now says *cancelled in the agent while still queued: it never ran*, or *interrupted in the agent while it ran* for a running turn.

  Verified:
  - **Stop, verified live.** Tested on a worktree stack with the pinned `hermes-agent:v0.22.4` image, the agent `ada-ops` on the completions arm, and a scripted mock model behind the stack's gateway. The mock streams `tick n` once a second for 40 s. **No real model was called.**
    - Control run, hanging up with no stop (what Stop did on this arm before): the model call ran all 40 ticks to the end, the admission was `completed`, and the whole reply landed.
    - With Stop: the route answered `{"ok":true,"hermes":true}` in 47 ms. The api logged *a person's stop: the turn was interrupted in the agent while it ran*. The client's stream ended with `finish_reason: "cancelled"`. The mock saw Hermes hang up 3.2 s later, at tick 7. The admission was `interrupted`, and the row is `complete`, `stopped: true`, with *working: tick 1 tick 2 tick 3 tick 4*.
    - Stop followed at once by a hang-up, the way the page does it: the mock saw the hang-up 2.2 s later, at tick 5.
    - A turn queued in Hermes: a direct turn on the thread's own derived session held the head, and the chat turn queued behind it. Stop logged *cancelled in the agent while still queued: it never ran*. Its admission was `cancelled`, the head kept running, and the mock never received the queued turn.
    - In Playwright: Stop pressed while ticks were on screen was answered 5 ms after the click. The mock saw the hang-up 2.6 s later, and the bubble reads *working: tick 1 tick 2 tick 3 tick 4 · stopped*. A Stop 150 ms after sending interrupted the turn before its model call.
  - **The guard's log, live.** A throwaway local app drove app turns on `ada-ops`; it was never committed and was uninstalled with `wipeData`. A queued app turn whose caller gave up was logged 18 ms later as *a turn its reader let go of was cancelled in the agent while still queued: it never ran (chatcmpl-907fa…)*, and its admission was `cancelled`. A running one was logged as *was interrupted in the agent while it ran*, and the mock saw Hermes hang up 2.2 s later.
  - **Malformed ids, swept live.** Every path-param route of the router was driven with a malformed id, as the admin and with an agent's key. Where an id sits under a parent, it was driven under a real channel, thread, agent and workchain. Routes that validate the body first got a valid body. Every converted route now answers 404, and on rc with #611, #614, #617, #618 and #621 merged in, the sweep finds no route that answers 500 or the database's text for a malformed id. The new live test `malformed_path_ids` (tests/it) drives all 50 converted methods, plus the folded `GET /api/conversations/{id}`, with three malformed spellings. It asserts a plain 404 with no database error, and checks that well-formed, upper-case, braced and hyphen-less absent ids still reach the read. With one gate taken out, it fails on that route's 500. A third test sends every one of those methods with no session and asserts a malformed id answers exactly what a well-formed absent id does. It caught `POST`/`DELETE /api/artifacts/{id}/links` answering 404 before the 401 (their gate ran before the route's own auth): it fails on those six requests with the old order and passes now. Over HTTP on the worktree api, both methods answer 401 with no session for a malformed, truncated, `urn:` or absent id, 404 to an admin for each, and a real artifact still links and unlinks (the `artifact_links` row was read back, then gone). New unit tests cover the shape check against Postgres' input rule, the parser naming its completion and reading a `cancelled` finish, the open-completion registry, each answer Hermes gives a stop, the stop's resend, and a refused agent in both the approval door and the guard (no address, port, `for url` or path in the text).
  - **Gates.** `bun run gate` was run on the final tree. CI is the proof line for the workspace graph, because `api/Cargo.lock` changed.

- **Fixed: a Stop pressed right after sending now halts the turn: on a thread that exists, from the moment the api has read the send and checked the caller's access, and on a new thread's first message, as soon as the response names the thread. A write to a well-formed id that names nothing answers 404, never 200 or the database's own text.** Stop used to miss a turn that had not yet named itself to Hermes, which covers everything from the send to the first chunk of its stream. The page offers Stop at once, so this was a real case. A Stop before the reply row existed answered 409 *nothing is streaming*. After the row existed but before the first chunk, it answered `hermes: false`. Either way the turn ran to the end. The send now claims its thread as soon as it has checked the caller's access (talaria-chat-persist `OpeningTurn`). The drain then fills in the reply row and the turn's handle: the completion id, or a session's run id. A Stop that finds the turn unnamed waits for that handle, for up to the 10 s control window, and then stops the turn. An agent that has not opened the turn's stream within the window gets the stop held: the route answers `{"ok":true,"hermes":false,"held":true}`, and the drain sends the stop the moment the turn names itself. A thread with nothing in flight still answers 409 at once, and so does a Stop that reaches the api before it has read the send and checked access: a few milliseconds for a typical message, longer for a very large paste. A new thread's first message had a second gap, in the page. Its id reaches the page only with the response headers, which the api sends once the agent has taken the turn. A Stop pressed before them sent no stop at all, and the page's hang-up ended the very request that would have named the thread, so the turn ran to the end. The page now freezes the transcript at once and keeps that request open. It sends the stop the moment the response names the thread, then hangs up (ui `stopOnceNamed`). Until then the composer keeps its stop face, and a message sent meanwhile is held and queued behind the stopped turn, as any message sent before a first turn has its id. The wait is bounded by the api's own: it answers a send within two minutes for an agent that is coming up, and within five for one that has gone quiet. Five write routes are also fixed:
  - `PUT /api/fleet/agents/{id}/secrets` with an id no agent has used to answer 400 with the foreign key's refusal (*secret write failed: error returned from database: …*). It now answers 404. A failure to seal or write is a logged 500, never the database's text.
  - `PUT /api/workflows/{id}` now answers 404 for an id no workflow has, including an empty patch. A malformed id gets the workflows family's own 400 (*not a uuid*), empty patch included.
  - `PUT` and `DELETE /api/fleet/endpoints/{id}` now answer 404, and any spelling Postgres' uuid input takes still reaches the endpoint. A malformed id with a field to write had been a 500.
  - `DELETE /api/workbench/coding/login/{id}` for a session this instance is not running now answers 404 *unknown login session*, as its poll and its answer already did.
  - 404 is the DELETE answer these routes' siblings give for an id they address directly: blueprints, tasks, templates, MCP servers and git hosts.

  The cron routes, the conversation schedule routes and the memory routes used to hand a database failure up as a 400 carrying sqlx's text. Their stores now log it and hand up a fixed sentence, which the routes answer as the house 500 (`talaria_error::store_fault` / `store_answer`). The agent edit route (`POST /api/fleet/defs/{id}/edit`) and the personal assistant's model change (`PATCH /api/me/assistant`) did the same with a failed endpoint-registry read, and now answer the house 500 too. A render or apply failure can still carry database text into the edit route's `warning`, the defs MCP route's 400 and the endpoints route's *re-render failed (…)*: the render's errors come from about 40 sites, and the PR names it as the one deliberate exception. `docs/API-CONVENTIONS.md` now writes down both rules: a well-formed path id that names nothing is a 404 (outside the *forbidden, not hidden* families), and a database error is never a 400's message. The three remaining uuid-shape copies (talaria-agent-managers, talaria-chips, talaria-realtime-watch) are now `talaria_params::uuid_shaped`. Where chips keys a conversation or a document by its text, it uses the new `uuid_canonical`, so every spelling the cast takes is one key. talaria-channels' `is_channel_id` stays hyphenated-only on purpose.

  Verified:
  - **Stop at once, verified live.** Same stack and mock as above (the pinned `hermes-agent:v0.22.4`, `ada-ops`, a scripted model that streams `tick n` once a second; **no real model was called**). On this PR's previous head, e34f8bc4:
    - A Stop sent 0 ms and 20 ms after the send answered 409 in 11–34 ms, before the reply row existed. Those turns ran all 40 ticks.
    - Stops at 30, 40 and 150 ms arrived after the first chunk, which came at 26–38 ms, and they worked.
    - A Stop 2 s into a send whose agent was paused answered `{"ok":true,"hermes":false}`. That turn ran to the end too, and its row landed `complete` and not stopped.
    - On the host that day the first chunk took 26 ms to 1.5 s to arrive.
  - **On the new code:**
    - Stops at 0, 10, 40, 75, 150 and 400 ms all answered `hermes: true`. All six rows are `complete` and `stopped: true`, and Hermes recorded every admission `interrupted`. The 150 ms one never reached the model. No model call ran to its end.
    - A Stop with the agent paused past the window answered `held: true` at 10 s. The agent opened the turn at 13 s, the drain sent the held stop, and Hermes interrupted the turn before its model call. The mock never received it, and the row is stopped.
    - An idle thread answers 409 in 12 ms.
    - In Playwright, the page's own Stop (Esc pressed with no delay after Enter) went out 19 ms after the send and was answered `{"ok":true,"hermes":true}`. Hermes hung up the model call at tick 3, and after a reload the bubble reads *Operation interrupted: waiting for model response (0.3s elapsed) · stopped*.
  - **A new thread's first message, in Playwright on the real page** (Esc pressed with no delay after Enter, each run on a fresh thread; same stack and mock):
    - On this PR's previous head, 94fdd786, the page sent no stop. The Esc came 22 ms after the send and the response headers 2 ms later, after the page had hung up. The turn ran all 40 ticks, Hermes recorded the admission `completed`, and the row landed `complete` with every tick and not stopped.
    - On the new code, four runs had the Esc before the headers (11–12 ms after the send, the headers at 19–420 ms). Each time the page sent the stop within 2 ms of the headers, and it was answered `{"ok":true,"hermes":true}`. Hermes interrupted each turn before its model call (*Stopped before this turn started*), and the mock never received one. The rows are `complete` and `stopped: true`, and the page's address names the thread.
    - With the agent paused, so the headers came late (1.2 s, 2.9 s and 14.8 s after the send): the stop went out within 1 ms of the headers each time, and was answered `hermes: true`. The first was interrupted before its model call; the other two after one tick. A screenshot taken while the page waited shows the bubble already reading *· stopped*, with the composer still on its stop face.
    - A first version of this fix gave up waiting after 10 s. With the agent paused for 18 s it hung up at 10 s without a stop, and that turn ran all 40 ticks. The wait now follows the api's bound instead, and the 14.8 s run above is that case.
    - A second message sent while the stop waited was held, then queued (202) beside the stop when the headers came. The first turn was stopped, and the second message was answered by its own turn.
    - On a thread that already had its id, the stop still goes out at the Esc (16 ms after the send) and was answered `hermes: true`; Hermes cancelled the turn while it was still queued.
  - **The 404s, verified live:**
    - Over HTTP, every route above answers 404 with no database text, for the plain, upper-case, braced and hyphen-less spellings of an absent id.
    - A real workflow, endpoint and agent take their writes in every spelling, and the rows were read back. The endpoint's audit row names its own id.
    - A deleted endpoint's second DELETE is a 404.
    - A refused secret name is still the route's 400.
    - With a column renamed on this worktree's own database to force the fault, and then restored, the cron list and create and the memory read and write answered `500 Internal Server Error`, with the full sqlx error in the server log. A secret write forced to fail the same way did too.
    - The edit route and the assistant's model change, with a fault on the endpoint registry's re-read: one column `list_endpoints` reads was renamed for two requests, after a warm cache let the edit's first read through and its auto-registered model dropped the cache. On this PR's previous head both answered 400 *error returned from database: column "model_efforts" does not exist*. Now both answer `500 Internal Server Error`, and the log carries *[agent-defs] endpoint registry read failed: …*. No version was written. With the column restored, the same edit lands as a new version and the assistant's change answers 200; a missing endpoint and an unknown tier still answer their 400s.
    - The new live test `absent_path_ids` (tests/it) covers all of these.
    - `malformed_path_ids` raced itself: the tests in a module run concurrently, and each one's sweep deleted a sibling's admin. It now tags its rows per test, and it passed three runs in a row. `secret_delete_live`, `conversation_schedules_live`, `agent_managers` and `chips_landing_live` pass.
  - **Unit tests:** `stopOnceNamed` sends the stop and then hangs up, sends nothing for a queued ack, hangs up once at its bound, and does nothing after a cancel; the canonical text against Postgres 16's own cast of each spelling; the opening registry, the wait, and a held stop sent exactly once; the chips hint and file keys across spellings; the store fault's 500; and `apply_config_edits` handing up the fault sentence, not the pool's or the database's text, when its registry read fails (it fails on the old line).

- **Fixed: a devbox's api now runs with the box's own `ui/.env` block; `box new` from a worktree no longer fails at its install; a box no longer inherits the primary's app data and build directories (UB1, UB2).** The Rust api reads no `.env` file, and in a box nothing else handed it the block `box new` writes: the box compose's environment carries only `TALARIA_DEVBOX` and the app database network, `box enter` sources nothing, and the devbox branch of `talaria dev` skips the S3 lift. So a box's api read `TALARIA_AGENT_DIAL` as unset, took its fleet and apps dirs from its cwd (`/work/talaria/fleet`, a path only the box container has, so every agent bind it rendered named a host path that did not exist), handed agents the host's MCP gateway URL, and dialled qdrant, embeddings and object storage on its own loopback. `talaria dev` now lifts every line of the block the api reads, for the box's own stack only (a `ui/.env` with the block's `TALARIA_DEVBOX` and no `TALARIA_WORKTREE`), and a cli test reads the api's sources so a block key the api reads cannot be left out. A primary's or a worktree's api is handed none of those lines, as before: a worktree's `ui/.env` is the primary's copied, so a `TALARIA_APPS_DIR` or `TALARIA_UPLOADS_DIR` set there by hand would otherwise point the worktree's api at the primary's apps, app databases and uploads. `boxUiEnv` also drops `TALARIA_APP_DATA_DIR` and `TALARIA_APP_BUILDS_DIR`, which both readers then derive from the box's `TALARIA_APPS_DIR`. Found while proving it: a `talaria worktree` checkout links `ui/node_modules` to the primary's, `box new` copied the link itself, and in the box it dangled, so `bun install` failed and `box new` removed the partial box; it now copies what each tree resolves to. Verified: `bun run gate`; `bun test` for the cli (the new tests fail with the old list, the old strip, and the lift before it was limited to a box: a primary's hand-set dirs and service lines reach neither its own api nor a worktree's, nor a worktree cut inside a box); rc's and this branch's `apiEnv` over a real box's `ui/.env` and its container environment (rc hands the api none of the block's dial, dirs, gateway or service addresses; this branch hands it all of them); `box new` from this worktree, which failed at its install before the snapshot fix and completes with it; in that box, its api's process environment carried every block line, and an agent hired there (the pinned `nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.22.4@sha256:7a69…`, a scripted mock model, no real model calls) was rendered with no published port, every bind under the box's state directory, and a manifest row of `http://agent-dialprobe2:8642`, through which the box's api read the agent's own job list, and which the box reached by name; `talaria-postgres-dev` kept its id and start time across both `box new` runs and `box rm`, which then left nothing of the box.
- **Fixed: an MCP package's container and network outlived the worktree or box that started them, and the cleanup sweep never saw them (UB3).** Both are made outside any compose project. The api now labels them with their owner (`talaria.mcp.instance`, `talaria.mcp.owner`, and for a worktree `talaria.mcp.checkout`, the checkout it runs from), and `bun talaria cleanup` lists a package container, and its network once nothing else names it, whose sibling `talaria-<name>` checkout is gone or whose box has no `box.env`. `--apply` removes them after re-inspecting each by id; the stop gate never does. One with no labels, made before this change, is named in the report and left alone. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-mcp` and `bun scripts/cleanup-sweep.test.mjs` (51 checks); live, the stack's api labelled the package container and network it started, and the sweep's own inventory and executor placed and removed test packages of a deleted checkout and a box with no `box.env` while keeping a live worktree's, an unlabelled pair, and a network a bystander container still named (rc's sweep listed none of them).
- **Changed: the one host directory the api binds itself, when an app's data is removed, is mounted with `--mount type=bind`, which refuses a source the daemon's host lacks instead of creating it as an empty root-owned directory (UB4).** No product code mounts a CA bundle: the directory #624's proof left at `/etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt` came from that proof's own stand-in container, and a package's `-v` and `--mount` are refused for any host path, a CA bundle included (new test cases). The daemon behaviour is reachable from product code only where the api's view of a path differs from the host's, the box case UB1 fixes. Verified: under `/tmp/talaria-r6-ui-ub4-*` only, `-v` with a missing source made a root-owned directory and `--mount` in the api's exact quoted form refused it and created nothing, and removed a real directory's contents, a comma in its path included; `cargo test -p talaria-apps`.
- **Changed: every dither field on a page now rides one shared frame request instead of one rAF loop each, painting exactly the same pixels (UB5).** A board with four working cards woke the page 480 times a second to paint at about 12 Hz; it is now 60, and 360 to 60 with two live and two queued. A field that throws stops only itself, as its own loop did, and its error is still reported. Verified: rc's engine and this one driven by one hand-stepped clock in real Chromium canvases, 12 fields (the board's washes and traces, a shimmer, tweens, a mask, reduced motion, a destroy and a late mount), every canvas hashed after each of 400 frames at DPR 1 and 2: 0 frames differ, 130 distinct pictures each, rAF requests 3,060 to 400; the same harness catches a 1 ms change to the wave clock (389 frames differ); live board measurements in Playwright; `dither-engine.test.ts` (4 new cases, the thrower's failing on the ticker without its guard).
- **Fixed: `ui/src/sdk/testing.test.ts` timed out under heavy host IO (UB7).** Each of four tests rewrote the same three doc-example files before importing them, and on XFS closing a truncated file starts its writeback: one rewrite waited 37 s on the disk, measured, against under 2 ms for a write to a new file. The files are written once, to new files, and shared. Verified: the old and new files interleaved under the same host load (old 109 ms to 1.18 s of test time, new 109 to 131 ms); vitest.

- **Added: the desktop app suspends an instance you have not had on screen for a while, and brings back the exact page the moment you return to it.** Every opened instance used to keep its webview, and with it a WebKit web process, for the life of the app: 25 opened instances held 4.35 GB. Now an instance that has been off screen for the timeout (10 minutes by default; Off, 5, 10, 30 or 60 minutes in the launcher and in Settings → Profile) has its webview closed, and the same 25 drop to 0.7 GB once suspended. The instance the window shows counts only while the window is minimized or hidden, never when it is merely unfocused, so a page on a second monitor stays. Showing a suspended instance by any route recreates it at once, with no probe, at its last path, query and hash, with its sessionStorage and scroll put back: a launcher row, the in-app switcher, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+H then a row, the window restored, or a relaunch (each instance's last page is kept on disk now, so a relaunch returns there too; sign-in and callback pages are never kept). A notification click opens the notification's own page. A page holding input a reload would lose is not suspended: text typed, a select or checkbox changed, or an attachment uploaded and not yet sent (the chat composer's text does not count: ui keeps the draft). Input inside an embedded frame, such as an artifact preview, cannot be seen. An instance whose Talaria predates this is not suspended either. While an instance is suspended, the shell posts its notifications itself, with that instance's own session, exactly as the page would have. If the shell cannot read them the way the page does, or within 30 s, the page stays, and a page on its way out is never asked twice. The session survives because ui's cookie is persistent. Separately, on GTK under Wayland the OS titlebar now shows "Talaria — <instance>" instead of always "Talaria". Verified on a headless rig (mutter on Wayland and Xwayland, WebKitGTK 2.52, WebKitWebDriver, a mock D-Bus notification server, mutter RemoteDesktop for real keys and clicks), against the production build and the unmodified rc build on the same host. 25 mock instances were measured process by process before and after. Every restore path was run on mock instances, with the URL compared before and after and window captures under X11. On the worktree's real Talaria UI, signed in inside the shell, the launcher row, the in-app switcher, Ctrl+Shift+H, a notification click and a relaunch were run, and so were a composer draft across a suspend, typed input keeping a page, and Off. Notifications were posted from a suspended instance on the real UI, and a banner click restored it at the notification's page. On screen but unfocused, minimized by the window manager, minimized by the shell, and restored by a taskbar or a banner were each run. The Wayland title was read through AT-SPI on both builds. After review, the rig was run again on the fixed build. On the real UI, a Comms channel with an uploaded, unsent attachment was kept 75 s off screen, and once the attachment was removed it was suspended at 65 s. On the same real UI in the shell's WebKit, a select picked, and the TLS checkbox toggled on its own, each counted as input, and each put back did not. These were driven through WebKit's own events, not real keys. A mock instance whose notifications read takes 12 s was read once and closed once, where the earlier build read it three times. One taking 45 s was kept at the 30 s bound and not asked again. The shell's own minimize on Wayland still suspended the instance on screen at 61 s. `bun run gate` ran `check`, ui svelte-check and 2539 vitest tests (18 new) green, then stopped at its desktop cargo step, which cannot build on this host (it has no GTK or WebKit headers). The same desktop commands ran in the devbox image instead: `cargo fmt --check` and clippy `--all-targets -D warnings` clean, and the test binary built there passed 64 of 64 (27 new) run on the host. Desktop svelte-check was clean. Nothing was run by hand on macOS or Windows: the packaging workflow's 20 s launch check is the only proof there, and CI is the full compile and test line.

- **Fixed: agent controls, config saves and starts say what happened.** A refused or failed control on the Agents roster (start, stop, restart, roll, retire, re-hire, delete) now shows the route's own sentence in a notice, *Could not stop Bob* with why (a 503 whose outcome docker has not confirmed reads *the stop is not confirmed yet*); it used to resolve into nothing, so the roster sat unchanged with no word of why. A **Save & apply** (or an MCP change) whose roll outlives three and a half minutes — a slow recreate and its health check — is answered 202 with the version saved, and the form says *Saved as version N. Applying it is taking longer…* and stays open (a no-op one, applying a version saved earlier, says *Applying version N is taking longer…*), while the roster notes the agent *still applying* until the verdict of a roll that began after the request went out is in; an MCP change saved without an apply answers within the same bound while its render goes on; the app proxy used to cut that request off at 300 s with a 502, and the form showed `[object Object]` for a save that had landed. A **Save & apply** with nothing changed now puts the current version on an agent that does not run it (a version saved without an apply, or one whose roll did not land): it renders and rolls only what moved, instead of warning and applying nothing, and the audit log records it as `agent.apply`; an agent already on the version, or a stopped one, closes quietly as before, and a retired agent or a docker that will not answer still say why. A database fault anywhere in the fleet's render and apply chain reaches an apply's `warning`, the roll picture and the endpoints route's *re-render failed (…)* as *the database could not complete this request*, with the database's own text only in the log; it used to carry the sqlx message. A start's browser-engine install container left in `created` (its CLI killed between docker's create and its start, so `--rm` never removed it) made every later install for that agent fail on its name, so the agent never got its browser tools: each start now clears such a leftover first, and a timed-out install's name is watched for two minutes and whatever lands there is removed; while it is watched, that agent's starts skip the install, so another agent's install that lands (which ends the fleet-wide cooldown) can no longer let the watch remove a new one. Verified on a worktree stack (two agents on the pinned Hermes v0.22.4 image, a scripted mock model, no real model calls, a docker shim on this api's PATH only), each case first on the branch head's own binary and ui: in Playwright, a failed Stop and a refused Roll showed nothing on the branch head and *Could not stop Bob* / *Could not roll Bob* with the route's sentence here, and every verb's refusal and failure was clicked on the real page (stop 403 and 500, restart 409 and 500, roll 409, start 409 and 500, retire 403 and 500, re-hire 409 and 500, delete 404 and 500, and a 503 stop titled *not confirmed yet*); a Save & apply whose recreate a docker shim held 320 s answered 502 at 302 s on the branch head with the form reading `[object Object]` while version 11 had been saved and rendered, and here answered 202 at 213 s with the form saying version 12 is saved and the tile *still applying*, the apply logging its own verdict when it ended; a no-op Save & apply on a version saved without an apply warned and rendered nothing on the branch head, and here applied it from the form (the container recreated, config.yaml on version 13, the form closed), stayed quiet with no roll once the agent was on it, left a stopped agent stopped and unrendered, kept the shared-department refusal, and kept docker's own sentence when the re-apply's recreate failed; with a column or table renamed on the stack's own Postgres for one request, the edit apply, the MCP apply and an endpoint delete's re-render carried `error returned from database: column d.max_children does not exist`, `agent key read failed: … column "key_enc" does not exist` and `relation "mcp_team_access" does not exist` on the branch head, and *the database could not complete this request* here, the sqlx text logged at each site (five render sites faulted this way); a browser-engine one-shot left in `created` made the branch head's next install fail with *Conflict. The container name … is already in use*, and here the next start removed it and installed, and a timed-out one-shot whose remove did not land was removed by the sweep 39 s later with no start involved (the lower-case *no such object* of docker 29 was found misread in this run and fixed). After review, on the same stack: a no-op Save & apply in the form, its render held 260 s past the bound by a lock on the render's key read, answered 202 at 212 s and the form read *Applying version 16 is taking longer…*; the roster kept *still applying* beside the *ROLLED* of a roll that had ended 81 s before the click (the old 300 s window would have taken that roll's verdict for this apply's), and cleared it once the apply's own roll was done (config.yaml v15 → v16, the container recreated), with one `agent.apply` row `{"version": 16, "reapply": true}`; an MCP unassign with `apply: false`, its render held the same way, answered 200 at 210 s and the render landed when the lock went; with Bob a Developer agent too, Ada's install held to its 90 s timeout and Bob's then landing, Ada's next start inside the watch skipped its install on the name (no one-shot of Ada's ran though a hold rule waited for one), and her start after the watch installed. `bun run gate` was green; CI is the full compile and test line.

- **Fixed: a Stop now lands when it reaches the api before the send it means, and when it is pressed on a new thread whose page then closes or starts a new chat. Five more DELETEs answer 404 for an id that names nothing. A database fault behind `POST`/`PATCH /api/me/assistant` is the house 500 instead of a 400 carrying the database's text. The render no longer closes the browser toolset for a def whose terminal runs in docker, ssh or another sandbox, because Hermes keeps its private-address check for that browser; and it now closes it, while the terminal is closed, for a browser Hermes lets reach private addresses anyway.** The page now names every turn it sends (`turnId` on `/api/chat`, a uuid it draws), and its Stop carries the name. A Stop that came before its send had been read and access-checked used to answer 409 *nothing is streaming*, and the turn ran on. Now it waits up to the 10 s control window for that send, then is held for it (talaria-chat-persist `turn_stop`, five minutes; only the same person's send, and only in the thread the stop named). The send hands a held stop to its own opening, and the drain sends it the moment the turn names itself. A new thread's Stop goes at once to the new `POST /api/chat/turns/{id}/stop` with `keepalive`, so a closed page or a new chat no longer takes the stop with it. A held stop is now placed with the five minutes the abandoned-turn guard gives the same stop, not the control window: on a starved agent store Hermes had not bound the turn's id after 10 s, refused the stop `409 not_found`, and the turn ran to its end. `DELETE /api/workflows/{id}`, `/api/keys/{id}`, `/api/rag/collections/{id}`, `/api/artifact-folders/{id}` and `/api/fleet/agents/{id}/secrets` answered 200 for an absent id, and three of them wrote an audit row for it (`key.revoke`, `rag.delete`, `agent.secret_delete`). `GET /api/fleet/agents/{id}/secrets` answered an empty list for an agent that does not exist. All six now answer 404 and audit nothing. The collection, key and secrets routes read the id by its canonical text, so an upper-case or braced spelling of a real id now deletes it (a collection's upper-case DELETE used to answer ok and delete nothing) and audits its own id. Every ui caller reads a delete's 404 as already gone (`delJsonGone`); the Studio workflow delete gains the error toast it never had, and the secrets tab drops a removed secret at once. talaria-personal-agent's 22 database sites, the create flow's 13 in talaria-fleet-create, and agent-secrets' template copy now log the error and hand up `store_fault`; a stored model tier that does not parse, the render's failure, the secretbox, the agent key write (on create as on rename: create used to answer a 400 naming the fleet `.env`'s host path) and a panicked task behind the same routes are the house 500 too. A rename that loses its handle to another between the handle check and the write is the handle-taken refusal, not a 500. Hermes v0.22.4's `_is_local_backend` asks last whether `TERMINAL_ENV`, which its gateway bridges from `terminal.backend` as `str()` of the value, is `local`. The render's `hermes_browser` and the toolset grid's `authoredBrowser` now read it the same way. Camofox is asked first and stays local. Neither side keeps a terminal-less agent's browser open when Hermes would pass it a private address: `browser.allow_private_urls` or `security.allow_private_urls` (read as Hermes' `is_truthy_value`) turns the check off for every browser, and a hosted provider (`browser.cloud_provider`) sends private addresses to a local Chromium sidecar that skips the check while `browser.auto_local_for_private_urls` is on (Python's `bool()`, on by default; a written provider is used whether or not its credentials are there), so both close the toolset; the grid's line says which setting did it. Verified on this worktree's stack with the pinned `hermes-agent:v0.22.4` and a scripted mock model behind the stack's gateway (no real model was called), on the branch's base (a63ff217, built and run first) and then this branch: the five DELETEs and the secrets read in four spellings of an absent id (200 and 12 audit rows before, 404 and none after), and a real row of each deleted in another spelling, then a 404 on the second delete (a revoked key stays the owner's ok, and someone else's key is the 404 and stays live); all five ui delete callers in Playwright against a row deleted behind the page (404, no toast, the row gone); seven injected database faults (statement triggers and one renamed column on this stack's own Postgres) behind the assistant routes (400 with the database's text before, the house 500 with the text in the log after), with the handle rule's and the unknown tier's 400 unchanged; a send whose 90 KB body took 5 s to upload with a Stop at 300 ms (409 and all 40 ticks before; the stop waited for the send and answered `hermes: true`, and the model was never called, after), the same over 15 s (held at 10.3 s, sent by the drain, model hung up after one tick), the old request shape without a name (still 409, unchanged), and another person's stop under the same name (409, the owner's turn ran on); in Playwright, Stop then close the page at once on a new thread while the agent's container was down (no stop sent and 40 ticks before; after, the turn stop left 44 ms after the send, was held, was sent when the agent opened the turn, and the turn never reached the model), and Stop then a new chat (stopped); a def with `browser.backend: off` and `terminal.backend: docker` rendered and read back from the running container (`browser` closed before, left open after; with `local` it is closed), and its grid line in Playwright; then, after review, eleven browser cases on that def rendered by the PR's earlier head and by this one, each read back from the container and put to Hermes itself in the container (`_url_policy_error` on a private address, with `TERMINAL_ENV` bridged as the gateway does): before, six cases had the toolset open while Hermes passed the address (a hosted provider with the sidecar by default, with it set to the string `"false"`, or with `allow_private_urls`; a docker terminal with either `allow_private_urls`; a CDP endpoint with it), after, the toolset is open in exactly the four cases where Hermes refuses it, and the grid's line for five of them in Playwright;
