`POST /api/me/assistant` with the fleet `.env` unreadable (400 naming its path before, the house 500 with the path in the log after); and a rename whose handle a trigger takes inside the rename's own transaction (500 before, the handle-taken 400 after, the same answer as a handle already taken). Unit tests cover the turn table (`turn_stop`), and a new live test (`turn_stop_live`) covers the turn stop's routes (a malformed name's 404, the 401, the thread stop's 400 for a bad `turnId`, another person's name's 409, a held stop and its hand-off to its own send); every terminal backend Hermes ships plus every non-string value, the private-address toggles and the hosted sidecar on every branch, the ui mirror, `delJsonGone`, `stopChat`/`stopTurn` and `newTurnId`. `bun run gate` was green locally (check, svelte-check, the ui vitest, and clippy `-D warnings` plus `cargo test` for the 15 api packages the diff touches, with `-p`), and the extended `absent_path_ids` live test passed against this stack's Postgres and Redis; CI's api job is the workspace compile.

- **Fixed: a live dither field no longer builds up brightness as it runs — a working or queued card, a list strip, the ticket's work strip, a streaming tail, generating blocks, drafting ghosts and the design splash now paint, frame after frame, exactly what a full redraw paints; every field, live or still, carries the median of the look people saw, and its dots sit on whole device pixels (N11).** The engine rewrites only the dots whose pixel changes, and it erased a dot over its own fractional rect before refilling it. The fill antialiases into the device pixels it half covers, and the erase did not reach them: Chromium rounds a clear to whole pixels and skips them, so their ink only grew (a card wash at DPR 2 held 6.7 times its designed alpha after 5 s and 28 times after a minute; a Generating block at DPR 1 reached 67 times, a solid slab); WebKit clears them by coverage, so they settled at 2 to 4 times. How much a field built up depended on the browser, the DPR, the page zoom and the canvas's sub-pixel position, so people saw anything from the designed look to a slab. The erase now covers every whole device pixel a dot can touch, outside the mask's clip, one erase per run of a row's rewritten dots; where dots share device pixels a changing frame is drawn as a full rebuild. Below DPR 1 (a page zoomed out) the canvas keeps a backing pixel per CSS px, so dots stay a device pixel apart. Each dot is drawn on whole device pixels (`snap`, on by default): crisp, the same pixels in Chromium and in WebKit on either canvas backend, and the same area at every DPR — a dot that is 1.75 device px wide is drawn 1 px wide in a quarter of the columns and 2 px in the rest. The look: the owner asked for the fix without the UI going faint, so the nine live fields and the three still ones (empty state, brief crest, ambient panel) are tuned to the median of today's look over 8 sub-pixel positions at DPR 1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75 and 2 in Chromium and WebKitGTK on its default backend plus Chromium at 90% and 110% zoom, fit on half of those positions and DPRs and checked on the other half, matching its ink and visible-dot area, with its highlights (the share of pixels past alpha 64, the brightest dots' alpha) where a field can carry them and no more weight over text than the median put there. The ticket strip moves to a 1 px dot; the drafting ghost keeps antialiased dots. A ring trace (`DitherBorder`) paints only the cells its 2 px ring can show (`edgeBand`), and a masked field skips cells its mask hides. Verified: a parity harness and `dither-engine.test.ts` (which rasterises like each engine and fails on the old engine with the same build-up, and on round 1's engine for a mask changed while the field was faded out) find 0 px between a live field and a rebuild of the same frame at DPR 1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75 and 2 and at 0.9, the ghost included; on the checked half, ink is within 10% of today's median and visible area within 20% for card wash, ticket strip, list wash, generating, splash, ghost and brief crest (Chromium and WebKit), and outside it for the card trace (ink 1.21), the list trace (visible area 0.73), the stream (visible area 1.22), the empty state (visible area 1.26) and the ambient panel (ink 1.12); WebKit's CPU and default backends paint the same pixels (ink, visible area and p99 ratios 1.000 on five fields); no field costs more canvas calls than rc (harness, calls a second against rc: card wash 0.49x, card trace 0.10–0.13x, ticket strip 0.96x, list wash 0.72–0.75x, list trace 0.12–0.21x, generating 0.72x, splash 0.85x at DPR 0.9, 1 and 2, stream 0.11–0.12x, ghost 0.21–0.37x; still fields paint once), and in the app (Chromium, DPR 1, a board with two working and two queued cards) canvas calls fall 43.2k → 12.3k a second and main thread 88 → 58 ms/s, the list view 173k → 101k and 226 → 167 ms/s, a board with one queued card 6.9k → 3.4k, at DPR 0.9 and 2 alike; before and after screenshots of every field in both themes, in Chromium at DPR 2, 1 and 0.9 and in WebKit, plus 4x crops of the HiDPI ring trace.

- **Changed: a loading skeleton keeps its motion and its pixels, and the page clock sleeps between its 8 Hz ticks instead of running 60 frames a second (UB6).** The skeleton's static re-rolls 8 times a second, but it filtered every frame of the shared page clock to find those 8, so one skeleton cost 60 animation frames a second. `subscribeToClock(fn, everyMs)` in `lib/motion.ts` makes a subscription periodic: it runs on the first frame past each multiple of `everyMs`, and while only periodic subscribers are left the clock sleeps on a timer and wakes one frame early for the boundary. The skeleton subscribes at 125 ms, and walks its mask's cells once per resize instead of once per tick. Every skeleton in the UI is the one `Skeleton` component (`SkeletonRows` and `SkeletonCard` compose it), so this covers them all. Verified: a parity harness in real Chromium and WebKitGTK mounted every skeleton shape the UI uses (text and title bars, an avatar, a tile's number slot, a block, a card-sized block, a status dot, a pill) on a virtual 60 Hz clock with a late mount, an unmount, a scroll out and back, a resize, a theme flip and reduced motion on and off, and hashed every canvas after every frame: 0 of 300 frames differ, old engine against new, at DPR 1, 1.5 and 2 in both engines, with 270 → 79 animation frames; a copy with a 126 ms bucket finds 26 frames differ, so the harness sees a millisecond. `globalAlpha` (and an 8-bit alpha) paints the same pixels in Chromium but moves a few edge pixels by a level in WebKit, so the per-dot colour string stays. Live in Chromium (DPR 1, 10 s windows): one skeleton (`/api/fleet/containers` held on Manage) 60 → 24 rAF/s and 24 → 18 ms/s of main thread at the same 1,147 fills/s; Manage with seven tiles loading 60 → 24 rAF/s, 67 → 61 ms/s; a board with every read held (79 skeletons) 58 → 24 rAF/s, 249 → 224 ms/s; idle Manage 0 rAF/s before and after. `skeleton-clock.test.ts` fails on the old clock (180 frames for 24 ticks).

- **Fixed: on Linux the background notice no longer tells you the dock's Quit quits Talaria, a tray that disappears gives the window back, and the tray icon shows the unread count.** The dash's or a dock's Quit only closes the window, the same as ×, because Talaria exports no quit action for GNOME to call; the notice and the docs now say so and name the ways that do quit (Ctrl+Q, the switcher's Quit, the tray menu). If the tray host goes away while the window is hidden to it (the GNOME AppIndicator extension turned off, updated or crashed), the window comes back with a notice instead of leaving a process nobody can see; when the host returns, the icon registers again. On Linux the unread sum is the label beside the tray icon (appindicator has no tooltip), and it clears at 0. Ctrl+Q works as soon as the window comes back from the tray, a banner or a second launch, without a click into the page first. A re-alert (a refreshed DM, Send test notification) closes the old banner and posts a new one, because a replaced notification may update silently; an update without a re-alert still replaces in place. A notification link with a `.` or `..` path segment, in any spelling (`/..//evil.example`, `/%2e%2e/x`), is refused like any other link that is not a plain same-origin path — the instance's own rule, so a link the server, the page and its service worker refuse is one the shell refuses too, and an instance at a path prefix cannot be climbed out of. Only the notification server's own signals count as clicks: another program on the session bus can no longer open an instance by sending `ActionInvoked` for one of its banners. Settings → Desktop shows each instance its own last error and last post, never another instance's. The badge reports the count it settles on after a burst (2 → 3 → 2 no longer leaves 3), and a signed-out page reports 0 instead of its last signed-in count. A suspended instance's watcher no longer stops for good on a Cloudflare challenge (a 403 with `cf-mitigated` or an HTML body is retried like an outage; only the instance's own JSON 401/403 means signed out), the shell's requests name themselves (`User-Agent: Talaria-Desktop`), and an event split across network reads, mid-character or mid-line-ending, is no longer dropped. The single-instance name is released when Talaria exits, so the updater's relaunch never hands over to the process that is leaving. A dev build started while the installed Talaria runs says to quit it first. Verified on the headless Linux rig (private mutter, private session bus, the recording notification server, real input through RemoteDesktop, real activation tokens) against this branch's stack: the corrected notice text in tray and no-tray mode; Close to the tray, then the tray host dropped: the window shown and the tray-gone notice posted, the status reading `minimize` and Close minimizing; the host restored: the icon re-registered and Close hiding to the tray again; the tray label `1` with one unread and empty at 0; a rogue peer's broadcast and addressed `ActionInvoked`/`ActivationToken` ignored ("not the notification server"), with no navigation or focus change, while the server's real click with a token landed and took focus; a page re-post replacing in place (2 → 2) and a re-alert closing 2 and posting 3; instance A's ServiceUnknown error shown to A and not to B; badge shares 1 + 1 = 2, and signing out of A in its UI dropping the total to 1; a second launch from the tray, then Ctrl+Q with no click, quitting, with `app.talaria.desktop.Shell` released 26 ms before the process's own bus connection closed; a real Alt+F4 (the same window delete GNOME's dash Quit falls back to) minimizing; three simulated Cloudflare challenges retried at 1.0/2.1/4.2 s with the watcher posting the next DM 0.6 s after it was sent, a real JSON 401 still ending the watcher, every watcher request carrying `User-Agent: Talaria-Desktop`, and a DM bannered 1.8 s after it was sent through an event stream delivered one byte per write; the window-state matrix 6/6 (unfocused, minimized, behind the launcher, suspended, tray, minimize fallback), each a banner from a real DM and a click that landed and took focus; and the tray menu's Open (back at 1280×800 with focus) and Quit. The split-event framing is also unit-tested at every split point of a multibyte event, and the badge reporter's debounce and sign-out in `lib/desktop-badge.test.ts`. Gates: `bun run gate` passes check, the ui svelte-check (0 errors) and vitest; its desktop cargo step needs GTK and WebKit headers this host lacks, so `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test` (95 passed) ran for the desktop crate in a Fedora 44 container, and the desktop svelte-check passes (0 errors). The dot-segment rule is unit-tested with the instance's own table (12 refused, 6 allowed: a dot in the query or fragment, or one that is not a whole segment) and ran live: links of `/..//evil.example`, `/%2e%2e//evil.example`, `/a/..//evil.example` and `/boards/..` posted with no link and their clicks dispatched nothing and loaded nothing, while `/boards?next=/..//evil.example` still opened in place; `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test` (97 passed) in the Fedora 44 container. With the web PR (#635) merged locally on one stack and the app built from the same tree, the integration contract passed against that real UI: a banner click reached the page, which routed in place with no reload and marked the row read; urgency and category followed the page's kind; a suspended instance posted a DM its page had missed exactly once and the restored page did not post it again; the badge tracked the bell; three DMs re-alerted under one tag; and reading the channel elsewhere cleared the badge, live and while suspended. Not verified on a real GNOME Shell or Plasma session, a real Mac or a real Windows desktop.

- **Fixed: desktop notifications work on Linux and macOS, closing the window keeps Talaria running so they still arrive, and the dock or launcher shows the unread count.** On Linux every banner now names its instance in the body, carries the desktop file the install actually has (detected: `Talaria.desktop` for deb/rpm, `app.talaria.desktop` for flatpak, AppImage and pacman, so no pinned launcher breaks), a category for messages and an urgency (approvals and other needs-you kinds are critical, status updates low), escapes markup so a DM saying `<b>&` shows exactly that, and replaces its own earlier banner by the id the notification server issued rather than an invented one. The whole app holds one session-bus connection: 30 banners left open used to cost 30 bus connections and 63 threads, now none. A click brings the window forward even when another app has focus on Wayland (the server's activation token is handed to the compositor), and reaches the instance as a `talaria:notification-open` event so the page can route without a reload; an older instance page reloads at the path as before. On macOS banners go through UNUserNotificationCenter with Talaria's own delegate: they show while Talaria is frontmost with its window closed, every click is routed back to its instance, permission is asked only when you click Allow notifications (on the launcher or in Settings → Desktop), and a post macOS refuses is reported instead of looking like a success. The macOS app is ad-hoc signed as `app.talaria.desktop`, the identity macOS ties notification permission to. Windows toasts are attributed to Talaria instead of Windows PowerShell. Closing the window now hides Talaria to the menu bar (macOS) or the tray (Linux with a tray host and libayatana-appindicator), or minimizes it where the desktop shows no tray icons (stock GNOME), with a one-time notice saying how to quit; Quit is in the instance switcher, the launcher and the tray, and Ctrl+Q (Cmd+Q on macOS) quits from any page; Settings → Desktop → Keep running in the background turns it off. Windows keeps quitting on close for now. A second launch on Linux brings the running window forward and exits. Settings → Desktop gains a Notifications panel that reads the real state from the OS ("On — shown by GNOME Shell", "Not allowed yet", "Blocked in System Settings", or the notification service's own error), the last error, and Send test notification. The badge is the sum of every instance's unread count (the macOS dock; Plasma, Ubuntu Dock and Dash-to-Dock on Linux). A suspended instance's watcher now starts from the page's own record of what it already showed, so a message the page missed (a dead stream, a sleep) is posted once instead of never, and the restored page does not post it again; it reconnects with backoff after a 502 instead of a fixed 5 s, and keeps its 30 s poll through the outage; clicking its banner marks the notification read. Instance pages still get no event permission, and every new command is rate limited per instance (20 banners, then one every 2 s). Verified on a headless Linux rig (private mutter on Wayland, a private session bus, a recording notification server, real clicks and keys through mutter's RemoteDesktop, real activation tokens from mutter, WebDriver on the launcher) against this branch's stack: a real DM's captured banner with each desktop file, urgency 2/0/1 and the category per kind, the escaped body, the in-place replace by the server's id, another instance's same tag getting its own id, 30 open banners changing bus names and threads by 0 and 0, activation with a token taking focus and the no-token control staying behind, the click event with and without a listener and a crafted cross-origin path dropped, the event channel refused to a page, 50 rapid posts giving 20 and 30 `rate limited`, junk kinds dropped, badge shares summing (2 + 3 = 5) and clearing, the tray registering and its menu's Open and Quit working, Close hiding with a tray and minimizing without one, the one-time notice, real Ctrl+Q, the switcher's and the launcher's Quit, Close quitting with the setting off, a second launch exiting in 0.09 s and focusing the first window, the handoff posting a missed DM exactly once and the restore merging it back, reconnect delays of 1.0/2.1/4.1 s after three 502s with the gap DM posted in 15 s and 12 s through the poll floor alone, a watcher banner click setting `read_at`, the honest status with no notification service and with one, and a banner plus a landing click in each of six window states (6/6). macOS through CI only: the new `desktop-macos` job compiles and lints the UN backend on every desktop pull request, and the packaging run checked the ad-hoc signature, the bundle identifier, the UserNotifications link, and the self-test through LaunchServices (`backend un`, `notDetermined`, and a post that is an error until permission is granted). Windows through the packaging run's installed-exe self-test (attributed by the Start-menu shortcut, AUMID `app.talaria.desktop`). Not verified on a real Mac or a real Windows desktop.

- **Changed: the notification contract — every notification takes a per-person, commit-ordered sequence number, a producer can coalesce rows into one per group, the server serves the class registry, a channel matrix, DND and working hours, presence and a devices list, and the read-sync event names exactly which rows were read; the Home Inbox's undo of a read now restores the row, and otherwise nothing a person sees changes yet.** The groundwork the second round of notification work builds on, in one change (docs/notifications/contract.md). One schema block with no data backfill: `users.notify_seq`, seventeen metadata-only columns on `notifications` (the seq, a group key and count, the alert level, actor and entity, Done, the client ack, and the push/mail due times), five partial indexes, `channel_members.notify_level`/`muted_until` and `push_subscriptions.user_agent`; rows filed before it keep a null seq and wave 1's arrival rule. Every write now runs in one transaction that takes the person's next seq under their row lock, so a reader that sees seq N has seen every row up to N, and a producer can pass a group key to update the one open row of that group instead of filing another (with a window, a quiet mode, and adoption of a pre-contract row that keeps its id and its snooze). `GET /api/notifications` keeps every key it had, in order, and adds the For-you count, the seq read in the same statement as the rows, `classes` (labels and defaults now come from the server), the channel matrix, DND state computed in the person's time zone, the mail frequency and `features`; each row adds its seq, alert, class, category, count, actor, entity and reason. `PATCH` takes `channels`, `dnd` and `emailFrequency`, and a write in either the old routes or the new matrix keeps the other in step; the digest's default can no longer be flipped by a new class. New doors: the ack, a per-device test push (501 until the delivery engine lands, already limited to 5 per 10 minutes), the devices list and delete (a push service's error is shown as at most 120 plain characters), a member's own channel notify level, and presence heartbeats with a GET. Reading an agent thread now tells your other tabs (it told none before); the instance email switch now merges instead of overwriting its row. The push edge can carry TTL, Urgency and Topic and sends exactly wave 1's headers when told nothing. Fixed in review: a re-alert's time now always moves later — two writes for one person racing could stamp the later one with an earlier time, and every client would miss it as a re-alert; a Push switch turned off in the new matrix is obeyed; a row made unread again goes through one door that cannot collide with a newer row of its group, and the Home Inbox's undo — which compared a microsecond timestamp with a millisecond one and so never restored a row — now does; a desktop client heartbeating from the tray while its machine is idle does not mark the person online; and a failed settings read can no longer erase the instance's other delivery switches.

  Verified: on the contract's own stack (app :5306, api :5406, Postgres 16.15 :5606) — a boot from 0 tables applied 517 statements, a boot of the contract on that wave-1 database with data applied exactly 9 and the next applied 0, and `migrations:check` replays all 526 from zero in a scratch postgres:16 and matches the regenerated snapshot. The schema block on a synthetic 1,000,000-notification / 200-user copy, with a concurrent writer, three runs: 0.85–2.8 s of server time in all, the longest writer stall 0.19–0.87 s, every ADD COLUMN metadata-only (relfilenode and size unchanged); the write path's p95 rose by 0.4–2.6 ms (3.6 ms for a keyed coalescing write). 8 concurrent writers × 2,000 rows for one person with a ninth reader sampling the cursor: 0 violations in 80,347 samples, seqs 1–16,000 unique and contiguous; 50 concurrent writes to one key gave one row with count 50 and the last writer's body; the window, Quiet/Realert, read-then-fresh and adoption (same id, snooze intact) behaved, and a window expiring under concurrent writers never conflicted. Over real HTTP, 42/42 checks: three DMs gave three stream frames with rising seq equal to the GET's; prefs both ways; DND pause and working hours in America/New_York; read-sync ids on two streams, mark-all, the channel and agent-thread reads, and `resync` past 100; presence frames only on a winner change, and a bare PUT still marks the person online; the ack; two devices with UA labels and a planted 512-character HTML error shown as 120 plain characters; 501 ×5 then 429 with Retry-After; channel levels (403 for a non-member with no row inserted, 409 for a task room); push headers TTL 3600 / Urgency normal / no Topic and a payload of wave 1's shape. Wave 1 unchanged: its browser checks c09, c10, c11, c12 (also with DND paused) and c06 on Chromium and c09, c11 on Firefox all passed as before, and the live push, read, fan, agent-reply and conversation-read suites pass. `bun run gate` passed check, the ui typecheck and its 2,702 tests, the cli, and fmt, clippy and tests for the twelve api packages the diff touches; its desktop cargo step cannot build on this host (no GTK development libraries) and runs only because the shell's own commits are in this diff — CI's desktop job builds it. `bun run check` passes, and each half of the new class-registry rule was shown to fail on a planted violation in a scratch copy. The review re-ran everything live on the same stack: on the old write path, 16 of 49 coalesce steps under 50 concurrent writers moved `createdAt` backwards or not at all, and after the fix none do; a fresh database migrates 526 statements and then 0, a wave-1 database with data takes exactly 9 and then 0, an older image's runner boots on the new schema applying 0, and the replay from zero matches the snapshot; the schema block again ran in 0.94 s of server time on a fresh 1,000,000-row copy with a 235 ms longest writer stall and every relfilenode unchanged, and with commit latency taken out the write path's p95 rose 0.2 ms (1.3–1.8 ms keyed); 8 × 2,000 concurrent rows gave 0 violations in 246,773 samples; the live notification suites pass, as do 46/46 HTTP checks (including the matrix Push switch, the online key for desktop and web heartbeats, and the Home Inbox undo of a plain and a grouped row); and wave 1's browser checks c06, c09, c10, c11 and c12 (also under a pause) on Chromium and c09, c11 on Firefox all pass. The widened class-registry rule fails on a planted ticket kind, a planted const kind and moved writers, and passes on the restored tree.

- **Fixed: notifications reach the browser — Talaria asks to turn desktop alerts on at a moment with a reason, keeps the push subscription healthy from boot to sign-out, survives Cloudflare's idle cut and a deploy's 502/524, surfaces what landed while a page was closed or the stream was down, shows one OS banner per notification per browser, opens it in place and marks it read; on the server, DMs ring for every message, reading a DM clears it, description edits notify only the people they add, and an assignment files one row.** Nothing used to ask: the only `requestPermission` sat behind a Settings toggle below the fold. Now an in-app card ("Get a desktop alert when someone needs you — mentions, DMs, approvals") appears only after a notification was just toasted in front of you (or came in while you were not looking at the tab, and you came back to it) on a page you have touched and had open 10 s, never on load; "Not now" is remembered on the account (7 days, then 30, then never) and holds for the page's life even if that write fails, and the bell keeps a row: Turn on, the per-browser and per-OS steps when alerts are blocked (Chrome/Edge/Brave, Firefox, Safari, GNOME Web; macOS, Windows, GNOME and KDE Plasma), or, on a plain-http dev stack, that alerts need HTTPS, naming the origin. Settings → Notifications → Desktop alerts shows the same state live (a grant or block made in the browser's own settings shows up without a reload) and whether this browser is registered for alerts with every Talaria tab closed; on Linux and Windows it adds that closing the browser's last window quits it and stops them, because those alerts need the browser running. A browser whose permission is granted files its push subscription at every boot with no click, replaces one bound to an old instance key, and signing out retires it at both ends (the server deletes every row that session filed, by a hash of the session; other sessions' rows stay) and closes the banners still in the notification centre. Event streams now open with `retry: 3000`, ping after 20 s idle, carry `X-Accel-Buffering: no` through the app's proxy, release their Redis subscriber the moment the client leaves, and end when the api gets its shutdown signal, so a restart no longer waits on connected browsers until the container's stop timeout; the client reopens a stream that went CLOSED on a 1/2/4… 30 s backoff (at once when the network or the tab comes back) and refetches everything the stream drives on reopen; the inbox query polls in hidden tabs too. A per-user arrival record in localStorage replaces the silent first-read baseline, so a reload, a reopen or a deploy surfaces what you missed (more than three at once become one "N new" summary), and rows read elsewhere, or already shown as a banner by the worker, never surface. Tabs elect a leader with a Web Lock and share their visibility over a BroadcastChannel: the tab you are looking at toasts, otherwise exactly one OS banner (and when this browser cannot post banners, because it is not granted, on plain http or switched off, the visible tab touched last toasts instead, so a Talaria window on a second monitor still shows it), posted through the service worker registration so a push of the same row and the tab's banner are one notification (a shared IndexedDB store records what was shown); the worker takes control at once, skips a push while you are looking at Talaria (never on WebKit, which revokes silent pushes), and on a click focuses the existing tab first and routes it in place. Every click path (toast, banner, the desktop shell's `talaria:notification-open` event) checks the href is a path on this origin and marks the row read. The server, the page and the worker refuse dot segments (`/..//host` resolves to the path `//host`, another host when parsed again). A notification with no link leaves you where you are, and only real rows are marked read, so a summary click opens the bell — in the desktop shell too, where the summary banner now carries the page it was posted from, because the shell hands a click back only for a banner that names a path. Banners carry a branded icon, a monochrome badge, a timestamp and `renotify` for re-alerts. On the server: a new DM refreshes the conversation's unread row in place and re-alerts it (no second email); reading a channel to its newest message clears its rows and tells your other tabs (`{type:"notifications",unread}`, also sent by every mark-read), and an open conversation reads only while you are looking at it (shown and focused), so a DM to a conversation left open in a background tab, a minimized window or an instance behind the desktop launcher still alerts and counts in the badge, and is read the moment you look; a ticket description edit notifies only newly mentioned people; a person assigned by a patch gets `task-assigned` without the duplicate status row; rows store only same-origin hrefs, with no `.` or `..` segment. Web Push is bounded (5 s connect, 15 s per POST, four devices at a time, 32 in flight), clamps its payload under the 4,096-byte record (a 413 gets one minimal resend), retries 429/5xx/timeouts at most twice honoring Retry-After up to 60 s, records `last_status`/`last_error`/`last_attempt_at` per subscription, prunes after three consecutive 401/403 (not for an Apple `BadJwtToken`-family fault, which is the instance's), and signs with `AUTH_PUBLIC_URL` (or the verified domain) as the VAPID subject. `talaria worktree` and `box seed` no longer copy push subscriptions or the VAPID key, so a dev stack cannot push to the source database's real browsers. One migration adds `session_hash`, `failures`, `last_status`, `last_error`, `last_attempt_at` to `push_subscriptions`. New: `docs/NOTIFICATIONS.md`. Verified live on the worktree stack with Playwright 1.63 (full Chromium new-headless and Firefox; D-Bus pointed nowhere, no display, so nothing reached a desktop), page visibility emulated because headless engines report every tab visible, and the push service stubbed in-page for the page-side lifecycle because headless engines refuse `pushManager.subscribe`: the soft ask (0 prompts on load, card only after a toasted arrival with activation, Not now → count 1 and +7.000 d, +30 d, retired after 3, bell row stays, and an answer holds for the page even with the account's memory wiped) 15/15 on Chromium and Firefox; Turn on (exactly 1 `requestPermission` with activation, SW registered, 1 row with the session hash, the confirmation banner) 7/7; blocked steps per engine and live re-grant/revoke with no reload 8/8 on both; the insecure origin `http://notify-lan.test:5304` explained with no toggle and no card 6/6; boot subscription, key-mismatch heal and sign-out (another session's row survives, and the banners on screen are closed) 6/6; the api's own process killed and restarted, and a 524 from an edge proxy: streams went CLOSED, reconnected on ≈1/2/4 s and within the pending step, refetched on open, and the outage mention surfaced exactly once, 11/11 and 9/9 on both engines; headers, `retry: 3000`, pings every 20 s (longest silence 20.0 s over 90 s) and `PUBSUB NUMSUB` back to 0 in 87 ms after 5 streams closed 11/11; the hidden fallback banner at 28.3 s and, after 6 min hidden, at 17.4 s; catch-up (offline, summary, read-elsewhere, reopen from the record, fresh profile silent) 6/6 on both; one banner per browser (focused tab toasts only, all hidden → exactly 1 show across pages and worker, a push of a row the hidden leader already showed, delivered with no window open and its banner dismissed → 0 because the bannered store skips it (an unseen control row → 1), push-first then the leader's read → 1 total, leader failover in ≤ 16 ms then exactly 1) 6/6; clicks routed in place with no reload and read_at set, and foreign or dot-segment hrefs (`https://…`, `//…`, `/..//…`, `/.//…`, `/a/..//…`, `/%2e%2e//…`) leave the tab where it was, 10/10 on Chromium and 9/9 on Firefox's page-Notification path; the worker's own rule on the two paths no page re-validates (no window at all, and a same-origin window that never answers) never left the instance for seven foreign or dot-segment hrefs, while a valid path was still navigated, 19/19; with banners off (permission default) a hidden leader plus a visible unfocused tab → 1 toast in the visible tab and 0 banners, focusing that tab raises the card, two visible unfocused tabs → exactly 1 toast in the one touched last, and with banners on the same layout still gets exactly 1 banner, 4/4 on Chromium and Firefox; the api exited 69 ms to 1.2 s after SIGTERM with streams open in 3 of 4 runs (the 4th outlived the 6 s check, and its overwritten log no longer shows why), and its streams ended 15–250 ms after the signal in all 4; the restart check passes 12/12; DMs (1 row, 3 alerts under one tag with renotify, channel read clears it and the other tab's bell drops in 72 ms, a 4th alerts again) 6/6; 55 edits → 0 rows and `@cy` → 1; one assignment → 1 row while a watcher still gets the move; the push transport against a capture server with every POST decrypted and its JWT verified (a hung device held nobody: ok in 58 ms; 3 × 15 s timeouts; 2,500-char title → 726-byte body; one 413 resend; Retry-After 2 s honoured; 500 three times; 404/410 pruned; 3 × 403 pruned; BadJwtToken uncounted; `sub` = `AUTH_PUBLIC_URL`) 12/12; the CLI's own seed pipeline from a DB holding push rows and the key → 0 rows, no key 6/6. `bun run gate` passed (check, svelte-check, 2,654 ui tests, cli tests, fmt/clippy/tests for the 11 touched api packages); `bun run docs:api` leaves no drift; the migration replays from zero and the snapshot matches; the live push, realtime and read suites passed 34/34. Against the desktop shell (#634), merged locally with this branch on one stack and Talaria Desktop built from the same tree, in a private headless desktop (its own session bus and a recording notification server): a banner click reached the page as `talaria:notification-open`, which this UI cancelled, routed in place with no reload and marked read; the page passed each kind (dm and mention gave category `im.received`, approval_pending urgency 2 with an attention request, task-status urgency 0); a suspended instance's watcher, started from this page's arrival record, posted a DM the page had missed exactly once, and the restored page, its record merged, posted neither of the watcher's two again; the launcher badge equalled the bell and the api's unread count at 0, 1, 4, 3 and 0; three DMs gave three alerts under one tag (renotify false, true, true), each re-alert closing the one before; reading the channel from another client dropped the badge to 0 in 0.62 s; the window-state matrix 5/5 with the page left on the conversation; and the web checks 10 (6/6), 12 (6/6), 6 restart (12/12) and 6 behind a 524 (9/9) in Chromium. That run found the two fixes above: a DM to a conversation left open behind the launcher was marked read 38 ms after it landed and never alerted, and every row of five more was read within 76–124 ms (after the fix: 5 banners, the row unread until the conversation came in front, then read; and in Chromium, hidden → no read and 2 banners, looking → read in 6 ms, visible but unfocused → unread and a banner, 11/11); and the summary's click in the shell opened nothing (after: the event carried `/boards` and the bell opened). Not verified: a real Mac, Safari or Windows (Playwright WebKit does not launch on this Fedora host), a real push service, real tab visibility and Chromium's hidden-page throttling, a real focus change from a click, and a real `bun talaria worktree` (creating worktrees was off limits; the same pipeline ran with the CLI's constants).

- **Desktop notifications, round two: every signed-in instance alerts, a read anywhere clears the banner, the dock badge counts what is for you, and the dock's Quit quits on Linux.** Instances you are signed in to but have not opened this session are now loaded hidden at launch (one second in, then five seconds apart, five at most) and handed to the shell's own watcher, so their DMs and mentions banner without a click, as Slack and Teams do for every workspace. The watcher speaks the notification contract: with an instance that serves it, it reads `?since=` its own cursor page by page and reopens its stream with `?since=`, so a reconnect after an outage or a sleep is exact rather than "the newest 50"; it never banners a row the server marked `feed`; while your Do Not Disturb is on it banners only what breaks through (approvals and other needs-you kinds); it acks every row it banners, so the instance's deferred push for it is cancelled; it heartbeats your presence as this desktop (`active` while the OS saw input in the last two minutes), so the instance can hold a push while you are at the desktop; and its catch-up summary carries the page's own tag, `talaria-summary`, so clicking it restores the instance and opens the bell. When a notification is read anywhere else, the banner closes: the watcher closes its own from the stream, and instance pages can close theirs through a new `desktop_notify_close` command (GNOME's `CloseNotification`; macOS removes it from Notification Center too), keyed by the calling instance so one instance can never close another's. A new `desktop_os_idle` command reports the OS idle time (mutter's idle monitor on GNOME, the screensaver service on KDE/X11, CoreGraphics on macOS) for presence. The dock and launcher badge, the launcher's per-instance count and the tray now count For you — what needs you and what is addressed to you — not everything unread; the tray menu lists each instance with its own count ("Acme — 3"), which drops when you read, and opens it on a click. Each instance's row in the launcher has a bell that mutes its banners on this desktop (its count still shows), and Settings → Desktop says when an instance is muted. On Linux the GTK application is now registered as `app.talaria.desktop` with a real `quit` action, so GNOME's dash and Alt+Tab Quit actually quit Talaria (every page remembered) instead of only closing the window; the window's Wayland app_id and X11 class are `app.talaria.desktop`, and the deb and rpm `Talaria.desktop` names it (`StartupWMClass`) without being renamed, so pins keep working. The deb and the rpm now recommend the tray library instead of requiring it (Talaria runs without it and minimizes on close). The macOS menu-bar item is a template image that follows the menu bar's light and dark look, and a left click shows its menu. Windows is unchanged this round. Verified on the headless Linux rig (a private mutter on Wayland, a private session bus, a recording notification server, real keys and clicks through mutter's RemoteDesktop, real activation tokens) against this branch's stack: a watcher banner closed 0.03 s after its row was read from another client, a page banner closed through `desktop_notify_close`, and another instance's tag closed nothing (0); every watcher banner was followed by an `ack` (200) with `surfaced_at` set; a `task-status` row filed as `feed` posted 0 banners, a DM during a Do Not Disturb pause posted 0, and an `approval_pending` during it posted with urgency 2; `desktop_os_idle` read 31,512 ms after 31 s with no input and 1,390 and 1,667 ms after a key press, and the watcher's heartbeat sat in `presence:dev` as kind `desktop`, `active`; For you 2 + Following 3 gave a LauncherEntry count of 2, from a page and from a watcher; the tray read "Rig A — 2" and "Rig B — 1" and dropped to "Rig A" and "Rig B" after the reads; a muted instance posted 0 banners from its watcher and from its page while its share stayed on the badge; a five-row burst on a suspended instance was one `talaria-summary` banner, and its click took focus from another window, restored the instance and opened the bell (the page cancelled the event); `org.gtk.Actions.Activate quit` over D-Bus exited 0 after remembering every page, the Wayland `set_app_id` was `app.talaria.desktop`, and a second launch still handed over in 0.11 s; two never-opened signed-in instances had watchers 2.95 s and 7.86 s after launch and each bannered a DM, at 274 MB PSS for the whole app afterwards; the six window states each bannered and landed a click (6/6), and a run with no tray library minimized on close with no panic. Gates: fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and 107 tests in the Fedora 44 container; desktop svelte-check 0 errors; `bun run gate` passed check, ui svelte-check (0 errors) and vitest (2,703), cli and the api packages, then stopped at the desktop cargo step, which this host cannot run (no GTK development files), so the container run stands for it. With the hub, engine and web-runtime streams merged locally (never pushed): an instance's watcher cut by a simulated Cloudflare outage while 60 rows were filed reconnected with `?since=`, posted one "60 new" banner and acked all 60, and after its click the restored page posted none of them, with its arrival record at the server's seq (138 = 138); with this desktop active the engine held a DM's push for 60 s and the watcher's banner and ack cancelled it (0 pushes), while a muted instance's (no ack) arrived at +64 s; and a live page closed its own banner 0.04 s after a read elsewhere through the web runtime. The packaging run on this branch: the deb's Depends and the rpm's Requires no longer name the tray library and their Recommends do, the deb's desktop file names `app.talaria.desktop`, the macOS bundle is still `app.talaria.desktop` (ad-hoc) and its self-test reports the idle time and `close: ok`, and Windows still attributes toasts to its shortcut. Not verified on a real GNOME, Plasma, Mac or Windows desktop. After review: a catch-up longer than the watcher's page budget no longer starts over on every read (an instance 1,100 rows behind used to repost a "700 new" summary every 30 s and never reach its last 100 rows; it now reads ten pages at a time and goes on from the last row read: one "1100 new", and 2,300 rows behind is "2000 new" then "300 new" once, every row acked); a suspended instance stays quiet while you are looking at, or active on, another of your clients (a browser tab, another desktop), as the web runtime does, so one device alerts instead of two, and it counts its own page on this desktop as itself; `gapplication launch app.talaria.desktop` (D-Bus `Activate`) shows the window instead of crashing the app; a tray count changes its row's text instead of rebuilding the menu, which made libayatana register the tray item again on every notification and read; an `&` in an instance's label shows in the tray; and the launcher's count pill keeps its shape on the selected row and is dimmed for a muted instance. Re-verified on the rig after review: the original head panicked on one D-Bus `Activate` (exit 101) and the fix showed the window three times running; a web client `looking` held a watcher's DM (0 banners) and the next DM after it went `hidden` bannered and was acked; a late heartbeat under the page's own id left the watcher posting and acking, the engine held the push to +60 s and 0 pushes came, while a muted instance's push arrived at +61 s; with the hub, engine, web runtime, center and producers merged locally the 60-row replay was one "60 new", 60 of 60 acked, the restored page posted 0 and its record's seq matched the server's (4717); a live page closed its own banner 5 ms after a read elsewhere; the tray held its item ids across count changes with no new registration; and the window-state matrix passed 6/6. The wave-2 integration run (all six streams merged locally, never pushed) found a watcher that went silent after its instance's database was restored or reset under it: its cursor only ever rose, so `?since=<old seq>` found nothing and every frame at or below that seq was ignored until the server passed it again. A complete page whose seq is below the cursor now makes the watcher rebase as the page does — the newest page judged by wave 1's rule, the server's seq taken — and a `resync` below the cursor asks for that read at once. On the rig against that merge, 5 mentions posted and acked, the rows after them deleted and the person's seq put back, then 2 more filed: the unfixed shell bannered 0 of 2 in 76 s; the fixed one 2 of 2 within 20.5 s and 17.4 s (two runs), each acked, with the rebase logged; container fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and 114 tests (2 new) pass.

- **Added: a notification center — the bell gets For you and All tabs, a badge that counts only what needs you or was addressed to you, rows grouped by the ticket or channel they are about with their counts, Done and read/unread on each row, a pause menu, and a full `/notifications` page with Done, filters, paging and keyboard shortcuts; Settings → Notifications becomes a per-kind matrix of In-app, Desktop, Push and Email with a missed-activity email frequency, Do Not Disturb (pause presets and working hours), and a status and troubleshooting panel.** The bell's badge is the For-you count (Needs you and Direct); Following shows under All without badging. Consecutive rows about one thing sit under one header ("TAL-112 · 3 updates"), a row that stands for several events says so ("3 messages", "Moved 4 times"), each row says why it reached you and shows who did it, and clicking one still opens it in place and marks it read. `/notifications` shows For you, All and Done, filters by unread, category and what happened (the filters are in the URL), loads more as you scroll, and takes `j`/`k`, `Enter`, `e` (Done), `u` (read or unread), `x` (select), `Shift+E` (Done everything shown or selected) and `?`. Done, Move to inbox, mark unread, the Done view and paging appear when the server offers them (`inbox-v2`); without it the tabs and filters work on the newest 50. Settings' class rows are replaced by a matrix drawn from the server's class registry, so a member sees 9 kinds and an admin 11; In-app is always on, Email is disabled with the instance switch's explanation while instance email is off, each row can be reset to its defaults, and the old per-class routes stay in step for older apps. Pause notifications from the account menu or the bell for 30 minutes, 1 or 2 hours, until 9:00 tomorrow in your profile's time zone, until you resume, or until a time you pick; set working hours with their days and "Let Needs you through"; the bell says "Paused until …" with Resume. The status panel checks this browser (permission, live; service worker; push subscription; whether the server has it on file; a local test banner), lists your registered devices with what the push service last said and a per-device test and Remove, says where alerts go right now by which device you are on, reads the desktop app's own notification service when you are in it, and shows the pause in force. A Done, one row in the bell or any number on the page, can be undone for a few seconds (the page's `z` too) and comes back unread if it was; a bulk Done over hundreds of rows goes through; Caps Lock no longer turns `e` into "Done everything shown"; and the bell, the matrix and the settings rows fit a narrow window. The client's own copy of the class list is gone (labels come from the server), and the invariant that refuses a second class list in the client has no exceptions left.

  Verified: vitest for the new modules (presets across the daylight-saving days of New York, London and Auckland and a spring-forward gap, the matrix rows for a member and an admin, the keyboard, grouping, filters and the device test lines) and svelte-check with 0 errors. On this change's own stack against the contract's api, in Chromium and Firefox (`ui/e2e/notify-center-ui.spec.ts`): with 2 needs-you, 3 direct and 4 following unread the badge read 5, For you listed 5 and All 9, the coalesced DM said "3 messages", the three rows about one ticket sat under "TAL-112 · 3 updates", opening a row routed in place with no page load and read it, and no Done control showed on an api without the inbox API; the matrix had exactly the served classes in registry order (9 for a member and 11 for an admin against the contract; 10 and 12 with the delivery engine's new account class) with In-app checked and locked, Push off for direct messages was sent as `{channels: {dm: {push: false}}}`, survived a reload and left the legacy `prefs.dm` derived from the channels, and Reset put it back; with instance email off every Email box was disabled under the explanation; the frequency saved as `1d` and read back after a reload; Pause for 1 hour from the account menu stored `pausedUntil` within a minute of an hour ahead and the bell showed "Paused until …" until Resume cleared it; "until tomorrow 9:00" for a person in Pacific/Auckland, in a browser set to Europe/London, stored exactly 09:00 Auckland time; working hours that exclude now saved and the server reported DND active by schedule; the browser permission flipped granted, denied and back with no reload (CDP in Chromium, grant and clear in Firefox); two devices listed with "This browser" on the one this session registered, Send test showed "Server test not available on this instance yet." for the contract's 501 and "Try again in …" on the sixth, and Remove deleted the row; a desktop presence heartbeat showed alerts going to Talaria Desktop; and in a faked desktop shell the panel read the shell's notification service and ran its test through the bridge. On throwaway local merges, never pushed: with the delivery engine, Send test reached a loopback capture service as an aes128gcm, VAPID-signed push and the row read "Delivered to the push service in 2 ms…", the sixth still limited; with the web runtime, the whole spec passed again and the panel showed the live stream as connected, this tab as the one holding it, and alerts going to this browser; with the inbox API, in Chromium and Firefox, Done on two For-you rows took them out of the bell and the badge (5 → 3) and into Done (archived and read in the database), Move to inbox brought one back read, Mark unread raised the badge by one, `unread=1&category=direct` listed exactly the rows an SQL query over the table gives, 130 rows loaded by scrolling with every one present once, and on the page `j` three times then `e` marked the fourth row Done with the focus staying in place, `u` read and unread it again, `?` opened the shortcuts, `x` on two rows then `Shift+E` marked both Done, and `Enter` opened the focused row in place. `bun run check` passes, and a planted three-class list in `ui/src` fails it. After review, on the same stack in Chromium and Firefox: with the contract alone, the whole spec passed again, now with a 390 px window where the bell's panel stays inside the viewport and each matrix label spans its row, rows without an actor lining up under a category glyph, Do Not Disturb's "Saved" shown in its own panel, and the live-connection sentence matching what the instance serves; and on a throwaway merge of all five sibling streams, never pushed, all 19 chapters passed in both browsers, including Done then Undo in the bell bringing the row back unread and badged, `Shift+E` over nine rows then `z` restoring each as read or unread as before, `J` then `E` with no Shift marking one row done (the reviewed head marked all six), a click on a select box then `e` still working, and `Shift+E` over 230 scrolled-in rows archiving all 230 in two writes of 200 and 30 (the reviewed head sent one write of 230, which the api refused, and archived none). The wave-1 checks this area touches passed unchanged: the soft ask 15/15, Turn on 7/7 and blocked 8/8 in both browsers, and the click 10/10 in Chromium and 9/9 in Firefox.

- **Changed: notifications are one row per thing with a count — a DM, a thread, a ticket's status burst, a flapping MCP server, an approval and its reminders each keep one row that updates — the people taking part in a ticket or a thread are told, every channel and DM gets a level (All / Mentions / Nothing) and a timed mute from its header, an approval's rows clear for everyone the moment someone decides it, and a plan @mention reaches the person again.** The producers half of the second round of notification work (docs/notifications/producers.md). A DM coalesces every message into one row per conversation (the newest line, the count, a re-alert), a row filed before the contract is adopted with its id, and a read row means the next message files a fresh one. An agent's replies in your thread, its daily outreach, a ticket's comments and a channel thread's replies do the same; a ticket's status moves within ten minutes are one quiet row ("Moved 4 times — now in review") that alerts once, and the ticket's creator now hears them. A comment on a ticket reaches its assignees, creator, watchers and earlier commenters, and a thread reply reaches the root's author and earlier repliers, each re-checked for access when the row is filed, so someone removed from a board gets nothing. Levels: a channel defaults to Mentions, a DM to All; All files one counting row per channel; Nothing silences @mentions too; a mute lands rows in the bell without a toast, banner or push. The header's menu sets them and says "Muted until …"; a person who reaches a channel only through a team cannot set a level yet (an owner decision). Approvals and their SLA reminders share one row per person, so a nag re-alerts it, and a decision reads every recipient's row with the read-sync ids; an MCP server's recovery reads every admin's down row, and a server going down again within the hour reopens it with the count. Every row now names who caused it and what it is about. A plan @mention had matched nobody whose email was not their first name, because the candidate list swapped name and email, and it read each person's teams one query at a time; both fixed. A caller that hangs up right after a ticket edit or a channel post no longer loses the notifications the write owed. A post with no text — a file on its own — rings the other side of a DM (and a channel at All) as a line of text does, the row reading "Sent an attachment"; the header's "Muted until …" follows the conversation's name and gives way first in a narrow header, and a change made on another device shows on the next refetch.

  Verified: on this stream's own stack (app :5309, api :5409, Postgres 16 :5609), over real HTTP with throwaway `.invalid` people and no push subscriptions: three DMs gave one row with count 3, the third line, three `notification` frames with seq 1, 2, 3 and a createdAt that moved each time, reading the DM made the fourth a fresh row, and a planted wave-1 row was adopted with its id (6/6); a one-hour mute filed a feed row and unmuting re-alerted it as a banner (2/2); a channel at its default filed nothing for a plain message, All gave one channel-message row whose count reached 3 with an unmoved createdAt, Nothing silenced an @mention that the default then delivered, and a DM reads All (6/6); four status moves in 62 ms gave the creator one row with count 4 and "Moved 4 times — now done" and one createdAt, and past a test-shortened 8 s window a fresh row while the old one kept its words and lost its key (4/4); against a local fake MCP server, ok → down filed one row per admin, recovery read both with a `readIds` frame to each, and down again re-alerted the same rows with count 2 (3/3); a board-access request reached its three editors with one keyed row each, and one editor's decision read all three in one statement, each editor's stream getting a read-sync frame naming their own row (3/3); the SLA job's own function, its clock moved past the nag, re-alerted the ticket owner's announcement row (the same id, count 2); a comment reached the assignee and the creator but not its author or a person removed from the board, and a thread reply reached the root's author and the earlier replier, coalescing (3/3); a plan @mention reached its reader, and one message read `team_members` once with 5 users and once with 45 — the previous binary, on the same database, missed the person and read it 45 times. A post-commit hang-up (a 500 ms pause injected after the ticket write, debug builds only): `curl -m 0.3` straight to the api lost Cy's @mention 10 of 10 times before and delivered it 10 of 10 after (and again on the final head), and a hang-up tied to the moment the write committed gave 0/10 before and 10/10 after. The header menu on Chromium and Firefox: Nothing, Mute for 8 hours and Unmute each survived a reload and matched the server's row, and a person taken off the channel behind the page saw the refusal and no membership row appeared (4/4). Wave 1's DM browser check (c12) passed 6/6 on Chromium, and the whole HTTP rig re-ran 29/29 on the final head. Live `it` suites `notify_producers_live` (6), `agent_reply_notify` and `group_dm_live` (3) pass, as does the contract's `notify_contract_live` (7); vitest covers the menu's helpers. `bun run gate` passed check, the ui typecheck and its 2,708 tests, the cli, and fmt, clippy and tests for the 24 api packages the diff touches, and stopped at the desktop cargo step this host cannot build (no GTK development libraries; it runs only because the stack's desktop commits are in the diff). After review, on the same stack: an attachment-only DM and an attachment-only post in a channel at All, which filed nothing on the reviewed head, each filed their row (2/2); the whole HTTP rig re-ran with stricter checks (a status burst's createdAt held from the first move; with the push plane armed, the muted DM recorded no push and the unmuted one did) 29/29 across its runs (the MCP trio with the fake server's loopback allowed, the mute pair with the scheduler armed); the approval escalation through the real scheduler re-alerted the same row (count 2); `curl -m 0.3` and a commit-tied hang-up each delivered Cy's mention 10/10; wave 1's c12 passed 6/6 on Chromium and Firefox; and the menu spec, with a new chapter that fails on the reviewed head (a change made elsewhere stayed hidden behind the page's last write), passed 6/6 on Chromium and Firefox. The wave-2 integration run (all six streams merged locally, never pushed) reproduced the review's open N4 in this stream's own live test: a burst's row said `count` 4 while its body read "Moved 3 times", because each move's fan-out runs detached and worded the line from a count read before its write. After the write, a fan-out whose count differs now rewords the body, but only while the row still holds its seq, so the last write keeps the last word. A new live test fires six concurrent moves per ticket; on this branch it failed 3 of 3 before the fix (count 5 with the first move's body, count 5 with "Moved 4 times", count 4 with "Moved 3 times"), and it passes 3 of 3 after it, with the rest of notify_producers_live (8/8) on this worktree's own stack.

- **Changed: notifications now reach a person once, on the device they are using, in the channel they chose — the server enforces the class × channel matrix, DND and working hours with a Needs-you break-through, holds a push for a minute while one of the person's clients is in use (cancelled when a client acks the row or the person reads it), batches missed-activity mail into one message per person, keeps "work finished" and paused workchains quiet by default while a channel you set to All alerts like a direct message, and hardens the push edge; the per-device test push works.** The delivery engine of the second round of notification work (docs/notifications/delivery.md). Every write now decides, inside its own transaction, from the class's Desktop, Push and Email channels, the person's DND and working hours (in their profile's time zone, or the workspace's when the profile has none — the zone their brief opens in, as Profile's "Workspace default" says; it used to be UTC), what the producer said, the instance switches (`emailEnabled`, and a new `pushEnabled` that defaults on) and whether one of their clients is looking or active. A row held by a pause or outside working hours is a feed row, is not pushed, and mails when the pause ends; Needs-you classes still banner and push unless the person turns that off. With a client in use, the push waits 60 s and a 5-second job sends it unless a client acked the row or it was read; the write reads presence before it locks the person's row, and treats a Redis failure as "nobody there" and pushes. Mail is no longer queued in memory and sent within 30 s: the row carries its due time (15 minutes for Needs you, else the person's frequency — 15 minutes, an hour, or 09:00 next on their clock), and a one-minute job sends each person ONE mail with every row of theirs still unread ("N unread in Talaria", grouped by category, through the same kill switch as the digest), mails a conversation that was already mailed again at the person's frequency while it stays unread (its next message re-arms it; a mail already pending stands, so a burst is still one mail), retries a failure after 5 and 15 minutes, gives up on the third, and drops due rows rather than holding them while mail is switched off; the legacy email-only route still files the row read once a provider takes the mail. Work finished and workchains paused (Following) default to the feed only; a stored route or channel still wins, so nobody who chose banners loses them. Channel activity, the one row a channel set to All files (only once the person picks All; a channel starts at Mentions), banners, pushes and mails like a direct message by default, and stays in the All tab, off the For-you badge. A new `account` class carries the notice that an agent now acts as you on Google (it used to fall into the quiet bucket). Pushes carry Urgency and TTL by category (Needs you: high, 24 h; direct: normal, 12 h; news: low, 1 h) and the row id as `Topic`, so a re-alert replaces an undelivered push. The VAPID key is unsealed once per key instead of on every delivery, the plane and the batcher read the live secretbox so a key rotation (which now re-seals `push_vapid` too) never breaks push or mail until a restart, a timeout is retried once instead of twice, a device that timed out or failed three times is skipped for 2^failures minutes (an hour at most) while the person's other devices are served at once, and ten failures in a row with no delivery and no re-subscribe for a week prune it. Sessions now write a liveness marker beside themselves, and a daily job deletes the push subscriptions of sessions that ended (logout or the 7-day expiry), after first marking every live session that predates the marker; another daily job deletes read notifications after 90 days and unread ones 180 days after their last activity, with their inbox-focus rows. The presence winner cache is ordered by the read each heartbeat makes (one atomic script and a counter), so two racing heartbeats can no longer leave the older winner cached with no `presence` frame for the newer one. `features` adds `email-batch`, `quiet-following`, `dnd-enforced` and `presence-gated-push`.

  Verified: on the stream's own stack (api :5407 run with two test-only knobs that shorten the mail delay to 20 s and run the daily jobs every 20 s, Postgres :5607 migrated from 0 to 526 statements, Redis :6507), over real HTTP, with web push aimed at a capture server that decrypts each payload (RFC 8291) and mail into a local SMTP sink, `.invalid` people, instance email on in that database only: Desktop off → a feed row; Push off → nothing reaches the device in 10 s; Email on → a due time; a pause → the DM is a feed row, not pushed, mailed no earlier than the pause's end, while a Needs-you row (a workchain hand-off) banners and pushes with Urgency high, TTL 86400 and the row id as Topic, and `allowNeedsYou: false` makes it a feed row; working hours outside now (America/New_York) behave as a pause; a fresh person's task-status is a feed row with no push or mail, a stored `work_complete: "both"` keeps banner, push (Urgency low, TTL 3600) and mail, the Google-principal row reads as `account`, and three seeded people's digest answers are unchanged; a refreshed DM re-alert carries the same Topic (normal, 43200). Presence, 7 runs each, on the final build: no heartbeat → the push within 2 s of the write (7/7, 7–119 ms; a second run was 6/7, its outlier 4.3 s while that DM's own POST took 26.7 s inside an IO stall); a looking web client, an active desktop, and a heartbeat that stops → no push for 55 s, then one at 61.2–61.6 s (7/7 each; 62.0–62.1 s on the build before the lease fix); an ack or a read at 5 s → no push in 120 s (7/7 each). The api SIGKILLed 10 s into a deferral and while a mail waited → after restart exactly one push and exactly one mail. The batch: 3 DMs and a mention → one mail, "4 unread in Talaria", 4 items; one of four read first → "3 unread"; all read → none; an SMTP 554 → attempts 1, 2, then given up at 3 and logged; mail switched off → the due row discarded, nothing sent. `POST /api/notifications/test` → 200 with the capture server's 201 and a decrypted `kind: "test"`, another person's device → 404, the 6th counted call → 429 with Retry-After. 50 deliveries → 0 unseals of the cached key; deleting `push_vapid` → a new `k=`; Admin → Encryption rotate re-sealed `push_vapid` under the new version and push still worked. A hung endpoint: two timed-out tries, skipped for the next three deliveries while the other device received each in under 80 ms, then tried again past its window and reset by a 201. Two sessions' devices: after `DEL sess:…` and its marker, the prune removed that row and kept the other. Retention removed the 91-day-read and 181-day-unread rows with their inbox-focus rows and kept the 30-day and 100-day ones. Live `it` against the same database: `notify_engine_live` (the whole engine, including approval_pending breaking through a pause), `push_live` (6, including the new backoff test), `notify_contract_live` (7), `notifications_reads`, `realtime_fan`, `agent_reply_notify`, `conversation_reads`, `unreads`, `workchains_live` (13), `pending_dedupe_live` and `conversation_schedules_live` all pass. `bun run gate`: check clean (the class-registry rule reads the new `account` class), ui svelte-check 0 errors and 2,702 tests, cli tsc and 457 tests, and fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and tests for the 16 api packages it chose; its desktop cargo step cannot build here (no GTK development libraries) and runs only because #634's desktop commits are in this diff — CI's desktop job builds it — and the desktop typecheck it would run next was run by hand: 0 errors. The host was under heavy shared IO load; runs that overlapped it saw single statements wait over 100 s on commit fsync, and the timing checks above are from runs outside those stalls. After review (commits on top of 3a1b101e, nothing rewritten): every check above re-ran live on the reviewed head (46/46) and again on the fixed build on the same stack — the setup-to-retention batch 33/33 (the working-hours check, which first hit a 100 s host IO stall, re-ran 5/5 with its batch), presence 7/7 in each of the six cases (deferred pushes at 63.8–63.9 s), the restart checks exactly once for the push and for the mail, and the batch mail 5/5 — plus the review's probes: two racing heartbeats replayed against Redis with the shipped scripts now cache the later read whichever compare-and-set lands first (the head's script cached the earlier read and published nothing); a mailed DM conversation's next message is mailed again with the newer line, and two more messages before that is due make exactly one more mail (on the head: no further mail at all); an unread group row born 181 days ago and updated yesterday survives retention while an untouched one goes (the head's SQL deleted both). Live `it` on the fixed build: `notify_engine_live` (now also asserting the re-mail rule and the active group row), `push_live` (6), `notify_contract_live` (7), `notifications_reads`, `realtime_fan`, `agent_reply_notify`, `conversation_reads` (2) and `unreads` all pass. Cross-stream, after review, on the same stack over HTTP: with the workspace's zone Asia/Tokyo (`brief_config`) and working hours bracketing Tokyo's hour, a person with no profile zone was served `dnd.timeZone: "UTC"`, DND active, and their DM was a feed row; now `Asia/Tokyo`, not active, and the DM banners (a profile zone of Asia/Tokyo banners on both builds). On a local merge with the producers branch (never pushed), a channel at All filed a feed row with no push and no mail; now its row banners, is pushed at once with nobody looking (Urgency low, TTL 3600, the row id as Topic) and is mailed at the person's frequency, a looking tab defers its push by 60 s and the job sent it at 60.5 s, three messages are one row counting 3 with one push, a read lets the next message alert again, and a member left at Mentions gets no row. `notify_engine_live` (now also asserting both), `push_live` (6), `notify_contract_live` (7), `notifications_reads` and `unreads` pass on the fixed build.

- **Changed: the live stream resumes and the inbox gains an API — one Redis subscriber per api process instead of one per open stream; a reconnecting stream replays every notification it missed, by seq, each exactly once; a stream ends when its session does (sign-out, a deleted or expired session); the api stops within about a second with streams open; and `GET`/`PUT /api/notifications` gain views, keyset pages, filters, a `since` read, Done (archive) and mark-unread.** The server half of the second round of notification work (docs/notifications/live-and-inbox.md). Every event stream — the person's own, boards, channels, runs and the run-watch tail — now rides one subscriber connection per process (`talaria-realtime`'s hub): a topic is subscribed while any stream wants it and unsubscribed the moment the last one leaves, a stream that falls 256 messages behind ends (its client reconnects), and when the connection drops the hub reconnects, resubscribes and tells every user stream to resync. On `/api/me/events`, a notification frame carries its seq as the SSE `id:`; a reopen with `?since=` or `Last-Event-ID` sends the person's presence, then every row after that seq (up to 100, else a "read it yourself" resync), then a resync frame, and drops the live copies of what it replayed. Logout publishes the session on `session:revoked` and every stream it opened ends at once with a `session` frame; every live frame is sent only after its session is re-read, and a quiet stream re-reads it every 20 s. `GET /api/notifications` takes `view=foryou|all|done`, `unread`, `category`, `class`, `kind`, `limit` and `before` (an opaque cursor; `next` in the answer), or `since=<seq>` (rows in seq order with `more`); with no parameters it answers exactly as before, plus `more`. `PUT` takes `entity` beside `ids` and `href`, and `archive`, `unarchive` or `unread`: Done also marks read, so the bell, the Home Inbox, the brief and the badges drop a Done row without a change of their own, and every path tells the person's other tabs (`readIds` for a read or a Done, the counts otherwise). The Home Inbox's mark-read and its undo now tell the other tabs too. Reading a row cancels its pending deferred push, and marking it unread never brings that push back or mails it at its old due time: a pending mail is re-armed from the reopen, at the person's own frequency and on their clock — their zone, else the workspace's, as the delivery engine reads it (a row already mailed stays mailed). `unread` leaves Done rows out, so it can no longer disagree with `unreadForYou`, and `/api/unreads`' research badge leaves them out too; a crafted page cursor is a 400 rather than a 500. On shutdown the hub closes with the streams, in-flight responses get at most 5 s, the pool 1 s, and each drain phase logs how long it took — which named the old linger: 3 of 10 stops with streams open took 11–35 s, every one waiting on a single boot-time seed query held behind a slow disk. New `features`: `since`, `inbox-v2`, `sse-replay`, `archive`. Nothing older breaks: the shell's watcher, older pages and the Kotlin client ignore the new frames and fields.

  Verified: on this worktree's own stack (api :5408, Postgres :5608, Redis :6508), over real HTTP and SSE with the stack's Redis read directly. 70 streams (50 user streams over 10 people, 10 board and 10 channel streams) held exactly one pubsub connection in `CLIENT LIST`, one subscription per topic; a DM to each person reached 50/50 streams with `id:` equal to the seq; closing all 70 took `PUBSUB NUMSUB` to 0 in 328 ms; `CLIENT KILL` on the hub brought it back with a resync on every user stream within 100 ms, and the next DM arrived on all 10. A stream reopened with `?since` after 7 DMs got exactly those 7 frames, ids equal to their seqs, then `resync complete:true`, and `Last-Event-ID` gave identical frames; 150 rows gave only `resync complete:false`, and `?since` returned all 150 in one page with `more:false`; a DM racing the replay arrived exactly once in 20/20 runs over HTTP (2 landed in the replay, 18 live) and in 20/20 deterministic runs of both orders in the live suite. Logout ended that session's stream 6 ms after the request while another session's stream kept receiving; `DEL sess:` with a DM right behind it ended the stream in 91 ms with no notification frame; on a quiet stream in 19.5 s. Shutdown with 20 streams open: before the pool bound, 3 of 10 stops took 11–35 s; after it, 10 of 10 exited in 92–1,118 ms, with no process or listener left (the contract's binary exited in 93–128 ms in 20 stops in which the seed query did not stall). The inbox API, 16/16: For you paged 50/50/30 matching a SQL oracle in order; `category=direct&unread=1` and the fallback class matched SQL; Done on 3 rows set `archived_at` and `read_at`, moved them from All to Done, named them in `readIds`, and took them off the Home Inbox; unarchive, mark-unread (the badge rose by one), the caller-only entity selector, and the Home Inbox's mark-read and undo each published. Old clients: with no parameters, the same top-level keys in order with `more` appended, and byte-identical newest 50 rows against the contract's binary on the same database; with a Done row unread, the contract's `unread` counted it and this one, like `/api/unreads`, does not. Wave 1's browser checks on this stack: c09 6/6 and c12 6/6 on Chromium (two earlier c12 runs missed the 1 s bell bound only because the read's own commit took 4 s and 22 s on this host's disk; the event reached the second tab within 1 ms of the read answering). `cargo test` for talaria-realtime (17), talaria-notify (43), talaria-routes-comms (19), talaria-routes-integrations (28) and talaria-inbox-focus (10) passes, as do the live `it` suites notify_hub_live (5), realtime (29), realtime_fan (1) and notifications_reads (4); `bun run docs:api` regenerated activity.md and account.md, and `bun run check` is clean. A separate review re-ran every check on the same stack and added four: with a row lock held on the boot seed's rows, the contract's binary outlived its SIGTERM by the whole hold (9.3 s on a 10 s hold, past 60 s on 40 s holds) while this one exited in 1.1 s, 3 of 3; with Redis paused for 45 s and its socket left open, the hub noticed by its ping and every user stream got its resync 1 ms after the unpause; `Last-Event-ID` and the stream's headers cross the app's proxy, and a logout through it ends the stream in 19 ms; and the research badge read 2 with one Done row unread, 1 after the fix. The engine review's cross-stream N3, checked over HTTP on a throwaway local merge with the delivery engine (`wt/notify-engine`, never pushed) on the same stack, with a push capture server and a local SMTP sink. Before the fix: DMs to a person whose tab was looking were deferred 60 s; 5 of 5 that were read at 5 s and marked unread at 20 s were pushed anyway, at 60.6 s (3 read through the API, 2 by a path outside the inbox module). Rows read before their mail was due (30 s, the engine's test delay) and reopened after it were mailed 0.3–0.4 s after the reopen, and one reopened before it was mailed at the old due time. At production delays, 4 aged rows (15m, 1h, 1d and a Needs-you approval) were mailed within two batcher ticks of their reopen. After it: the read clears `push_due_at`, a reopen leaves it null, and 0 of those 5 rows were pushed in 120 s, while an unread control was pushed at 64 s. A reopened mail is due 30.004–30.006 s after the reopen, the rows were mailed 32.0–32.3 s after it, and a never-read control was mailed at its due time. At production delays the due times are 15 min, 60 min, 09:00 New York time, and 15 min for the approval at a 1d frequency; `off` arms none, mailed and given-up rows are unchanged, and none of the 7 rows was mailed in the 130 s after its reopen. `cargo test -p talaria-notify` (45, with the due-time and DST cases) and `-p talaria-inbox-focus` (10) pass; the live suites notifications_reads (5, with a new test for the deliveries) and notify_contract_live's reopen, clear and coalesce tests (3) pass on this branch alone. The wave-2 integration run (all six streams merged locally, never pushed) found the reopen still reading a person with no zone of their own on UTC while the delivery engine's write reads the workspace's zone: on that merge, with the brief's zone set to Asia/Tokyo, a reopened daily mail was re-armed for 09:00 UTC (18:00 in Tokyo) while the engine served `dnd.timeZone: Asia/Tokyo`. The reopen now reads the same chain (the profile's zone, else the brief's `timeZone`, else `TZ`, else UTC); `cargo test -p talaria-notify` covers the zone rule and the Tokyo due time, and a new live test in notifications_reads (6/6 on this branch's own stack) sets the brief's zone aside, reopens a no-zone person's daily mail at 09:00 Tokyo time, and a New York person's at 09:00 New York time.

- **Changed: Talaria alerts on the device you are on — one event stream per browser however many tabs you have open, board and channel streams that sleep in hidden tabs, nothing lost across a reconnect where the server can replay, no toast or banner for what you muted or while Do Not Disturb holds it, a row read on sight when you are looking at its page, banners and toasts that close everywhere when you read a notification anywhere, and "(2) Talaria", a favicon dot and an app badge for what is waiting for you.** The browser's half of the second round of notification work (docs/notifications/web-runtime.md). The tab that holds the notification leader lock now owns the browser's only `/api/me/events` and passes every event to the other tabs; when it closes, the next tab takes the stream over at once (five tabs were five streams and five server subscribers). A board, channel or work-session stream closes once its tab has been hidden for 30 seconds (5 on a plain-http dev stack, where a browser allows six connections to a host) and catches up when the tab is shown, so eight tabs on a dev stack no longer starve each other, and a work session that finished while its tab was hidden shows that it ended.
