Against a server that serves it, each tab catches up by sequence number (`?since`) — every notification filed while the stream was down arrives exactly once, as one summary past three — and the arrival record keeps its key and gains `v: 2` and `seq`. Each arrival is decided in order: a muted ("feed") row and a row held by Do Not Disturb are counted in the bell but never toasted or bannered (Needs-you rows still break through); a Direct or Following row whose page you are looking at is marked read instead of toasted (a hidden tab never reads it); the tab you are looking at toasts; and when the server says you are looking at, or using, another device, this browser stays quiet. Each tab now reports itself — looking, active, idle or hidden, with the desktop shell's OS idle time — on the presence heartbeat it already sent, a tab that closes says so on its way out, and a toast shown to you or a banner posted is acknowledged so a delayed push can skip it. When a notification is read anywhere, the banners for it close (in the desktop shell through `desktop_notify_close`) and its toast is dismissed; mark-all clears them all. The tab title counts your For-you unread, the favicon gets a dot, and an installed app's badge shows the count; a web app manifest is served. Visiting a page reads the Direct and Following notifications that point at it. A stream ended because its session ended re-checks the session at once. A Do Not Disturb pause that has ended holds nothing, even before the page's list is read again; a duplicated tab takes its own presence id instead of sharing its original's; and the desktop shell is asked to close banners at most 100 at a time, the summary first. After the cross-stream review it also holds when the server's notify seq goes back (a restored database, a reset dev stack: the browser takes the server's seq, so rows filed afterwards still alert), signs a tab out when its session ends elsewhere even if the first session reads fail, counts the desktop shell's own watcher as this device after a restore, and its service worker drops a push older than the banner it already shows.

  Verified: on this branch's own stack (app :5310 on plain http, api :5410, a fresh database), live in Playwright 1.63 Chromium and Firefox with D-Bus pointed at nothing, hidden tabs emulated (neither engine reports a background tab hidden). One stream: 5 tabs held one `/api/me/events` and one server subscriber, a DM reached all 5 (4–177 ms after its frame), and closing the leader opened a new stream in exactly one other tab within 20–68 ms, the next DM reaching all 4 — on both engines; the closed tab's subscriber goes when the api's next ping notices it. Topic pause: a board and a channel tab closed their streams 5.0 s after hiding (on an h2 page, 30.0 s), nothing reopened while hidden, and a ticket renamed and a message posted meanwhile showed 2 ms and 5–21 ms after the tab was shown; a work session ended while its tab was hidden showed "Session ended" 10–76 ms after show; 8 tabs on the dev origin held one user stream and one topic stream, and each tab showed its own change when shown (55–2,063 ms, the slowest being the one tab whose stream never paused, i.e. the server's event latency). Decider: mention rows with the person's Desktop channel off were filed as feed and gave 0 toasts and 0 banners while the bell moved; during a pause a DM gave nothing and an approval banner broke through; a DM to the conversation being looked at gave no toast and was read in 228–378 ms; the same tab hidden bannered it and left it unread. Cross-device, two contexts as two devices: with A looking, B made 0 banners and said why, A toasted and acked (the server set `surfaced_at`); after 130 s with no input A's heartbeat said idle, B saw no winner and its leader bannered the next DM once; with presence stripped from B's answer, B bannered as wave 1 did. Read-sync: a read in A closed B's banner in 57–71 ms, mark-all left 0, a toast for a read row went in ~215 ms, and a faked desktop shell posted through `desktop_notify` and got `desktop_notify_close` with the read ids (and, on mark-all, its recent tags plus `talaria-summary`) — on both engines, Firefox through the page's own Notifications. Ambient: "(2) Talaria" on every route and plain at 0, the favicon dotted and restored, `setAppBadge` 2 then 0, the manifest valid with its icons served. Heartbeat bodies went looking → active (at 63.7 s) → idle (123.7 s) → hidden → idle → looking, never two beats inside 5 s; the faked shell beat `kind: desktop` with `osIdleMs` and stayed active with its window hidden. Wave 1's own checks still pass on this branch: c06 restart 11/11 (adapted to one stream: the leader's stream goes CLOSED and backs off 1/2/4 s, the follower owns none and refetches on the hub's reopen, the outage row surfaces exactly once), c09 6/6, c10 6/6, c11 10/10, c12 6/6, c17 11/11 on Chromium, and c09 6/6 and c11 9/9 on Firefox. With the live stream's replay merged in (a throwaway local merge of the hub stream's head, never pushed): five times over, 60 notifications filed while the browser was offline gave exactly one "60 new" summary, nothing on its own, every row in the record's seen set and the record's seq equal to the server's — 0 lost, 0 repeated — on Chromium and Firefox, and a wave-1 record surfaced only the row it had not seen. With the delivery engine merged in the same way, the person looking at one device saw the toast, the other device stayed quiet, and after the 60-second deferral the acknowledged row was never pushed. The new e2e spec passed against this stack. vitest (2,800+ ui tests, the decider matrix, tracker v2, the hub, read-sync, ambient and presence among them) and svelte-check pass. On review, re-run on the same stack: one stream 8/8 (Chromium and Firefox), topic pause 11/11, decider 12/12, cross-device 9/9, read-sync 7/7 on both engines, ambient 7/7, heartbeat 5/5, and wave 1's c06, c09, c10, c11, c12 and c17 (c09 and c11 on Firefox) all green; with the list's `dnd` frozen at a pause that had since ended, a DM was bannered (the code before the fix recorded it silently as "do not disturb"), and with the pause still ahead it was held; a tab opened with its original's client id split into two clients within 17 ms, the server held both, and the looking one stayed the winner. On a throwaway local merge of the reviewed live-stream (`290c1c96`) and delivery-engine (`0a6a259e`) heads, never pushed: the 60-row catch-up gave one "60 new" five times over with the record's seq equal to the server's on Chromium and Firefox, and a wave-1 record surfaced only its unseen row; an online burst of 60 rows cost each tab two `?since` reads and one summary; the acknowledged row was never pushed after the 60-second deferral; a logout elsewhere sent both tabs to the sign-in page within 116 ms with no reconnect; and the one-stream, decider, read-sync and wave-1 catch-up checks passed again. Found and fixed live on the way: the status setters looped inside an effect; a cached dev page read the protocol of a font CDN and held hidden streams for 30 s; a view re-created in a hidden tab reopened its stream; a resumed stream could miss a change between its read and its subscription; closed tabs stayed the presence winner for 75 s; acks queued in the last half second before a tab closed were lost; banners posted with no worker could not be closed. Since the cross-stream review, on slot 10 and a throwaway local merge of this branch with the live-stream (`290c1c96`), delivery-engine (`0a6a259e`) and notification-center (`bac58d64`) heads (never pushed): with the server's seq put back below the browser's cursor (five rows read, then the seq reset and the rows deleted, as a restore would), a row filed afterwards never alerted and the record kept its old seq before the fix (after a reload and after an api restart), and after it the record took the server's seq and both following rows toasted in about 110 ms, on Chromium and Firefox; with the first two session reads after a logout elsewhere answering 502, the page stayed signed in and kept reopening its stream before the fix, and after it reached the sign-in page in about 2 s with no reopen (one tab, two tabs with four failed reads, and Firefox), while the plain logout, the logout after an api restart and the live-stream review's own probe went to sign-in in about 110 ms; in a faked desktop shell whose watcher id was the winner, the page recorded "on another device" before the fix and posted the banner after it, while another machine's watcher still kept it quiet; with the notification center open on six loaded pages, a live arrival's toast came 41 ms after its frame against 30 ms on Home (the center's refetch does not hold it, so nothing changed there); unit tests pin the rebase, the merge, the watcher id, the session retry and an out-of-order push on every engine. The wave-2 integration run (all six streams merged locally, never pushed, with Talaria Desktop on a private rig) found one more duplicate: with the person active on the desktop (the presence winner) and a browser tab still focused and visible but untouched for 130 s, a DM was bannered by the desktop and toasted by the idle tab. The in-app toast now needs the person to be looking at the tab (touched in the last 60 s) or no other device to win presence, so the desktop alerts alone; a tab the person is looking at still toasts whatever the server's winner says, and with no presence nothing changes. On that merge the idle tab toasted 1 copy before the fix; a decider unit test pins both sides. On WebKit, an out-of-order older push now shows the newer copy still on screen again, silently, instead of showing nothing, because Safari counts a push that shows nothing against the subscription; a unit test pins it and fails on the code before.

- **Fixed: creating an agent on a server that does not have the agent image yet no longer stalls and fails — the download is its own step of the hire, the roster shows it moving ("downloading the agent image — 412 MB so far, 36 of 38 layers ready (4 min)"), the hire finishes when the image lands however slow the link, and a hire that fails anyway has a Retry on its row.** The Hermes image is about 1.1 GB to download and 4.5 GB on disk, so the server needs about 6 GB free. A server downloads it for its first agent, and every server downloads it again on its first start after a pin bump (this release moves the pin). To make the first hire after upgrading instant, pull the pin on the server first: `docker pull nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.22.4@sha256:7a69201726bc64db2072a1371557137c23312d29705cda2b8ea2a0214a50a4cf`. On main the download ran inside `compose up`'s 120-second deadline, so on a link slower than about 9 MB/s or a busy disk the first hire was killed mid-download every time, and so was every Start after it. On rc it ran ahead of `up` with a 20-minute deadline, but inside the hire's boot step, which the run engine files as an error at 10 minutes and never retries. A download slower than about 2.5 MB/s failed the hire with "step exceeded maxStepMs (600000ms) at phase "starting the container"", and the roster said "starting the container" the whole time. Now the pull is one per service in the api process, on a task of its own. The hire's new pull stage waits 15 seconds at a time on it and shows its bytes and layers as the phase, or "waiting for docker to start downloading the agent image (2 min)" while docker has not begun. A Start, roll or re-entered hire of the same agent joins the download in flight instead of starting another (two different agents run two pulls, and docker downloads each layer once for both), and a caller that goes away no longer cancels it. A Start now downloads the image before it takes the agent's lock, so a Stop or Retire pressed during the download lands at once, and the start it interrupted does not happen afterwards. "Start all agents" answers within 75 seconds and finishes in the background, instead of holding the request past Cloudflare's 100 seconds; its outcome and each agent that would not start are logged and written to the audit row. A Start the stop cancelled says "Not started: a stop was asked while the agent image downloaded", on the agent and on the hire alike. The pull reads compose's `--progress json` events, and is stopped only when docker says nothing for 10 minutes or after 3 hours, never for being slow. A hire that fails says what to do: Docker Hub's pull limit, a full disk, a download that stopped, docker never starting, or docker's own error for a container that would not start (not compose's first line of progress, "Container … Creating", which is all the row used to say). A failed hire's row now has a Retry (`POST /api/fleet/hires/{id}/retry`). It runs the hire again on the same agent, which the create modal refused before, because the failed hire had already taken the handle and the department. Only the agent's managers and admins can retry it, and only its newest hire. An agent deleted since can be retried only by an admin, or by the person who ran that hire if they still hold `agents.manage`. A second Retry of the same row is refused, and so is a retry of an agent that has run since: that agent is its people's to start. The newest failed hire of an agent that is still a draft stays on the roster whatever its age, so drafts left by hires that failed before this upgrade (on main, a cold server's first hire always did) appear there with a Retry: press it, and the roster shows the download and the start. Deleting the draft and hiring again also works. An `up` killed at its deadline that left the container half-created waits for docker to show the container, then runs once more, which starts it. The boot step's ceiling is 15 minutes, up from 10. The roster drops a failed row once a newer hire of the agent exists or the agent runs.

  Verified: live on this branch's own worktree stack (app :5311, api :5411, a fresh database). Agents pointed through `HERMES_IMAGE` at a test image: the pinned v0.22.4 plus one fresh random layer, served by a local registry behind a rate-limiting proxy, so only that layer was missing on the host. The disk was saturated by other sessions throughout (`/proc/pressure/io` "some" 60–92 %, Postgres statements up to 269 s), so the times are pessimistic. Main's verb (`compose up -d`, killed at 120 s), 1 GB at 3 MB/s, three times: 351 MB, then 0 MB twice, because the busy daemon sent no request in 120 s. The image never landed. An unkilled pull afterwards resumed with a 206 for the remaining 649 MB. rc 65dbae86, a dashboard hire, 1 GB at 3 MB/s: "starting the container" for 10 minutes; then "step exceeded maxStepMs (600000ms) at phase "starting the container""; then the background pull was killed at 1,200 s with 697 MB down, and the agent stayed a draft. Re-hiring from the modal got 409 for the handle and 409 for the department. This branch, two dashboard hires at once, 1 GB at 2 MB/s: both rows read the same live count ("22 MB so far" up to "1.0 GB so far … (8 min)"), and the proxy carried 1,001 MB for the two. Both then hit FLEET-4 under the stall: `up` timed out creating the container, and the second `up` hit a name conflict while the create was still landing. That is why the second `up` now waits for the container and the row shows docker's error. Retry on each row answered 200, and each agent was up and healthy 20 s and 30 s later. A pull cut at 67 MB failed the hire at once with "The agent image could not be downloaded. Press Retry … Docker said: … short read: expected 500152789 bytes but got 68137984: unexpected EOF". Retry in the UI resumed it with a 206 for the remaining 432 MB, showed "downloading … 110 MB so far" through "unpacking … 500 MB", and the agent was up and healthy 7 minutes later. A pull killed at 44 MB was resumed one second later, and an unrelated 20 MB pull beside it took 14 s: a killed client leaves nothing stuck in docker. Unit tests pin the stage machine (the slow pull stays its own stage and never boots early; a failed pull or up fails with its sentence), compose v5.5.1's real json events, the failure sentences, the retry's input, and the roster's `hiresToShow`. cargo tests for talaria-fleet-docker, talaria-runs-agent-hire and talaria-routes-fleet pass, and so do vitest (`fleet-defs`, 27) and svelte-check (0 errors). After review, live on the same stack: a hire failed (registry refused), its row aged two hours in the database, and it was still on the roster with its Retry. A member holding `agents.manage` who does not manage the agent pressed Retry in the UI and got "only this agent's managers (or an admin) can retry its hire" under the row. The admin's Retry answered 200 with the derived run id, and the agent was up and healthy in about 20 s. Retrying that failed row again got 409 "a newer hire of this agent exists". A finished hire got 409 "only a failed hire can be retried". A draft started by hand since its hire failed got 409 "… has run since this hire failed … press Start on Rv Three instead". Two Retries at once on one failed hire gave 200 and 409, and one retry run. Before the fix in this round, the second answered 500: the run store re-wraps the duplicate-key error. compose v2.31.0's json events (the production image's Alpine package) are pinned from a real capture inside `alpine:3.21`. Live-DB tests (`api/tests/it/agent_hire_retry.rs`) pin `may_act`, the newest-hire query, the derived id's 409 and the listing clause, and a unit test pins the stop-cancel. Each one failed with its target broken (always-allow, always-newest, never-retried, no aged clause, no stop check) and passed restored.

- **Fixed: the Admin → Search choice for agents reaches every agent's config.yaml again, so agents search with the picked provider and stop falling back to Hermes's keyless public tiers once the operator has turned them off.** The render built the `web:` block (`search_backend`, `extract_backend`, and `keyless_fallback: false` / `keyless_rescue: false` unless the public tiers are allowed) but never wrote it. A branch merge (24ed46e2) dropped the one `merge_into` call from `render_fleet`, and only the vendor-key env loop was restored afterwards. So an agent ran on Hermes's own resolution (`search_backend: ''`, `keyless_fallback: True`). The picked vendor was ignored, a failing provider fell through to the anonymous Exa, Parallel, Firecrawl and Keenable tiers, and Admin → Search's "rendered" preview described a config no agent had. The fleet-owned steps that shape each agent's config (secret passthrough, approvals, Nous off, delegation, the toolset floor, the search choice, the local-browser close, guardrails, title generation, model routes, config version) now run from one function, `fleet_owned_config`, so a test runs the same sequence as the render. A changed choice also moves the agent's start fingerprint, so the next roll recreates the container. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-fleet-render` (two new tests: the choice is read back from the written config.yaml text with the def's own `web:` keys merged, no choice leaves the block alone, and the choice moves the start fingerprint; with the `merge_into` line removed both fail, the first reading `{extract_char_limit: 9000, search_backend: ddgs}`) and `bun run gate`. Live on a worktree stack at rc 65dbae86 with one agent on the pinned `nousresearch/hermes-agent:v0.22.4@sha256:7a69…` and no model calls: Admin → Search set to SearXNG for search, Firecrawl (a fake key) for pages, public tiers off. On the rc binary, `POST /api/fleet/render` answered 200 and left config.yaml byte-identical with no `web:` key (same mtime), while the preview and the compose env (`FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`) showed the choice. On the fixed binary the same render wrote `web: {search_backend: searxng, extract_backend: firecrawl, keyless_fallback: false, keyless_rescue: false}` and moved `talaria.config-start-hash`. A roll recreated the agent, and inside it Hermes's `load_config()` read those four values; its own resolvers answered search `searxng`, extract `firecrawl`, keyless tier off, rescue off. Against the rc render's config in the same container they answered search `firecrawl`, keyless tier on, rescue on. Not exercised: a live `web_search` / `web_extract` call, and the Admin → Search page in a browser. CI is the compile and test proof line for the rest of the workspace.

- **Fixed: an app's grants belong to the repository installed under its slug, so a different repository installed under the same slug starts with no grants; app code can no longer read or run on another app's model setting; and the harness docs' free probe now sees the harness's own.** Uninstall used to leave every person's and team's grants on the app (`/x/<slug>`, `/x/<slug>/manage`) on their rows. A different repository installed later under the same slug, even after `keptData: "wipe"`, then inherited every one of them: its members reached the work and manage surfaces nobody had granted it, against "enabling one gives members nothing". Grants are named by slug alone, so they are now tied to the record of the repository that the slug's data directory keeps (`source.json`, repository identity = host plus the owner/name path, compared without case). Short of a wipe, uninstall keeps that record, alone when the app stored nothing, and keeps the grants with it. The record is taken from the host's own `app_sources` row whenever there is one, so a record the running app wrote in its own data directory cannot vouch for another repository. Keeping it means uninstalling and reinstalling the same repository leaves who may use the app as it was. A wipe removes them and their denials from users and teams along with the data. An install keeps them only when the record names its own repository, even when it wipes its own data. Another repository starts with none whether it adopts the data or wipes it, and so does any install of a slug whose grants no record vouches for, which covers grants an uninstall left behind before this release. Before it places the new app, the install also removes the other repository's record, so a failed write can never leave that record vouching for the new app's grants. A renamed or transferred repository has a new URL and counts as another repository: `keptData: "adopt"` hands its data over but not its grants, so grant the app again. Other apps' views, a slug that begins with this one's included, and core views are never touched. Install and uninstall answer `grantsRemoved`, and their audit rows carry it. Manage → Apps says it after an install, and the uninstall prompt says that deleting the data takes the grants too. **What an admin should do:** this release does not clean up a grant that another repository already inherited, because that repository's own record now vouches for it, and no migration can tell an inherited grant from a given one. Where a slug was reused for another repository before this release, review who holds `/x/<slug>` and `/x/<slug>/manage`. The free probe `resolveHarnessModel` and the free `runHarness` used to take a `model.slot` from app code as written, so an app could resolve or run on `app:<other>/<id>`: another app's admin-assigned model. Both now keep a slot only when it is the calling app's own, as the host knows it (`appInScope`), and log the rest as ignored. They read the spec once into a copy the host built, so a getter or a Proxy cannot show the check one slot and the chain another. The harness docs' bridge example guarded its run with `resolveHarnessModel(triage.model)`. That spec carries no slot, while `ctx.harness.run` resolves `app:<slug>/<harness id>` first, so wherever the admin's assignment was the only model that routed, the probe answered null. The example, the export table, the SDK reference and the apps skill now probe with `{ ...def.model, slot: \`app:${ctx.app}/${def.id}\` }`. Verified: `cargo test -p talaria-apps --lib -- --include-ignored lifecycle::` against a migrated Postgres, 12 passed, in three full runs of the module. One earlier run had failed once in the unchanged update test (two stray requests at its mock host), and the failure did not recur in six further runs. The live test `grants_go_back_only_to_their_own_repository` covers a member and a team holding allowed and denied views, with a case-variant denial, a `<slug>-two` app and core views. It walks through these cases: keep and reinstall; another repository refused, then wiped; explicit adopt; the same repository wiping its own data; an uninstall with nothing stored, where the record stays alone, the grants stay and a repair keeps them; a record written from `app_sources` for an unrecorded install; another repository over a lone record, which installs fresh with the grants gone; a wipe; and an orphan. On this fix's base it failed at "another repository", with all of A's grants still held. The vitest cases for the slot guard, including a getter slot and a Proxy spec, fail against the guard without the snapshot. The unit test `the_host_row_wins_over_a_record_the_app_could_write`, plus a forged-record step and a failed-record-write step in the live test, fail with the file preferred and with the `forget_data_source` call removed, respectively. `bun run gate` passes. Live on a worktree stack at rc 678dd627, with scratch repositories under one slug and test users. On rc's api, after uninstalling X keeping its data and installing Y with `keptData: "wipe"`, Y answered 200 to every member granted X. On the fixed api they got 403, `appGrants: []`, and `grantsRemoved: 3`, and the first install after rc's uninstalls dropped the 3 grants those uninstalls had left. A same-repository reinstall kept its grants (200), and a wipe removed them (`grantsRemoved: 2`). With the real app host every app got its database when built, UI-only ones included, so the lone-record path ran only in the Rust live test. A scratch app running the doc's probe answered `bare: null` and `slotted: {model: "Z.ai coding/glm-4.7-flash", step: "slot"}`. When it named kit-notes's assigned slot it answered `foreign: null`, and the host logged `named the slot "app:kit-notes/kit-notes:tidy-title", which is not app "fb12probe"'s own`. No model call was made. Not exercised: the Manage → Apps notice and prompt in a browser, the plugin approval install path (it calls the same `install_app`), and a GitHub or Forgejo source (the identity rule is the existing `same_repo`, unit-tested on GitHub URLs).

- **Fixed: an app's server-side code can import `zod` again — `import { z } from 'zod'` in `server.ts`, `mcp.ts`, `harnesses/` or a `lib/schema.ts` they share builds, loads and updates, as the SDK promised before this release; it had been refused by name, so the first boot after the upgrade would have turned such an app off.** `zod` is now a shared server package, like `@talaria/sdk/server`, and it is the same module the SDK re-exports as `z`: a built `server.js` imports it from the host's runtime file `rt-zod.js` beside `rt-talaria-sdk-server.js`, both re-exporting the host's one zod (named, whole and default imports alike), never a copy bundled into the app. The SDK kit carries the same runtime file, so `talaria-app build` and the host link an app the same way, and `talaria-app check` typechecks a bare `zod` and maps it for the app's own tests. In dev, where an app's server-side code loads from source, `zod` resolves from the host as svelte does; an update that added a zod import used to roll back with "Cannot find module 'zod'". Only the bare entry is shared: `zod/mini` fails the build by name, and so does zod in a surface, with a sentence saying a surface takes its types by `import type`. The refusal of every other unshared package is unchanged.

  Verified: reproduced first on rc 65dbae86. The rc SDK kit's `talaria-app build` of a fixture whose `lib/schema.ts`, `server.ts` and `mcp.ts` import zod (named, `* as`, and default) failed with `"zod" is not shared with apps`, and its `check` failed with 5 "Cannot find module 'zod'" errors. On this branch's own dev stack (app :5309, api :5409), installing that fixture failed `server failed to load: Cannot find module 'zod'`, and updating an installed copy to the zod commit rolled back with the same error. The owner's leadworks and waypoint (scratch clones, read only) both failed the rc kit's build with the zod sentence. With the fix: the same update applied (`rolledBack: false`); the fresh install rebuilt `ready` and enabled; its route reported zod from `'zod'` (named, namespace and default) identical to the SDK's `z` and `instanceof` across them; and `parseBody` with the app's own zod schema answered 400 with zod's issue and 200 with defaults filled. A host built from the branch (`bun run build`) emits `dist/server/runtime/rt-zod.js` and keeps zod external in both shims. The production `server-entry.ts` rebuilt the fixture with `server.js` linked to `rt-zod.js` and `rt-talaria-sdk-server.js`, no zod bundled, and it served the same identity report. After the host build id was changed and the server rebooted (an upgrade's first boot), the boot sweep rebuilt every installed app under the new key: the fixtures and a leadworks install, with `server.js`, `mcp.js` and `harnesses.js` all `ready`. The branch's kit built leadworks (6 MCP tools, 4 harnesses) and waypoint (5 tools, 4 harnesses) `ready` with the probe ok, and the fixture's kit-built `server.js` imported natively under node reported one zod. The new tests (app-build, specifiers, SDK kit) fail on rc's code and pass here, among them a dev server that imports zod from the host first and then from an app. `bun run check` and `bun run gate` pass on the branch merged with rc 346c222b. Not verified: a production container image, a real instance upgrade, macOS or Windows hosts.

- **Fixed: an app's server-side code can import `zod/v4` as well as `zod` — the same host copy, so `instanceof ZodError` holds across the two names and the SDK's `z`; main's in-host build bundled `zod/v4`, so refusing it was a small regression for main upgraders.** `zod/v4` is linked to the host's `rt-zod.js`, exactly as bare `zod` is (the host's zod is ^4, where `zod/v4` is the same API), and the SDK kit typechecks it and maps it for the app's own tests. `zod/mini`, a different API, is still refused, and the refusals now say what they mean: `zod/mini` in a surface used to be told "shared with server-side modules only", which implied it is shared, and a server-side subpath was told the host shares "its listed subpaths only" when there are none; they now say it is not shared with apps and name `@talaria/sdk/server`, `zod` (or `zod/v4`) and node's builtins as what is. Upgrade notes, from the #649 review: an app that a boot of an earlier rc already switched off for importing zod stays disabled until an admin re-enables it in Manage → Apps (the rebuild is `ready`, the enabling is not automatic); an SDK kit downloaded from an rc host before #649 still refuses `zod` (and before this, `zod/v4`) and needs a fresh download; reverting #649 brings the refusal of zod back, so switch an app's imports to the SDK's `z` before rolling back.  The shipped `talaria-apps` skill teaches agents the same rule, and the build recipe is bumped to 5 so an app that failed on `zod/v4` under the old recipe rebuilds on dev and checkout installs, where the host build id does not move.

  Verified: the new tests fail on rc's code (8 of the 68 in `specifiers.test.ts`, `build.test.ts` and `sdk-kit.test.ts`) and pass here. They build an app whose server imports `zod/v4` (named, whole and default) next to `zod` and the SDK's `z`, check `server.js` links `rt-zod.js` with no zod source bundled, load it and see one module with a `safeParse` error that is `instanceof` the SDK's `ZodError`; check every export of `zod/v4` is the very value `zod` exports; load a dev-server app file that imports `zod/v4` after the host imported `zod` and get the same `z`; check the kit's tsconfig maps `zod/v4` and not `zod/mini` and its vitest config aliases `zod/v4` to the zod shim; and check `zod/mini` and `zod/v4/core` are refused by name in a server module and a surface. `bun run gate` passes. Not verified: a live instance, a production container image, or a host build's `dist/server/runtime/rt-zod.js` (unchanged by this; #649's captures cover it).

- **Fixed: a restart or a stop leaves the chat thread usable.** A reply cut off by an api restart no longer holds its thread for 15 minutes: each process stamps the replies it writes every 10 s, and a `streaming` reply nobody has stamped for 120 s (450 s for one nothing has written since it was made, which a container from before this release may still be waiting on) is closed at boot or on the next beat, its words kept and the reason after them. A message sent after the restart is answered once the reply is closed; one queued before the restart is answered by the thread's next send. A stop before the model spoke no longer saves Hermes' "Operation interrupted…" notice as the reply, and a stopped turn files no "replied" notification. A stop Hermes could not place inside its 10 s window is sent again until it lands (`held: true`) instead of a 502 the page swallowed; a stop the agent refuses still answers 502, and the page now says when a stop is held or did not reach the agent.

  Verified: on the rel-fleet stack (api :5407, Postgres :5607) against a mock Hermes API server that mirrors v0.22.4's completions wire. On rc 65dbae86: a stop before the first token stored "Operation interrupted: waiting for model response (2.8s elapsed)." and filed "Rfops replied"; a stop Hermes answered `409 not_found` for 20 s got a 502 at 9.6 s and the agent finished; after a `kill -9` mid-reply and a restart, the follow-up answered 202 and was still unanswered 3 min 25 s later. On this branch: the same restart closed the reply 120 s after its last stamp and answered the follow-up a second later; with the api down 130 s, boot closed it and the next send ran at once; a turn that sent no byte for 150 s stayed alive; the early stop landed empty and stopped with no notification; the unplaced stop answered `held` at 9.3 s and landed at 22.9 s. Live tests `orphan_live` (8, four runs) and `stop_landing_live` (3) fail against rc's code and pass here, including a reply nothing has written since it was made surviving the sweep at 200 s and closing at 500 s, and a revived orphan landing without its `orphaned` stamp; unit tests pin Hermes' exact notice shapes (a reply that merely begins "Operation interrupted" keeps its words), the stop classifier (only `409 not_found`, `503 storage_unavailable` or no answer are sent again), and one patient sender per turn.

- **Changed: CI runs a job whenever a file it reads changes, not only when its own directory does. The release docs roll the changelog through a pull request, which is the only way flow-guard lets it reach rc.** ci.yml's `changes` job skips a job whose surface did not move, and a skipped required check reports success. Several surfaces left out files their jobs depend on. The e2e surface had none of the crates behind this release's three notification specs, so a pull request touching only `talaria-notify`, `-realtime`, `-push` or `-routes-comms` skipped e2e. It now also lists `-realtime-watch`, `-channels`, `-tz` (the "until tomorrow 9:00" zone math), `-session`, `-api-facades`, the api binary (`api/src`), the workspace `api/Cargo.toml`, and the chassis template the job copies in for the hire. The desktop job never ran for `ui/src/lib/dither-engine.ts`, which the launcher bundles as `@dither`. desktop-package.yml's `paths` gain it too, so an edit to it on main builds the installers again. The ui surface gains the fixtures it shares with the api (`api/tests/it/fixtures/`), the three Rust sources its tests hold their tables to, the chassis template and workbench image files, `check-invariants.mjs` and the secretbox vector generator. The cli surface gains every api `.rs` file (box.test.ts reads them for env keys), `docs/CONTAINER.md`, the devbox compose and `.gitignore`. The api surface gains the chassis template, the Hermes toolset and skill-authority files, `scripts/skills/`, and `mcp/src/index.ts`. `RELEASING.md` and the cut-release skill used to say "push the roll commit" to rc and "releasing never edits a file". flow-guard refuses any rc tip that is not a merge. They now give the roll as a branch from rc and a pull request, merged before the tag. Two older changelog entries now match the house format. The README entry's `## ` headings would have become three fake version sections in a rolled CHANGELOG.md. The 2026-10-28 stop entry gains its `Verified:` paragraphs. talaria-state's live tests name their schemas with a per-process counter, so two parallel tests can no longer get the same name and fail `create schema` on a duplicate key, as they did on CI.

  Verified: the `Which surfaces moved` script, extracted from both ci.yml versions and run in bash on one file at a time. On origin/rc, the four notify crates, `-channels`, `-tz`, `-session`, `-api-facades`, `api/src/main.rs` and `api/Cargo.toml` ran only `api`. `dither-engine.ts` ran `ui,e2e` but not desktop. The chassis template, the Hermes files, `scripts/skills/`, the workbench image files, `check-invariants.mjs`, the vector generator, `docs/CONTAINER.md`, the devbox compose and `.gitignore` ran no job at all. On this branch each file runs the jobs that read it. An unrelated crate (`talaria-kb`) still skips e2e, and docs, changelog and README edits still run nothing. The roll, run in a scratch copy and never in the repo: on origin/rc it writes `## What actually happened`, `## The fix` and `## Verification` at CHANGELOG.md lines 3015, 3037 and 3045. On this branch it writes none, and `changelog-roll.mjs --check` passes all 645 entries. `cargo test -p talaria-state` passes (2 tests, 3 live ones ignored without a database). CI's live-tests job runs those three against Postgres. `bun run check` and `bun run gate` pass.

- **Fixed: Talaria Desktop always has a way back when an instance's page does not come up.** While an instance restarts behind Cloudflare, its page could hang for 100 seconds and end on Cloudflare's 524, show a 502 or a challenge, or, on Windows, WebView2's network error page — in a window with no close, minimize or drag, because the styled titlebar is drawn by the page. Now a page on the instance's own address that is not Talaria puts you back on the launcher with a card saying what answered. A page that answered (an error page, a Cloudflare challenge, a sign-in gate) stays alive behind the card: **Show the page** shows it as it is, with **← Instances** at the bottom left as the way back; opening the instance any other way (its row, the tray, a notification, another instance's switcher) loads it fresh instead. Retry and Back to instances close it. A page the desktop app cannot reach into (a load that got no answer, a page where its script never answers, such as WebView2's own error page) is closed and offers no Show the page. A page that has not loaded in 25 seconds gets "<instance> is not answering", with Keep waiting. If Talaria comes up while a card is up, it opens by itself. On a page on another address (a sign-in provider the gate sent you on to), ← Instances and Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+H still take you back to the launcher — a real click or key press, for the page on screen, once a second — and the instance opens fresh next time; Ctrl+Q works only on the instance's own address (the system's own quit works everywhere). No page, frame or script can quit Talaria Desktop or send you to the launcher from the background, and no page can quit it in its first seconds after launch. A page with Talaria up is never interrupted, older Talaria versions included (their titlebar's call counts, and a page still starting is looked at again about 8 and 20 seconds after it loads); pages on other addresses are never judged; after a page that was not Talaria, Retry opens the instance's home, while a dropped connection or a stall keeps the page you were on; and an instance loaded in the background at launch that does not come up is tried again later.
  Verified: on Linux, on a private headless rig (WebDriver on the launcher, fake instances whose beacon answers so the open reaches the webview), against this change's earlier rounds. Main's real UI build with its lazy Tauri chunk 10 s late: opened, no card (the first round closed it at 3.9 s); 30 s late: the card at 21.5 s with the page kept, then opened by itself at 31.0 s. Held, then a 524: the not-answering card at 25.2 s, then the 524 card with the page kept; the instance's row then loaded it fresh, and so did another instance's switcher for a page carded while the person was elsewhere (round 2 would have shown the kept page as it was). A Cloudflare-style challenge that passes by itself: opened by itself at 7.4 s. A challenge that wants a click, under a strict CSP: Show the page, ← Instances back to the card, then the click and Talaria. A same-origin sign-in gate: Show the page, sign in, Talaria; on to another origin from the gate, the provider page's call to go back was taken (the way-back grant) while its Quit was refused; there the page's own scripted Ctrl+Shift+H, Ctrl+Q and pill click did nothing, a page calling the way back every 100 ms sent the person to the launcher once and was refused from the background while they used another instance (which stayed on screen), and the instance then opened fresh; a page whose own script asked three times in 1.3 s was taken once a second. A page holding a sandboxed microsite frame and a plain frame aimed at the earlier build's `talaria-desktop.invalid` ways back: each navigation refused, nothing taken, the app still running, and the frame saw no IPC. Real presses were driven in Chromium against the shell's exact scripts (this rig's headless compositor takes no injected input into the window): a real Ctrl+Shift+H, Ctrl+Q, click and Enter on the pill each reached the shell, and the scripted ones did not. A page whose script never answers: the card at 29.8 s, the page closed, no Show the page. A share page as the last page: Retry opened the root; a dropped connection kept the last page, and Retry went back to it. Unit tests cover each rule and every row of the decision after a page finishes. `bun run gate` passes its check; its desktop cargo cannot build on this host (no GTK headers), so fmt, clippy and the 162 tests (with rc merged in) ran in the Fedora 44 rig image. Not verified: Windows and macOS at run time (WebView2's own error pages among them, and the way-back grant there), the tray's entry (this rig has no tray; it takes the same `activate` as the switcher), a real instance behind Cloudflare.

- **Changed: Talaria Desktop tells you when a new version is out. It checks on its own, 30 seconds after launch and then every 6 hours, and shows a small chip, "Talaria Desktop 0.13.0 is available", with Update and Later — on the launcher, and over whichever instance you have open, whatever Talaria version that instance runs. Over an instance it looks for room, since instances run different Talaria versions: where the top bar's middle is empty (an older Talaria's titlebar, the tab bar on a wide window) it sits there as one row, covering nothing you type or read; where tabs fill that middle, or with the OS titlebar or none, it starts as a small pill just below the top bar, where nothing under it takes a click — across the bar's lower edge on a small window zoomed in. It never moves while the pointer is on it, and stops measuring the page once it is gone. "–" makes it a small pill at any time, even while an update downloads, and the pill keeps counting; a small window or a page zoomed in starts with the pill. Later puts that version off for a day, everywhere at once and across a relaunch; a newer version shows straight away. Update downloads it with its progress showing, checks its signature, installs it and restarts Talaria (on Windows the installer runs on its own and reopens the app); a download that has had nothing arrive for a minute is given up with a sentence and Update is offered again, however slow the connection otherwise is. Where the app cannot replace itself — a Linux .deb, .rpm, pacman or Flatpak install, a Windows .msi install, or a Mac copy still running from its disk image — the chip says how to update instead and offers only Later, and Check for updates no longer offers an Install that could not work (on a .deb or .rpm it downloaded the AppImage and then refused it).** The shell checked only when someone pressed Check for updates on the launcher or in Settings → Profile, so nobody learned about a release. The check is the same bounded one (10 s), off the main thread; a check that fails is only a log line, and tries again an hour later. Update's own look at the feed is bounded at 20 s; the download's only bound besides the minute without bytes is a 4-hour backstop for a download that trickles forever, whose sentence points to github.com/outcrop-labs/talaria/releases. The chip over an instance is the shell's own, put into the page by the shell (it needs nothing from the instance's UI, reappears after a reload, and is never put into a sign-in provider's page); a failed install, or one that panics, shows "↑ Update failed" instead of staying on "Updating", and opening it gives the sentence saying why.
  Verified: on Linux, on a private headless rig (its own mutter and session bus, WebDriver on the launcher), with a test build of the shell (version 0.12.0) reading a fake `latest.json` on localhost and trusting a throwaway signing key. As a package install (no `$APPIMAGE`): the feed was asked 30.4 s after launch and the chip appeared on the launcher with Later only and the package sentence, and in the instance page opened next; `install_update` refused with the same sentence; Later in the page took the chip down in the page and on the launcher and wrote `updateSnooze` for 0.13.0 exactly 24 h out; a manual check of the same version stayed put off; the feed saying 0.13.1 brought the chip back in both views at once; a feed answering 500 left it as it was and said so in a sentence; and a relaunch with the feed on the version put off showed no chip in either view. As an AppImage (`$APPIMAGE` set, as the AppImage runtime sets it), on a page whose `style-src 'self'` refused its own inline styles: the chip sat at [474, 4, 806, 32] in a 1280-wide window, centred, its buttons at 11 px weight 600, styled by its constructed sheet; a payload that stopped after half its bytes was dropped 60.8 s after Update with "The download stopped: nothing arrived for 60 seconds, so nothing was installed. Try Update again.", the AppImage untouched; on a page where a constructed sheet never applies, the chip was styled through CSSOM instead (the same 6 px radius, 11 px buttons); and a 200 KB payload trickled at 10 KB a second showed its progress (4 %, 14 %), was made a pill mid-download ("↑ Updating 29%", then 44 %, 59 %), finished without being cancelled, and replaced and relaunched the AppImage; a signature that did not match said so and installed nothing. Over the real Talaria UI (its own vite dev server, the api mocked, Chromium, the shell's chip script evaluated into the page as the shell does), at 1000 and 1600 px wide, on a channel with a four-line draft in the composer and on a thread in the side panel, with three toasts up: the chip, the installing chip and its pill each sat inside the 36 px titlebar, clear of the window controls, and overlapped no composer, send button or toast. In round 3, over the real UI in each titlebar mode at 1000 and 1600 px (Chromium, the chip script evaluated as the shell does, counting only controls that could be hit under it): on main's UI (a 36 px titlebar) with the themed titlebar, the row sat in it and touched nothing; on rc's UI, whose tab bar is the titlebar, it was the pill below the bar at 1000 px and the row in the bar's empty middle at 1600 px; with the OS titlebar or none, the pill at [466, 62, 535, 83] (1000 px) touched nothing, and opened, the row overlapped the header's star button by 3 px at 1000 px; a failed install folded to "↑ Update failed" everywhere; four progress pushes changed the title in place and kept the same nodes; a 760 × 600 window at 175 % zoom (434 CSS px) started with the pill, across the tab bar's lower edge at [183, 46, 252, 67], touching nothing (opened, the row covers the end of the sidebar's search until it is folded), and on main's UI in the titlebar. On the rig the shell put the row 4 px down with the themed titlebar, moved it to the pill at 62 px when the launcher switched to the OS titlebar and to none, and back when it switched back. Unit tests cover the snooze (a day, a newer version, a pre-release, an unparseable version, a clock that went back), which copies are offered Update on each OS, the download's bounds (an AppImage at 256 kbit/s is never stopped), progress, an install that panics, the error sentences, the page script and the log saying each change of the chip once, not each percent. The connect smoke passes on the rig. `bun run gate` passes its check and the ui typecheck and tests (the desktop typecheck passes on its own); its desktop clippy cannot build on this host, which has no GTK headers, so fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and the 146 tests ran in the Fedora 44 rig image. Not verified: Windows (NSIS passive install and relaunch, the .msi case) and macOS (the app's own replace, the disk-image case) at run time; the real GitHub feed; a page whose CSP restricts `script-src` or `connect-src` (only `style-src` was restricted on the rig); a panic inside an install at run time (the guard is unit-tested); WebKit's layout of the real UI (the screenshots are Chromium); Settings → Profile's package sentence inside a real instance UI (it is a template branch, typechecked only).

- **Fixed: the stop gate's sweep no longer deletes the stack of a live worktree named `<x>-fleet`. A `.talaria-keep` holds a stack's containers and volumes. A recut `wt/<name>` no longer reads as merged. `pr-watch` watches the promotion PR. Seeded stacks drop main's mail config. Local catalogs reach the api's SSRF allow-list. A new worktree never takes a stopped stack's port slot.** The sweep removed the Postgres and Redis of the running worktree `rel-fleet`. It stripped `-fleet` from every `talaria-wt-*` project, read `talaria-wt-rel-fleet` as worktree `rel`'s agents, found no `../talaria-rel`, and took the project's containers and volumes at a stop-gate turn boundary. Now a `-fleet` project has both readings, the way box projects already did, and either checkout keeps it. A `.talaria-keep` in the owning `../talaria-<name>` or box directory keeps the project, its volumes and networks. Every removal asks again at the moment it acts. "Merged" now needs a merged PR whose head is this checkout's HEAD. A recut `wt/r6-ui` sat on rc's tip with 0 commits ahead and read as finished because #629 of that name merged. `pr-watch` refused #597 (`rc` → `main`) as `base` before it read a check. It now watches a same-repository `rc` → `main` PR against `main`. It reads the head from GitHub's `rc` and points red and conflict advice at a pull request into `rc`, never a push. It also keys checks by event: the promotion runs ci.yml and flow.yml for both the push and the pull request, and a SKIPPED copy with the newer job id hid the other event's verdict. `talaria worktree` and `box seed` delete the copied `app_settings.email_config` alongside `push_vapid`, so a test notification cannot mail real users through main's provider. `talaria dev` lifts `TALARIA_FETCH_ALLOW_HOSTS` from `ui/.env` into the api, which owns the SSRF guard now. `talaria worktree` skips a slot whose ports any container publishes, running or stopped, or any checkout's `ui/.env` names. Verified: `bun scripts/cleanup-sweep.test.mjs` (62 checks) and `bun scripts/hooks/pr-watch.test.mjs` (51), run against rc's rules lifted into the same shapes, fail 8 and 4 of the new checks. Among them: `talaria-wt-rel-fleet` with only `../talaria-rel-fleet` checked out is an orphan on rc and kept here. The recorded #597 reads `base` on rc and green here. A recorded push-run FAILURE reads green on rc's grouping and red here. A `talaria-wt-*-fleet` network, a box held only by `.talaria-keep`, and #629's real head beside rc's tip are covered too. `cd cli && bun test` (463) and `tsc --noEmit` pass; new tests cover the scrub, the env lift and the slot claims, including the recorded port bindings of a stopped stack. On a throwaway `postgres:16-alpine` (tmpfs, no network) holding the real `app_settings` table, the scrub statement deleted `email_config` and `push_vapid`, kept `storage_config` and `github_config`, and exited 0 with no table at all. Read-only against this host: the sweep report (no `--apply`, no `--gate`) lists no orphan project. The live `docker compose ls` judged with the `../talaria-rel` placeholder ignored makes rc's rule remove the running `talaria-wt-rel-fleet` and the fix remove nothing. `pr-watch --pr 597` settles green (34 checks, 10 skipped) where rc exits `base`. With slots 1 to 9 recorded, rc's picker hands out slot 3 (the stopped `talaria-work-view`) and the fix hands out slot 10. Not exercised: a sweep `--apply` or `--gate` run, a real `talaria worktree` or `box seed`, a red or conflicted promotion on GitHub, and a loopback catalog fetched by a running api.

- **Fixed: rc's CI is green again — the notification center's Done chapter waits for the bell's count before it reads it, and the group-window expiry test no longer depends on how fast the disk is.** `notify-center-ui.spec.ts`'s "mark unread counts again" read the badge once, right after `page.goto('/notifications')`, and expected one more. On the built ui the shell mounts the bell after `goto` returns, and the bell shows 0 until its first `/api/notifications` read answers (the visible badge is blank meanwhile, as main's is), so the read said 0 and the test waited 30 s for "1" while the badge went 3 → 4, which is right. It failed the same way on push run 41499717714 and PR run 41499718207 for 65dbae86, so the promotion gate failed. The product counts are right: For you went 3 → 4 (the server said `unreadForYou` 3 and `unread` 7 at the read), so no split between For you and All explains it. The chapter now waits for the literal counts (3, then 4). `notify_contract_live::concurrent_window_expiry_never_conflicts` started four bursts 2.5 s apart on a 1 s window, timed from the spawn: when a slow disk held one burst's commits past the next burst's start, the next burst rightly joined that row (2 rows instead of 4 under IO pressure). Each burst now lands before the next starts. The person's rows are moved back past a 600 s window, so no burst ever depends on a sleep. The ten writers of a burst all queue behind the person's row lock before the first one gets it, so every run races the expiry against nine upserts. The test also checks after each burst that its ten writes are one row. No product code changed.

  Verified: `bun run gate` green (check, svelte-check, vitest 2904/2904, `talaria-api` fmt, clippy and tests); against the worktree stack running CI's shape (built ui, `bun run start`, debug api of 65dbae86), the old chapter failed 5 of 6 runs with CI's exact message (expected "1", received "4"; the call log shows 3 then 4). An instrumented copy showed the one-shot read returning "0" about 0.4 s after `goto` returned, while 1.5 s later the badge said 3. The new chapter passed 10/10 (`--repeat-each=10`) and with its first read held 400 ms, and the whole spec passed 19/19, with host IO pressure at 70–90 %. The old expiry test, with the person's row lock held for 3 s across the first burst boundary, failed (3 rows, 0 errors, 1 keyed), and it passed without the stall. The new test passed 20/20 (0.4 s each, it was 7.5 s), and `notify_contract_live` passed 7/7 both serially and the way CI runs it. A mutant that lets an expired row be adopted again fails the new test at burst 2 (one row of 20) and the old test too (1 row).

- **Fixed: the Missed-activity email fine print in Settings → Notifications follows your frequency and your Email cells — on Never it says nothing is mailed, instead of "Needs you waits 15 minutes whatever you pick".** The sentence added with the Following fix (#648) stated the Needs you delay for every pick, but the notify engine's `email_due` (`deliver.rs`) returns no due time for `off` before any class delay applies, so on Never nothing is mailed at all; and it named a delay for classes whose Email cell the person had turned off, though only a row with Email on is mailed. `mailNote` now takes the person's frequency: on Never it says "Nothing is mailed while this is Never, whatever the Email column says."; on any other pick it names a class's own delay only for a class whose effective Email cell is on, and the Following clause still follows the cells.

  Verified: the new tests fail on rc's code (3 of the 16 in `notify-matrix.test.ts`) and pass here. They pin the Never sentence (no "waits", no Following clause), that 15 minutes, hourly and daily all read as before, that a delayed class with its Email cell off (by the person or by default) is not named and is once the person turns it on, and that Settings passes the frequency. The wording was checked against `email_due` and its doc comment in `api/crates/talaria-notify/src/deliver.rs`. `bun run gate` passes. Not verified: in a browser, or by mail delivery.

- **Fixed: a page loaded while the api restarts (every deploy) says "Could not reach the server." instead of "[object Object]", Home's Inbox tab counts what the bell counts, the notification settings say what Desktop and Email actually do, and an empty direct message no longer reads "Welcome to #Dana Okafor".** While the api is down, the app's proxy answers every `/api/*` path with 502 `{"error":{"message":"upstream unreachable"}}`. It keeps that OpenAI-style shape because it also fronts `/api/llm/v1/*`. The browser's one fetch door read only the house `{"error":"…"}` and handed the object to `new Error()`. So every surface, the session gate, the bell and the hire modal said "[object Object]". `fetch-json.ts`'s `errorSentence` now reads both envelopes, and anything that is not a non-empty string becomes "request failed (N)". `errorMessage` maps the proxy's "upstream unreachable" to the same "Could not reach the server." a bare "Failed to fetch" gets. Home's Inbox tab badge used `/api/home`'s `unread`, which counts every unread row, while the bell counts For you, so one ticket move showed INBOX 2 beside a bell of 1. The tab now reads the bell's own query through the same `badgeCount`. The dock's Inbox icon is the decision queue and keeps its own number. Settings → Notifications: the Desktop column said it banners "while you are not looking at Talaria", but unticking it also stops the in-app pop-up. It now says it is the pop-up while you look and the banner while you do not, and that with it off neither shows. In-app no longer claims every notification is "counted on the bell". The missed-activity line said "Following is never mailed", while Channel activity mails by default. That line is now built from the server's class registry and your own Email cells ("Needs you waits 15 minutes whatever you pick. Under Following, only Channel activity is mailed."). An empty DM shows "The start of your conversation with <name>" and "Say something to <first name>." under a ◈, not a channel's `#` hero; a DM with agents keeps the "@mention … to bring the agents in" hint. `docs/NOTIFICATIONS.md` loses its wave-1 text: the path diagram names the delivery decision, the deferred push and the missed-activity mail; the stream resumes by seq; I-3 carries the v2 record; the read-sync event is described; and the Safari entry says what presence does and does not stop. Verified: 13 new tests in `fetch-json.test.ts`, `notify-center.test.ts`, `notify-matrix.test.ts` and `comms-dm.test.ts`, 12 of them failing against rc's sources (`getJson` gave "[object Object]"; the 13th pins the edge's own HTML 524, unchanged); live on a worktree stack in headless Chromium, with the api stopped and the app server up, 7 surfaces (home, boards, comms, notifications, settings, agents, manage) went from "Could not reach your session — [object Object]" to "… — Could not reach the server.", and the hire door went from `{"error":"[object Object]"}` to the same sentence; a DM plus a ticket move by a teammate gave `unreadForYou 1` / `unread 2`, and INBOX 2 beside bell 1 became INBOX 1 beside bell 1; Settings showed the new column titles, and the mail line changed to "only Work finished and Channel activity are mailed" when that row's Email was turned on through the matrix's own PATCH; in a looked-at tab a DM toasted in 198 ms with Desktop on, and with Desktop off it showed nothing while the bell went 0 → 1 (row `alert: feed`); an empty 1:1 DM and an empty group DM showed the new text, and an empty #channel kept "Welcome to #fb7-empty"; `bun run gate`.

- **Fixed: slow agent controls, chat to a stopped agent, and cron changes to a stalled agent answer inside Cloudflare's 100 s instead of showing its 524.** Every real instance sits behind a Cloudflare tunnel, which answers 524 for a request whose origin has sent no headers for 100 s. The agent control route (start, stop, restart, retire, re-hire, delete) and the def and MCP edits' apply waited up to 210 s before answering 202 "still working" — sized for the app proxy's 300 s — so a slow verb (a cold pull of a new pin, a slow disk, a health wait) reached the person as "request failed (524)" while it went on and landed; they now answer within 75 s, the 202's read of the container is bounded at 10 s (a slow daemon says `unknown`), and a const assert naming Cloudflare keeps the whole answer under 85 s. A chat to an agent that is stopped or restarting held its headers for two minutes (first byte at 124 s) before the "restarting (or down)" reply; a turn a person is reading now holds 80 s and the sentence says so ("didn't come back within 80 seconds"), while channel replies and harness turns nobody waits on keep the two-minute hold, and the hold's last attempt lands on its deadline instead of up to 5 s past it. A cron create, pause, resume, run, edit or delete that the agent took and did not answer within 40 s (Hermes writes its jobs file under a lock and an fsync, which stalls on a starved disk) answered 400 "cannot reach … no answer within 40s" for a change that then landed; it is now a 503 saying the change may still land and to check the job list before trying again, while refusals keep their 400.
  Verified: `bun run gate` (check, ui typecheck + test, and the `talaria-agent-crons`, `talaria-fleet-docker`, `talaria-gateway` and `talaria-routes-fleet` packages' clippy and tests), with new tests that fail on the old values: the edge budget and the bounded 202 read, the attended hold window and the hold's last pause, the 80-second sentence, the may-still-land wording, and the 503 mapping. Live on a worktree stack (the pinned Hermes v0.22.4 agent on a recording mock model, no real model calls), each case first on the rc binary: a start under heavy IO answered 202 at 210.0 s and a stop 503 at 161.7 s on rc, and a start held 150 s by a docker shim with a 30 s inspect answered 202 `state: unknown` at 85.0 s here; a chat to the stopped agent had its first byte at 124.1 s on rc and at 80.1 s here, with the 80-second sentence; a cron create the stalled real agent never answered was a 400 on rc and landed in its jobs file eight minutes later, and against a stand-in agent that applies each write 60 s after taking it, a pause answered 400 on rc and landed, while a resume and a create answered 503 with the may-still-land sentence here and landed, and a run on a paused job and an unknown job kept their 400. Not verified through a real Cloudflare tunnel (the cutoff is reasoned from the measured first byte), nor in the UI beyond the route's sentence, which the Crons panel shows as-is.

- **Fixed: on Linux, a stable Talaria Desktop installs over its RC as the upgrade it is, the tray entry is named "Talaria", an AppImage's banners carry its own icon and desktop entry, and a suspended instance's ack that never reached the server is sent once more.** Release candidates sorted above their release in all three Linux package formats, so `dnf`, `apt` and `pacman` refused the stable package over an RC as a downgrade. Tauri stamps the tag's `0.12.0-rc.1` into the deb and rpm as written: dpkg reads that as 0.12.0 with Debian revision `rc.1`, and rpm (where the rewrite made it `0.12.0_rc.1`) and pacman (`0.12.0_rc.1`) read the extra `rc` segment as newer. The deb and rpm `Version` is now `0.12.0~rc.1` (`~` sorts before everything, the end of the string included; `packaging/linux/recommend-tray.sh`, which now also checks the order with each format's own compare), and the pacman `pkgver` is `0.12.0rc.1` (pacman has no `~`; `pack-pacman.sh`). The file names keep the tag's spelling, and `desktop-package.yml` asserts the deb and rpm carry the stamped version in that spelling. The tray item's StatusNotifierItem Title, which Plasma shows as the entry's name, read `app.talaria.desktop`: libayatana falls back to GLib's application name, which falls back to the program name. The shell now sets the application name to `Talaria`; the program name (X11 `WM_CLASS`, the Wayland `app_id`) stays `app.talaria.desktop`. An AppImage's banners named the desktop entry `app.talaria.desktop` and the icon by that name, neither of which an AppImage ships or installs, so a banner showed a generic icon. They now name the `Talaria.desktop` at the AppImage's mount root, and the icon by its path there (`$APPDIR/talaria-desktop.png`, else `.DirIcon`), since a notification server looks icon names up only in its own theme. An AppImage integrated under v0.11.0 (Gear Lever, AppImageLauncher) keeps that version's `StartupWMClass=talaria-desktop`, so after the in-app update its window no longer groups under the pin: integrate it again. A suspended instance's watcher acks every banner it posts so the phone's push 60 s later is cancelled, and a lost ack let that push fire. An ack that hit a transport error, or a gateway's 502, 503 or 504 (a Cloudflare tunnel answers 502 while the origin restarts), is now sent once more 2 s later, on its own task so it never holds up the next banner. A 4xx or any other answer is not retried.

  Verified: each item reproduced first. **Version order:** with dpkg 1.23.7, rpm 6.0.2 (`labelCompare` and `rpm.vercmp`) and pacman 7.0.0's `vercmp`, `0.12.0-rc.1` (dpkg) and `0.12.0_rc.1` (rpm, pacman) sort above `0.12.0`, and pacman puts `0.12.0~rc.1` above it too. The new spellings sort below, with rc.1 < rc.2 < rc.10, an RC above the previous release, and a trunk `0.0.0~sha…` below `0.0.0`. The last desktop-package run's packages (b85b0339) carry deb `0.0.0-shab85b0339900f`, rpm `0.0.0_shab85b0339900f` and pacman `0.0.0_shab85b0339900f-1`. **Packaging dry run**, in a Fedora 44 container with dpkg, rpm, rpmbuild and pacman: Tauri's own deb and rpm bundlers (`tauri bundle` over the rig's debug build, symbols stripped), stamped `0.12.0-rc.1`, `0.12.0` and `0.0.0-sha678dd6271661` the way the workflow stamps them, then rc's and this branch's `recommend-tray.sh` and `pack-pacman.sh`. rc's left the RC and the trunk build above their release in all three formats. This branch's writes `0.12.0~rc.1` and `0.0.0~sha678dd6271661` (pacman `0.12.0rc.1-1`, `0.0.0sha678dd6271661-1`), which sort below. It leaves `0.12.0` as it is, the rebuilt rpm carries the same files, and the workflow's new check, run verbatim, passes for all three. **Tray:** on a private headless rig (its own mutter, session bus and a recording notification server with a StatusNotifierWatcher), the rc build's tray item read `Title app.talaria.desktop`; this build's reads `Talaria`, with the GTK application and program name still `app.talaria.desktop`. **AppImage:** the CI AppImage (b85b0339, whose `linux.rs` equals rc's) run under its own runtime on that rig posted `desktop-entry app.talaria.desktop` with icon `app.talaria.desktop`. Its live FUSE mount holds `Talaria.desktop` (`Icon=talaria-desktop`), `talaria-desktop.png` (128x128) and `.DirIcon`. This build, with `APPIMAGE` and `APPDIR` set to that mount, posted `desktop-entry Talaria` with icon `/tmp/.mount_Talari…/talaria-desktop.png`. **Ack:** new tests run the watcher's own HTTP client against a fake instance that hangs up mid-request, answers 502, 403, or fails twice. A lost or 502 ack is sent exactly twice and lands; a 403 is sent once; a second loss is the last try. Desktop fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and 123 tests pass in the rig image (`talaria-desk-rig:f44`). The six new tests fail with each fix put back to the old code. `bun run gate` runs check (passes) and the desktop `cargo fmt --check` (passes); its clippy then stops at `glib-sys`, because the host has no GTK headers, which is why the rig ran it. Not verified: a real GNOME or Plasma session (Plasma's tray list, GNOME's banner icon), an rpm, deb or pacman upgrade actually installed over an RC, a release-profile bundle and the AppImage, which only CI builds, and a watcher ack lost on a real instance behind Cloudflare.

- **Fixed: web push no longer reaches inside the server's network — a push subscription's endpoint must be a public address (the safe-fetch policy, checked when the subscription is filed, before every POST and again when the socket connects), the push edge follows no redirect, a refusal reads back one sentence whatever it hit, and a person keeps at most 20 device browsers.** Any signed-in member could file `https://127.0.0.1:<port>/…`, an RFC1918 address or the 169.254.169.254 metadata service as a "device", fire the per-device test push, and read back how long the answer took and up to 512 characters of it (`POST /api/notifications/test`; `GET /api/push/devices` kept the same in `lastError`): an internal port scanner with a readable answer. The push client was a plain reqwest client that dialled anything https and followed up to ten redirects, and subscriptions had no per-person ceiling (500 filed in 1.3 s, every notification posted to all of them). Now `POST /api/push/subscribe` answers 400 "Push endpoint refused: not a reachable public address" for every inside target, by address or by name (`localhost`, `.internal`, `.local`, …), and for a name that does not resolve, and files nothing. The delivery edge runs the same check before each POST (rows filed before this release, a name that has moved since), dials through safe-fetch's validating resolver, takes a 3xx as the answer, and reads at most 2 KiB of an answer's body; a refused row records `refused: not a public push service address`, is never retried, and counts as a failure under the existing skip and prune rules. An operator whose push service really is on their own network admits it with `TALARIA_FETCH_ALLOW_HOSTS`, the same escape hatch every other user-supplied fetch uses. Filing a 21st device retires the one seen longest ago (a browser re-files every time it opens Talaria, so a device in use stays), and a delivery reads at most the 20 most recently seen rows, so a person filed past the cap before this release is bounded too.

  Verified: on the rel-notify-web stack (api :5405, Postgres :5605, Redis :6505), over real HTTP with throwaway `.test` members and a loopback listener that logs every connection. Before, on the rc 65dbae86 binary: subscribing and test-pushing `https://127.0.0.1:<listener>/`, a closed loopback port, `https://localhost:5405/`, `[::1]`, `169.254.169.254` and `10.255.255.1` all answered `{"ok":true}` and then `connect:` in 0–2 ms or `timeout:` in 5,001–5,002 ms, the listener logged the api's TLS ClientHello, and `GET /api/push/devices` repeated the error; 25 subscribes kept 25 rows; one DM to a person with 25 rows attempted all 25. After, on the fixed build: those six endpoints and three more (`[::ffff:127.0.0.1]`, `db.internal`, `push.invalid`) each answered 400 "Push endpoint refused: not a reachable public address" and filed nothing; six inside rows inserted directly (as if filed before the upgrade, including plain `http://127.0.0.1`) test-pushed `{"status":null,"error":"refused: not a public push service address"}` in 0–1 ms, `lastError` the same, and the listener saw no connection in either run; 25 subscribes to `fcm.googleapis.com` endpoints kept 20, the newest 06–25; the DM attempted exactly the 20 most recently seen rows; a made-up FCM endpoint still reached FCM and read back its 410 in 81 ms, a made-up Mozilla autopush endpoint its 404 in 134 ms (both rows pruned as gone). Unit tests: the edge never dials nine inside endpoints, the push client hands a 302 back and refuses `localhost` at connect time, an answer body is cut at 512 characters, the policy table, a refusal is final and counted, and the delivery query's 20-row limit; run against the rc edge, the first fails (the loopback listener was dialled 4 times), the redirect test sees 11 connections and a redirect error, and the row-limit pin fails. Live `it` against the same database: `push_live` 8/8, including the two new tests (the door through the real router: nine inside endpoints refused, 25 → 20 kept, the seen-longest-ago retired first, another person's two untouched; a delivery to 25 legacy rows posts to the newest 20), and `notify_engine_live` passes run on its own (it now admits its loopback capture server with `TALARIA_FETCH_ALLOW_HOSTS=127.0.0.1`, as the e2e stack does). `bun run gate` passes: check, then fmt, clippy `-D warnings` and tests for `talaria-api`, `talaria-push` (18) and `talaria-routes-comms` (19), 131 tests in all with the live ones ignored; it chose no desktop step (desktop is untouched).

- **Fixed: the second message of a conversation no longer buzzes your phone a minute later while you are reading it at your desk, and a Mac that resumes straight into an instance now asks for notification permission there.** A re-alert (a second DM folded into the same notification) is a new version of the row: the server forgets the first version's ack and arms a new deferred push. The page, in a browser tab and in Talaria Desktop alike, acked each notification id only once per page, so the re-alert's toast or banner was never acked and the push went out 60 s later. The page now acks each version (the row id at its `seq`, or its `createdAt` on a row from before the contract). On macOS, nothing can be shown until the person allows Talaria, and the shell asks only from a click. Until now that click lived only on the launcher's card and in Settings → Desktop. Someone who upgraded from 0.11, or relaunched after adding an instance, resumes straight into the instance and never saw either: every banner was refused, and nothing said why. While the shell reports "not determined", the instance now shows a card (once the page has been open 10 s and you have clicked or typed in it) whose Allow button runs the macOS prompt. Don't Allow says where to turn it on later, and Not now is remembered for that instance. Linux and Windows have no such prompt and never show the card.
  Verified: on this branch's own stack (app :5308, api :5408), with no push subscription in its database, so a deferred push that fires reaches no device and shows as `pushed_at` and the scheduler's "pushed 1 deferred notification(s)". In a looking headless Chromium tab, two DMs 8 s apart: on rc, one ack (for the first), `surfaced_at` NULL after the second, and the push fired 60 s later; on the fix, two acks, `surfaced_at` set again, and no push 75 s on. In Talaria Desktop on the private headless rig (rc shell build, its own mutter, D-Bus and notification recorder), with instance B on screen and unfocused and the OS input active: on rc, `Notify 2` re-alerted with no second ack and the push fired at +63 s; on the fix, both banners were acked and no push followed. The permission card was driven against a faked shell answering `desktop_notification_status` and `desktop_notification_request` as a bundled macOS shell does. In Chromium: no card at load, the card after a click, Allow → one request and the card gone for good, Don't Allow → the "off" note, Not now → no card after a relaunch, and a `granted` shell → never a card or a request. In the real shell on the rig (WebKitGTK), with the rig's proxy answering only those two commands and real clicks through mutter: no card at load, the card after a click into the page, Allow → the request and the card gone, Don't Allow → the "off" note and Close, Not now → no card and no status call after a relaunch that kept the instance's storage; with the shell's real Linux answer (`fdo`, `granted`), no card. Unit tests: the batcher acks a re-alert again (it failed on the old code, which acked an id once), and `createShellAsk` covers every path over a faked shell. `bun run gate`. Not verified on a real Mac: the macOS prompt itself is on the owner's Mac smoke list.

- **Fixed: rolling back to the previous release after the git-hosts upgrade keeps GitHub connected and the workbench writing, and Talaria's own gateway key stays metered after a rollback and a second upgrade.** The git-hosts migration (#611) deleted `app_settings.github_config` after moving it into the `github` row, dropped the `'github'` default from every `host_id`, and re-keyed `workbench_repos` and `workbench_repo_flow`. That broke the overlap contract in `docs/UPDATES.md`: during a roll's drain, after an aborted roll and after **Roll back**, the previous release runs on the migrated schema. It reported GitHub as not configured, and its grants, `start_job` and repo requests failed `null value in column "host_id"`. New statements at the end of `MIGRATIONS` add what it reads back. `github_config` is copied back from the `github` row, with the same sealed values and the repo-creation orgs. Two triggers keep the setting and the row equal while both releases can run, so a connect, rotate, clear or remove on either side reaches the other. The four workbench tables default `host_id` to `'github'` again. The contract step (drop the triggers, delete the setting, drop the defaults) ships in the next release. One thing is still broken on the previous release, and `docs/UPDATES.md` now says so: editing a repo's git flow answers 500, because its upsert targets `ON CONFLICT (repo)` and a unique index on the repo alone would refuse the same owner/name on two hosts. `bun run check` gets a roll-safety guard (`scripts/check-invariants.mjs`). A statement at index 526 or later that drops a table or column, renames, retypes a column, drops a default, sets NOT NULL, drops a primary key or unique constraint, or deletes an `app_settings` row now needs `-- contract: <what goes>, unread since <vX.Y.Z or #PR>`, and `-- deliberate:` no longer passes those. The guard also checks itself against the five #611 statements it exists for, and the destructive guard's line numbers now point at the statement instead of about 19 lines above it. The relay (`llm_chat.rs`) now ignores a `fleet-gateway` entry in `gateway_unmetered_keys`. The previous release's render puts that entry back on every render, and the one-shot migration that removed it does not run again, so calls on the persona key were booked nowhere. Operators' own entries, the workbench key's included, still count.

  Verified: with main's published image (`ghcr.io/outcrop-labs/talaria:sha-805e679977e6`) on a throwaway Postgres restored from the release sweep's main-era dump (a seeded main install with a sealed GitHub PAT, a repo flow, an agent's grants and `fleet-gateway` on the unmetered list).
